Flexible regulation beats any fixed strategy (Bonanno 2004; Cheng 2001). Inflexibility marks depression and anxiety, and cardiac vagal control may integrate its forms. Causal direction is open. It recommends experience sampling and multi-informant measures over global self-report. | Read |
| [NOTE-437](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-437.md) | The Future of Intervention Science: Process-Based Therapy | A programme paper. Thirty years of DSM-linked trials never turned syndromes into diseases, so evidence-based therapy should target theory-derived, empirically supported processes of change with procedures shown to move them. Its distinctive commitments are a falsification rule for models of change, moderated mediation as a basis for a new nosology, and an idiographic, functional-analytic diagnosis. It offers predictions and cited examples, not new data. | Read |
| [NOTE-438](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-438.md) v2 | A meta-analytic review of experiments examining the effects of extrinsic rewards on intrinsic motivation | 128 experiments on interesting tasks, separate meta-analyses for free-choice behaviour and self-reported interest. Tangible rewards expected for engaging in, completing or doing well at a task undermine free-choice intrinsic motivation (d from −0.28 to −0.40), and less so self-reports; unexpected and task-noncontingent rewards do not; positive feedback enhances, except for children's free choice. The pattern fits cognitive evaluation theory and contradicts Eisenberger and Cameron's helplessness and learned-industriousness account. | Read |
| [NOTE-439](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-439.md) | The "What" and "Why" of Goal Pursuits: Human Needs and the Self-Determination of Behavior | Needs in SDT are innate psychological nutriments, identified functionally by the costs of their thwarting, not by individual differences in their strength. The three needs organize findings on intrinsic motivation and internalization, predict that both the "why" (autonomous vs controlled regulation) and the "what" (intrinsic vs extrinsic aspirations) of goals affect well-being, and explain need substitutes and rigid defences when needs are thwarted. Autonomy is self-organization, defended as an evolved, domain-general design feature. | Read |
| [NOTE-440](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-440.md) | Basic psychological need theory: Advancements, critical themes, and future directions | The authors set out nine criteria a basic psychological need must meet, separate need frustration from mere lack of satisfaction, review need frustration's costs (ill-being, compensatory behaviour, need substitutes) and propose it as transdiagnostic, review the interplay with sleep, food, sex and safety, map need-supportive and need-thwarting practices on a circumplex, and argue that the needs are universal in their effects ("output side") while the practices that satisfy them vary ("input side"). Novelty, morality and beneficence are weighed as fourth needs and not yet admitted. | Read |
| [NOTE-441](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-441.md) | Self-Regulation and the Problem of Human Autonomy: Does Psychology Need Choice, Self-Determination, and Will? | SDT's autonomy is "regulation by the self": acting with reflective endorsement, graded along the internalization continuum, compatible with external influence, dependence and a single option. Ryan and Deci align it with phenomenological and hierarchical (Frankfurt, Dworkin) accounts and use that definition to answer behaviourist, social-cognitive, reductionist, nonconscious-priming, choice-overload and cultural critiques. Autonomy lies not in being an uncaused cause but in the capacity to "reflectively endorse or reject prompted actions" (p. 1573). | Read |
| [NOTE-442](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-442.md) v2 | Self-determination theory and the facilitation of intrinsic motivation, social development, and well-being | SDT's canonical short statement. Social contexts that support competence, autonomy and relatedness sustain intrinsic motivation and let people internalize and integrate extrinsic regulations; controlling, rejecting or overchallenging contexts undermine intrinsic motivation and leave regulations external or introjected. Autonomy is graded: four kinds of extrinsic motivation lie on a continuum of relative autonomy (Ryan & Connell's quasi-simplex). Basic needs are defined by their consequences for well-being, and need-deprivation is offered as a principal source of distress and psychopathology. | Read |
| [NOTE-443](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-443.md) | Précis of Breakdown of Will | Hyperbolic discounting makes preference reverse with delay alone, so a person is a population of interests that forestall one another. Will is the recursive bundling of choices by treating each as a precedent, which gives an intertemporal repeated prisoner's dilemma and makes Kavka's toxin rational to drink. The same recursion predicts legalism, "lapse districts", motivated misperception and compulsive over-control, and premature satiation of appetite limits what will can do for emotional reward. | Read |
| [NOTE-444](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-444.md) | An Organizational Account of Biological Functions | Functions are contributions to a differentiated self-maintaining organization by traits that organization produces and maintains (C1–C3). Closure alone grounds teleology and normativity but is shared by flames and hurricanes; differentiation is what makes functions meaningful. The account unifies "why is T there?" and "what is T for?" in current organization, and distinguishes functional, useful, dysfunctional, primary and secondary contributions. Reproduction is left to future "second-order" self-maintaining systems. | Read |
| [NOTE-445](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-445.md) | The Diffusion Decision Model: Theory and Data for Two-Choice Decision Tasks | The full diffusion model (drift v with across-trial SD η, boundaries 0 and a, starting point z with range s_z, non-decision time Ter with range s_t) fitted by the χ² quantile method. In three dot-motion experiments with 14–17 participants difficulty maps to drift alone, speed–accuracy instructions to boundaries alone, and a 75:25 proportion mainly to starting point; RT distribution shape is invariant across conditions. Drift variability gives slow errors and starting-point variability fast ones. Reviews aging, aphasia and neural-firing applications. | Read |
| [NOTE-446](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-446.md) | The Expected Value of Control: An Integrative Theory of Anterior Cingulate Cortex Function | The paper proposes that dACC estimates the expected value of control: probability-weighted payoff of a control signal minus an intrinsic cost rising with its intensity. dACC uses that estimate to specify the identity and intensity of the control signal, which lPFC and subcortical structures (STN, LC) implement. The account unifies conflict monitoring, reward and prediction-error responses, effort costs and the override of defaults. It is a synthesis without a fitted model, and it leaves open how EVC is computed and what the cost function is. | Read |
| [NOTE-447](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-447.md) | The Emperor's New Markov Blankets | Pearl blankets (conditional-independence shields in a Bayesian network) and Friston blankets (agent–environment boundaries in the world) are different constructs conflated in the free-energy literature. The four-way partition needs a chosen internal node, sensorimotor labels and steady state; in Friston's soup it also needs electrochemical-only coupling and a fixed cluster size. Realist use needs metaphysical premises; instrumental use is innocent but settles nothing about boundaries. | Read |
| [NOTE-448](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-448.md) | Goal Striving, Need Satisfaction, and Longitudinal Well-Being: The Self-Concordance Model | Sheldon and Elliot's integrated model of goal striving. Self-concordance (identified + intrinsic − introjected − external reasons) predicts sustained effort, effort fully mediates attainment (Study 1 β = .02 ns vs .76; Study 3 β = .08 ns vs .72), attainment predicts change in well-being more strongly when goals are self-concordant (interaction β = .11, .23), and accumulated daily autonomy, competence and relatedness partly mediate attainment's effect on well-being (Study 3). Three correlational student samples; SEM fits reached after adding paths the modification indices suggested. | Read |
| [NOTE-449](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-449.md) | The Time Course of Perceptual Choice: The Leaky, Competing Accumulator Model | The LCA: dx_i = [ρ_i − k x_i − β Σ_{j≠i} x_j] dt/τ + ξ_i √(dt/τ), with x_i floored at 0. For two choices x₁ − x₂ is an OU process with K = k − β; d′(t) = d_asy (1 − e^{−Kt})/√(1 − e^{−2Kt}) and d_asy = (2v/σ)√(1/K). On new time–accuracy data the OU curve beats diffusion-with-drift-variance in 7 of 9 fits (combined likelihood ratio about 62). Leak versus inhibition predicts recency versus primacy; 2 of 6 participants favoured the end cluster and 2 opposed it. A fixed-accuracy criterion gives Hick's law in all three models simulated, so it does not discriminate them. | Read |
| [NOTE-450](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-450.md) | The Markov blanket trick: On the scope of the free energy principle and active inference | The FEP is true of things defined its way, but its scope is limited: a Markov blanket fits only some things, is placed where the model needs it, and cannot represent relational properties or a boundary the system makes. Its real job is to give any system the partition variational Bayes requires. Active-inference models smuggle perception and action into hand-built generative models. A conceptual critique; no new formal result and no data. | Read |
| [NOTE-451](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-451.md) | Hierarchically organized behavior and its neural foundations: A reinforcement learning perspective | The paper introduces hierarchical RL (options) to psychology and neuroscience as a response to RL's scaling problem. An actor-critic options model learns faster with useful options (doorways in the rooms task) and slower or worse with unhelpful ones (windows; a shortcut ignored). It proposes DLPFC for option identity, DLS for option-specific policies, and OFC for option-specific values and option-level prediction errors. It predicts phasic dopamine at subtask boundaries and a possible neural pseudo-reward. Option discovery is named as the central problem. | Read |
| [NOTE-452](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-452.md) | The Intimate Contest for Self-Command | Schelling's essay proposes "egonomics", the art of managing oneself. Its core claim is that many self-control tactics are the tactics for managing another person, applied to a "sometime self" who will be in command later. It gives a taxonomy of habits by time profile, onset time, warning time, cost, visibility, damage function and self-aggravation. It refuses a general answer to which self is authentic. It estimates the stakes at "on the order of a trillion dollars" for the current population. | Read |
| [NOTE-453](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-453.md) | Evolution of the Internal Family Systems Model | Schwartz's short statement of the IFS model. A person is "an ecology of relatively discrete minds", parts forced into managerial, exiled or firefighting roles by experience, which can return to valuable roles. At the core is a Self with leadership qualities (the eight Cs), reached when parts "step back", as in the founding case of "Diane". The Self is an active healer, not a witness. A practitioner's essay; its evidence is clinical experience. | Read |
| [NOTE-454](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-454.md) | Sophisticated Inference | Expected free energy evaluated recursively over the beliefs an agent would hold after each plausible outcome turns active inference into a pruned tree search over belief states, formally analogous to Bellman recursion. Small simulations show it planning through short-term costs (an aversive cue; a maze barrier needing horizon four) and exploring by novelty. Its scalability is argued from pruning, not demonstrated; its first-principles grounding is cited, not developed. | Read |
| [NOTE-455](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-455.md) | The Normative Constitution of Agency | Korsgaard asks whether agency is natural (a movement caused by the right mental state) or normatively constituted (a movement backed by an agent whose unity is achieved by following norms). Ordinary attribution of action implies activity and identity. Self-constitution explains both: the categorical and hypothetical imperatives give action the form of self-determined efficacy, and the maxims chosen under them constitute practical identity. Reflective self-consciousness breaks given unity and sets the task of rebuilding it, so unity of agency is "an achievement, not a given". | Read |
| [NOTE-456](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-456.md) | Participatory sense-making: An enactive approach to social cognition | An enactive account of social cognition built on coordination dynamics. When coordination and the encounter shape each other, the interaction gains its own precarious operational closure; it is social only if the interactors stay autonomous. Coordinated sense-making then ranges from one partner's sense-making being modulated to meanings made jointly. Conceptual throughout; evidence is illustrative (corridor, charades, mother–infant timing, perceptual crossing). | Read |
| [NOTE-458](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-458.md) | Defining Agency: Individuality, Normativity, Asymmetry, and Spatio-temporality in Action | Minimal agency needs a self-individuated system that is the source of modulations of its coupling with the environment and regulates them by norms it generates. An autonomous organization, a precarious network of mutually enabling processes, generates all three when it adaptively modulates its coupling for its own maintenance. Life is sufficient, not necessary. The definition is a proposal: the authors say asymmetry's formalization is incomplete and modeller-relative. | Read |
| [NOTE-459](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-459.md) | Uncertainty-based competition between prefrontal and dorsolateral striatal systems for behavioral control | Habit and goal-directed action are model-free (cached values) and model-based (tree search) reinforcement learners, arbitrated by which controller's Bayesian posterior over action value has the lower variance. Over-training shifts control to the cache because tree search accrues computational noise per step. Task complexity and proximity to reward keep the tree in control. It also predicts that incentive learning should become unnecessary when the caching system is lesioned. | Read |
| [NOTE-460](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-460.md) | Précis: Being No One | Metzinger's own sketch of the self-model theory. Six constraints (globality, presentationality, transparency, convolved holism, dynamicity, perspectivalness) build up consciousness; a transparent self-model yields phenomenal selfhood, so "no such things as selves exist in the world"; transparency is graded, inversely proportional to the attentional availability of earlier processing stages. Phenomenal unity is one global functional cluster. The first-person perspective is a model of the intentionality relation, whose iteration gives introspective and social intelligence. A theory statement: no new evidence. | Read |
| [NOTE-461](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-461.md) | The Physics of Optimal Decision Making: A Formal Analysis of Models of Performance in Two-Alternative Forced-Choice Tasks | Proves the pure DDM is the continuum limit of the SPRT and so the optimal two-choice decider. The linearised Usher–McClelland model decouples into a difference process, an O-U with λ = w − k, and a stable sum process, so it reduces to the DDM when k = w and both are large; feedforward inhibition does so at u = 1, pooled inhibition with fast inhibitory units, the race model never. The reward-rate-optimal threshold is unique and depends only on the total delay, giving a parameter-free optimal performance curve (peak decision time about 0.2 of the delay at ER about 18%). | Read |
| [NOTE-462](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-462.md) | An Accumulator Model for Spontaneous Neural Activity Prior to Self-Initiated Movement | A three-parameter leaky stochastic accumulator, δx = (I − kx)Δt + cξ√Δt, fitted to Libet-task waiting times (k = 0.5, I = 0.11, threshold at the 80th percentile of output), reproduces the readiness potential (r² = 0.96) and the linear mean–SD relation of waiting times (r = 0.9). In a variant with random clicks, fast responders showed a slow negativity before the click (P < 0.005), and fast and slow clicks were spread equally through the trial (P = 0.64). The neural decision to move is placed at the threshold crossing about 150 ms before movement. | Read |
| [NOTE-463](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-463.md) | Model-based and model-free Pavlovian reward learning: Revaluation, revision, and revelation | The paper argues that Pavlovian prediction has a model-based form. A cue that predicted disgusting salt was instantly "wanted" in a novel salt appetite, before retasting, with mesolimbic activation. That needs identity-specific prediction revalued by current state, which no model-free cache provides. It proposes "defocusing" of the predicted outcome as a model-based source of apparent habit. It argues dopamine can carry model-based evaluations. A kappa-transformation model fits the data but is described as phenomenological, and no algorithm is offered. | Read |
| [NOTE-464](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-464.md) | A Planning Agent's Self-Governance over Time | Bratman's model of a planning agent's self-governance over time. It needs (1) planned temporally extended activity with a time-frame to "plan's end", (2) synchronic self-governance along the way, (3) cross-temporal links of intention that are intrapersonal analogues of shared intention, so the agent acts "together" with herself, and (4) "diachronicalized" standpoints holding a conditional, reflexive end of diachronic self-governance. The model makes some willpower and resistance to shuffling self-governed and excludes the toxin case. Argued by cases, not tested. | Read |
| [NOTE-465](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-465.md) | The Sources of Normativity | Korsgaard's Tanner Lectures. The normative question (what justifies morality's claims on us) is not answered by voluntarism, substantive realism or reflective endorsement alone. Reflective consciousness forces us to act on reasons, and so to identify with a law: a "practical identity", the description under which we value ourselves. Obligation is the reflective rejection of a threat to that identity. Valuing any identity commits us to valuing humanity, reasons are public, and animals' pain can obligate us. Argued, but "sketchy" by its own account. | Read |
| [NOTE-466](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-466.md) | HDDM: Hierarchical Bayesian Estimation of the Drift-Diffusion Model in Python | HDDM fits the full DDM (v, a, z, t with sv, st, sz) by MCMC in PyMC, with group-level priors such as μ_a ~ Gamma(1.5, 0.75), μ_v ~ N(2, 3), z_j ~ invlogit(N(μ_z, σ_z²)), and the Navarro–Fuss likelihood. A patsy-style regressor lets a parameter vary with a trial covariate. In simulations with 12 subjects and 20–150 trials, hierarchical Bayes had the lowest trimmed recovery error for every parameter and the highest power to detect drift differences and covariate effects, by up to 20% for the latter with larger effects and few trials. | Read |
| [NOTE-467](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-467.md) | The Haken–Kelso–Bunz (HKB) model: from matter to movement to mind | Kelso's retrospective on HKB. The relative-phase equation dφ/dt = −a sin φ − 2b sin 2φ has stable in-phase and anti-phase states for b/a > 1/4 and only in-phase below; with noise the switch is a nonequilibrium phase transition with critical fluctuations and slowing. Symmetry breaking gives metastability (relative coordination); merged with Kuramoto it models groups. The same dynamics is reported within and between people and in brain activity. A first-person account, not a review. | Read |
| [NOTE-468](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-468.md) | Biological organisation as closure of constraints | A constraint acts on a process while being conserved at that process's time scale; closure is a set of constraints, each directly dependent on and generative for another, that cannot be split. This separates closure from cycles of processes, grounds functions, and gives a boundary criterion, refined by a preliminary count-based tendency to closure for symbionts and by nested separated closures for levels. Applied only to schematic examples; closure is not claimed to define organisms. | Read |
| [NOTE-469](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-469.md) | Thine Own Self: True Self-Concept Accessibility and Meaning in Life | Five studies with students. True-self accessibility, the residual speed of "me" judgments for one's own true-self traits, predicts MLQ presence of meaning (β = .29, .24, .19 in Studies 1, 2, 4) beyond actual-self accessibility, affect, need satisfaction, liking, overlap, state self-esteem and AI-3 authenticity. Subliminal true-self primes raised reported meaning against actual-self primes (Study 3, ANCOVA F = 4.46) and against disliked actual-self primes (Study 5, contrast F = 5.07), with disliked true-self traits as effective as liked ones. | Read |
| [NOTE-470](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-470.md) | “First we invented stories, then they changed us”: The Evolution of Narrative Identity | McAdams's review essay on narrative identity: "the internalized and evolving story a person invents to explain how he or she has become the person he or she is becoming". Storytelling is placed in human evolution as a tool for simulating social life and binding groups. The self is layered as actor, then agent, then author, with the life story arriving in adolescence on the back of autobiographical memory, theory of mind and autobiographical reasoning. Story features predict well-being and generativity. Culture supplies master narratives. Claims are cited, not shown. | Read |
| [NOTE-471](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-471.md) | Bayesian Interpolation | Evidence ≈ best-fit likelihood × Occam factor, the ratio of posterior to prior accessible parameter volume. At the evidence maximum the regulariser's χ² equals γ = Σ λ_a/(λ_a + α), the number of well-determined parameters, and the data χ² equals N − γ. Polynomials show an "Occam hill" in k, and the true Hermite model wins on data drawn from it. | Read |
| [NOTE-472](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-472.md) | Natural Gradient Works Efficiently in Learning | Natural gradient ∇̃L = G⁻¹∇L is steepest descent under metric G (Theorem 1); for a statistical model G is the Fisher information. Online learning w_{t+1} = w_t − (1/t)∇̃l is Fisher efficient, Ṽ_t = G⁻¹/t + O(1/t²) (Theorem 2). Explicit G and G⁻¹ for a perceptron (Theorems 3–4) and the natural gradient ∇L·WᵀW on the matrix group (Theorem 6). The plateau claim for multilayer perceptrons is a conjecture resting on Yang & Amari (1997). | Read |
| [NOTE-473](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-473.md) | A Widely Applicable Bayesian Information Criterion | The Bayes free energy of a singular model is nL_n(w0) + λ log n − (m − 1) log log n + O_p(1), with λ the RLCT. The posterior mean of nL_n(w) at inverse temperature 1/log n (WBIC) reproduces the first two terms without knowing λ, equals BIC for regular models, and two temperatures estimate λ. In reduced-rank regression WBIC chose the true rank 100/100 times, and estimated RLCTs within about 0.5 of theory. | Read |
| [NOTE-474](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-474.md) | Traces of Class/Cross-Class Structure Pervade Deep Learning Spectra | G = Gclass + Gcross + Gwithin + Gc=c′ (Eq. 6.4); knockouts give C outliers to Gclass, a C² mini-bulk to Gcross, the bulk to Gwithin, in log-spectra. Gˡ = Σ w (hhᵀ) ⊗ (δδᵀ) (Eq. 7.8), so gc ≈ hc ⊗ δc. K-FAC Hˡ ⊗ Δˡ misaligns G's outliers; CFAC Ave_c Hˡc ⊗ Δˡc aligns them at deep layers. For multinomial logistic regression on a Gaussian model the expected Fisher has C outliers, C(C−2) mini-bulk and a bulk (Theorem 8.1). | Read |
| [NOTE-475](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-475.md) | Deep Equals Shallow for ReLU Networks in Kernel Regimes | For κ(xᵀx′) on S^(d−1), µ_k = (ω_(d−2)/ω_(d−1)) ∫ κ(t)P_k(t)(1 − t²)^((d−3)/2) dt (Eq. 8), shared by N(d, k) ~ k^(d−2) harmonics. Theorem 1: an endpoint expansion κ(1 − t) = p(t) + c t^ν + o(t^ν) with ν non-integer gives µ_k ~ C k^(−d−2ν+1), parity-dependent. ReLU kernels have ν = 1/2 (NTK) and 3/2 (random features) at any depth, so the deep NTK decays as k^(−d) and the deep RF kernel as k^(−d−2) (Corollaries 2–3). MNIST and Fashion-MNIST accuracy is flat in depth from L = 2 to 5 (Table 1). | Read |
| [NOTE-476](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-476.md) v2 | Prevalence of Neural Collapse during the terminal phase of deep learning training | NC1 Σ_W → 0 (Tr(Σ_WΣ_B†)/C falls), NC2 centred means → simplex ETF (cosines → −1/(C−1)), NC3 W ∝ Ṁᵀ, NC4 nearest class mean; 7 datasets × 3 nets, 480 models. Median TPT gains: +0.35 points test accuracy, +0.0252 DeepFool robustness. NC1–2 ⇒ NC3–4 for Webb–Lowe and max-margin (Theorems 2, 4). Optimal small-noise error exponent C/(C−1)·1/4, only at simplex ETFs (Theorem 5). | Read |
| [NOTE-477](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-477.md) | Bayesian model reduction | The free energy of any model that differs from a fitted one only in its prior is ln E_Q[P̃/P] plus the fitted free energy, with closed forms for Gaussian, Dirichlet, beta, gamma, categorical and multinomial priors. Greedy pruning by this quantity recovers sparse structure in three simulations. Hierarchical models invert as a cascade of reductions. | Read |
| [NOTE-478](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-478.md) | The Full Spectrum of Deepnet Hessians at Scale | Hess = H + G (Gauss–Newton). At 28M parameters the Hessian has a bulk and about C outliers; outliers are in G, the bulk mostly in H; H is symmetric and power-law, φ ∝ \|λ\|⁻²·⁷ (R² 0.99), not Marchenko–Pastur or semicircle. G = A₁ + A₂ + B₁ + B₂ (Eq. 5): C class means give the outliers, cross-class spread and within-pair spread give two bulks. FastLanczos costs O(Mnp) time and O(p) memory. | Read |
| [NOTE-479](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-479.md) | Measurements of Three-Level Hierarchical Structure in the Outliers in the Spectrum of Deepnet Hessians | G = (1/n)ΔΔᵀ with δᵢ,c,c′ = column c′ of diag(√p)(I − 1pᵀ)∂f/∂θ. C² group means δc,c′, C cluster centres δc; G = G₀ + G₁ + G₂ + G₃ (Eq. 28). Top-C eigenvalues of G ≈ those of G₁ = (C−1)Ave_c δcδcᵀ, from a C×C Gram matrix, with λc(G) ≥ λc(G₁₊₂) ≥ λc(G₁). 18,000 CIFAR/MNIST models plus ImageNet VGG16/ResNet50. Group means switch from clustering by logit c′ to by class c during training. | Read |
| [NOTE-480](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-480.md) | Shampoo: Preconditioned Stochastic Tensor Optimization | Matrix case: L = εI + Σ GGᵀ, R = εI + Σ GᵀG, W ← W − ηL^{-1/4}GR^{-1/4}. Lemma 8: εI + (1/r)Σ ggᵀ ⪯ L^{1/2} ⊗ R^{1/2} for rank-r gradients, so the Kronecker preconditioner dominates full AdaGrad. Regret √(2r) D Tr(L^{1/4}) Tr(R^{1/4}) = O(√T) (Theorem 7); order-k tensors use power −1/2k per dimension (Theorem 10). Steps per second within a few percent of SGD/Adam/AdaGrad (Table 1); on LM1B 3.509 against 4.87–4.92. | Read |
| [NOTE-481](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-481.md) | The Convergence Rate of Neural Networks for Learned Functions of Different Frequencies | For uniform data the wide two-layer ReLU Gram matrix H∞ is a convolution on the sphere, so its eigenvectors are Fourier modes or spherical harmonics. On S¹, bias-free: λ_k = 1/π², 1/4, 2(k²+1)/(π²(k²−1)²) and 0 for k = 0, 1, even k ≥ 2 and odd k ≥ 3 (Eq. 12). With zero-initialised bias, odd k ≥ 3 get 1/(π²k²) (Eq. 13). Learning time grows as k² on S¹ and about k³ on S², as measured for shallow, deep and residual networks (Figs. 6–7). | Read |
| [NOTE-482](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-482.md) v2 | Gemma Scope: Open Sparse Autoencoders Everywhere All At Once on Gemma 2 | JumpReLU SAE: f(x) = z ⊙ H(z − θ), z = W_enc x + b_enc, x̂ = W_dec f + b_dec, loss ‖x − x̂‖² + λ‖f(x)‖₀, with θ trained by straight-through estimators (bandwidth ε = 0.001). Released on all layers and sublayers of Gemma 2 2B and 9B and three layers of 27B, at widths 2¹⁴–2²⁰. Evaluated by delta LM loss and FVU against L0. Residual SAEs cost the most loss; base-model SAEs transfer to the IT model; wider SAEs split latents. No agreed SAE quality metric exists. | Read |
| [NOTE-483](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-483.md) | Towards Understanding the Spectral Bias of Deep Learning | Theorem 4.2: n^(−1/2)‖V_(r_k)ᵀ(y − ŷ(T))‖ ≤ 2(1 − λ_(r_k))^T n^(−1/2)‖V_(r_k)ᵀy‖ + ε for any labels, given n ≥ Ω̃(ε^(−2) max{(λ_(r_k) − λ_(r_k+1))^(−2), M⁴r_k²}) and m ≥ Ω̃(poly(T, λ_(r_k)^(−1), ε^(−1))). Theorem 4.3: on uniform S^d the NTK's eigenfunctions are spherical harmonics, µ_k = 0 for odd k ≥ 3, and µ_k = Ω(max(k^(−d−1), d^(−k+1))) for even k. Experiments in R¹⁰ learn degrees 1, 2, 4 in that order, also on three non-uniform densities. | Read |
| [NOTE-484](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-484.md) | Bayesian hypothesis testing for psychologists: A tutorial on the Savage–Dickey method | For nested models the Bayes factor for a point null is the ratio of posterior to prior density of the tested parameter at the null value, under the larger model (Eq. 12, derived in Appendix A). It needs the nuisance parameters' prior to be continuous at the null. Worked examples give BF10 ≈ 2.2 where p ≈ .006, and BF01 ≈ 4 in favour of a null of no group difference. | Read |
| [NOTE-485](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-485.md) v2 | An Active Inference Approach to Modeling Structure Learning: Concept Learning as an Example Case | A partially observed MDP with spare hidden-state slots learns new animal concepts without feedback, refines coarse categories into fine ones, and generalises to an unseen animal in one shot. Bayesian model reduction on the learned state prior resets unneeded slots: right in 45–80% of runs for 4–7 true concepts, never for 2–3, and always when the likelihood is given. | Read |
| [NOTE-486](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-486.md) | Optimizing Neural Networks with Kronecker-factored Approximate Curvature | Fisher blocks E[āāᵀ ⊗ ggᵀ] ≈ E[āāᵀ] ⊗ E[ggᵀ], with error a sum of third- and fourth-order cumulants; the inverse is approximated as block-diagonal or block-tridiagonal over layers. Factored Tikhonov damping (π chosen by trace norms), re-scaling by the exact Fisher, and a two-parameter momentum solved on the quadratic model. On three deep autoencoders it beats tuned NAG-SGD by orders of magnitude in iterations; block-tridiagonal gains 25–40% per iteration over block-diagonal. | Read |
| [NOTE-487](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-487.md) | Post hoc Bayesian model selection | Models that differ only in their priors can be scored from one fitted full model: reduced evidence is full evidence times the posterior expectation of the prior ratio. Savage–Dickey is the point-mass case, ARD the continuous one. Under Laplace the reduced free energy is closed-form. Simulations recover a sparse regression (4,096 models) and a three-edge brain network (64 models). | Read |
| [NOTE-488](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-488.md) | Conscious birds | Review. Crow NCL neurons track the reported percept, not the stimulus, and NCL is nuclear rather than laminar; the pigeon connectome has the hub-and-module form GNWT requires; avian pallium has recurrent connectivity (RPT); IIT's markers (PCI, grid-like lattices) are untested in birds. Pigeons and roosters fail the mark test but discriminate their mirror image from a conspecific. GNWT and RPT requirements "seem to be mostly met"; the authors call the evidence short of a strong conclusion. | Read |
| [NOTE-489](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-489.md) | Three types of phenomenal consciousness and their functional roles: unfolding the ALARM theory of consciousness | ALARM: basic arousal (level-1 experience, subcortical) alarms the agent when homeostasis fails, triggering survival behaviour, care for the body and generalised learning without choice; general alertness (level-2, cortical, attention-guided) enables flexible learning and decision; reflexive self-consciousness is general alertness plus metacognitive self-relational content, enabling long-term planning. IIT, HOT and GNWT are said to cover only general alertness. Argued, not tested. | Read |
| [NOTE-490](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-490.md) | Block — The Mind as the Software of the Brain | An introductory chapter that says what the computer model of the mind claims and defends it. Intelligence is explained by functional decomposition into primitive processors; meaning-respecting processing by an isomorphism between syntactic and semantic functions that must hold counterfactually; intentionality by a language of thought whose symbols get meaning from functional role. The Turing test, Stich's syntactic theory and Searle's Chinese room are criticised. Block grants the model for intelligence and intentionality and doubts it for phenomenal consciousness. | Read |
| [NOTE-491](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-491.md) | Block & Fodor — What Psychological States are Not | Block and Fodor argue that behaviourism and type physicalism fail on empirical grounds, and that machine-state functionalism (FSIT) fails because psychological states cannot be one-to-one with the machine-table states of a probabilistic automaton. Dispositions, simultaneity, productivity and structure all break the correspondence, and machine-table identity is too fine-grained. Inverted and absent qualia are a prima facie objection to any functional definition. What survives is that psychological states may be computational states of an automaton, typed by the laws they fall under. | Read |
| [NOTE-492](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-492.md) | Block — Functional Role and Truth Conditions | A use (functional role) theory of meaning must say why 'aluminum conducts electricity' has different truth conditions on Earth and Twin Earth. Internal inferential roles cannot, and appeals to referential uses beg the question. A public-use theory can only do it with long-arm roles that import the devices of a theory of reference, and the result is equivalent to a two-factor theory whose internal part is narrow meaning. Burge's arthritis cases further require role in a language, structured by deference, alongside individual roles. | Read |
| [NOTE-493](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-493.md) | On a confusion about a function of consciousness | P-consciousness is experience and is not a functional notion. A state is A-conscious if its content is poised for reasoning and for rational control of action and speech. From blindsight or petit mal to a function of P is a fallacy, because A is missing too and A's machinery has that function. A without P (superblindsight) seems not to occur; P without A is suggested, not shown, by the noticed drill, Sperling arrays, hypnotic analgesia and anaesthesia. | Read |
| [NOTE-494](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-494.md) | Cross-region neuron co-firing mediated by ripple oscillations | In 35 patients (43 sessions, 1,373 units) doing a Sternberg task, ripple co-occurrence between bundles is about 5% at every distance from 71 to 223 mm, and unit pairs co-fire a median 34% more during co-ripples than in no-ripple periods (n = 31,489 pairs), 117% more by rate-corrected STTC. Load 3 raises co-ripple co-firing 13% (maintenance) and 19% (retrieval) over load 1. Encoding co-firing recurs at retrieval in 0.29% of cell-pair trials in co-ripples versus 0.14% outside them, 0.36% versus 0.23% for fast versus slow load 3 responses. | Read |
| [NOTE-495](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-495.md) | What Is Wrong with the No-Report Paradigm and How to Fix It | No-report paradigms separate consciousness from report but not from post-perceptual cognition that tracks the percept (the bored monkey problem), so prefrontal decoding in no-report rivalry does not show that prefrontal cortex is part of conscious perception. A no-differential-post-perceptual-cognition paradigm is needed. Brascamp et al.'s inconspicuous rivalry, whose switches subjects detected at chance, found no prefrontal difference by fMRI, which Block counts as some support for non-cognitive theories while warning fMRI may be too coarse. | Read |
| [NOTE-496](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-496.md) | Two neural correlates of consciousness | Proposes a phenomenal NCC (minimal basis of an experience's content, for seen motion recurrent MT/V5–V1 activity) and an access NCC (frontoparietal workspace broadcasting). Because access is winner-take-all, a recurrent sensory content can lose and go unaccessed. Signal-detection readings of the exclusion task and of Supèr et al.'s V1 figure–ground modulation, which persists when low salience or many catch trials uncouple it from detection, are offered as evidence. | Read |
| [NOTE-497](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-497.md) | Consciousness, accessibility, and the mesh between psychology and neuroscience | States the methodological puzzle: the neural basis of phenomenology can be found only by deciding whether it includes the machinery of access, which reports cannot decide. Answers it by inference to the best explanation: in Sperling, Landman et al. (capacity 6–7 of 8 when cued up to 1.5 s after offset, versus 4) and Sligte et al. (up to 32 items, 4 s) phenomenology overflows a working memory of about four. If workspace activation is not part of phenomenology, losing recurrent sensory coalitions explain the overflow. | Read |
| [NOTE-498](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-498.md) | Block — Précis of The Border between Seeing and Thinking | Block restates the thesis of his 2023 book, that perception is constitutively iconic, nonconceptual and nonpropositional and cognition paradigmatically discursive, and develops its least explained notion, the cognitive envelope: the global workspace conceptualises percepts, and the representations held in working memory are task-dependent abstractions that differ from perceptual ones in nine documented ways. Iconicity is defined by tracking and mirroring. Infant and animal iconic thinking is conceded but placed inside a cognitive envelope. | Read |
| [NOTE-499](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-499.md) | Distinct ventral stream and prefrontal cortex representational dynamics | In 430 visually responsive subdural electrodes from 10 patients, HFA (70–150 Hz) amplitude and category selectivity fell about 80% from peak by 800–900 ms while images stayed on. Ventral temporal decoding stayed near ceiling (face–watch AUC 99.8%), generalised across time, and ended about 230–450 ms after offset at every duration. Prefrontal and parietal decoding (peak AUC 84–86%) was confined to about 150–600 ms and ignored duration. Exemplar geometry was sustained only in ventral temporal cortex. | Read |
| [NOTE-500](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-500.md) | Perceptual consciousness overflows cognitive access | Against sparse readings of Sperling and the Amsterdam change-detection tasks, which posit conscious generic or fragmentary representations plus detailed unconscious iconic memory: there is no independent evidence for the latter, and the one direct test of unconscious working memory (Soto et al., just above 55% at 5 s) is too weak. Fragile VSTM holds 7, 6 and 5 of 8 items at 1, 2.5 and 4 s, is cortical, and is spared by inattention and right dlPFC TMS that impair working memory. | Read |
| [NOTE-501](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-501.md) | The Harder Problem of Consciousness | An argument for a conditional. If naturalism (physicalism is the default), phenomenal realism and anti-scepticism hold, then whether a superficial functional isomorph with a different physical basis is conscious is meta-inaccessible. Physicalism is then the default yet inaccessible, and it is the subjective default that the isomorph is not conscious while the question stays open. Disjunctive and superficial-role identities are metaphysically possible but could never be accepted by inference to the best explanation. | Read |
| [NOTE-502](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-502.md) | Interacting spiral wave patterns underlie complex brain dynamics | Phase fields of 0.01–0.1 Hz HCP fMRI on the flattened cortex hold about 16 spirals per hemisphere at rest (radius 10.5 ± 4.8 mm), centred on phase singularities that move at 2.2 mm/s with superdiffusive exponent β ≈ 1.5 and sit on functional boundaries. Opposite spirals annihilate (51% fully, 46% partly), like ones repel (2.6%). Spiral centres and charges decode four language conditions at 48.3% (chance 25%, raw-amplitude decoder 30.2%), and spiral pairs act as gates and walls that route task activity flow. | Read |
| [NOTE-503](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-503.md) | Block — Advertisement for a Semantics for Psychology | Block advertises two-factor conceptual role semantics as the only approach that could meet eight desiderata for a semantics serving cognitive science. Narrow meaning is an expression's short-armed conceptual role, its abstracted causal role in reasoning and deliberation; a separate factor relates it to referents. Conceptual role explains behaviour shared across Twin Earth, learning without definitions, relativity of meaning to representational system, and the inheritance of public meaning from the language of thought. Harman's long-arm roles reduce to the same two factors, and Gricean and indicator semantics either are not naturalistic or fail. | Read |
| [NOTE-504](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-504.md) | Block — Inverted Earth | Block gives the converse of the inverted spectrum: on Inverted Earth a subject or twin with identical brain, identical qualitative content and no internal disturbance comes, through his embedding in the environment and language, to have inverted intentional content and an inverted long-arm functional role. So qualitative content is not a functional state, and public colour talk expresses intentional content. The argument is stronger than the inverted spectrum on testimony and supervenience. A short-arm functional theory of qualia would escape it, and Block can only ask what that theory is. | Read |
| [NOTE-505](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-505.md) | Comparing the Major Theories of Consciousness | Compares higher-order thought, global workspace and biological theories by whether they can recognise the explanatory gap. HOT and the workspace replace it with puzzles of their own making; only the biological theory fully acknowledges it, and concept dualism (Nagel, Loar) keeps it from implying dualism. Ambitious HOT also suffers ad hoc stipulation, the mismatch problem and implausibility for infants. Goldberg et al.'s data suggest self-related activity is inhibited in intense perception. The biological theory is the least friendly to machine consciousness. | Read |
| [NOTE-506](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-506.md) | Block — Psychologism and Behaviorism | A machine that stores every sensible conversation of a given length and looks up its next reply has the capacity to respond sensibly to anything said to it, so it meets the strongest behaviourist conception of intelligence, but its intelligence is its programmers'. So psychologism is true: whether behaviour is intelligent depends partly on how it is produced. The standard objections to behaviourism only ever refuted necessary conditions; this refutes the sufficient one. Psychologism does not require our kind of processing, only processing that is not of the most elementary sort. | Read |
| [NOTE-508](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-508.md) | The Weighted Likelihood Ratio, Linear Hypotheses on Normal Location Parameters | States the Savage–Dickey ratio in general, not only for normal models: for a sharp hypothesis η(θ) = η_H with positive prior mass, the Bayes factor L_D(H) equals the alternative's posterior density of η at η_H over its prior density there (3.9), provided the null's nuisance prior is the alternative's conditional prior at η_H (3.8). Dickey calls it Savage's density ratio and credits the proof to Dickey & Lientz. He then applies it to normal means, the Model-I F test and the univariate and multivariate Behrens–Fisher problems with conjugate priors. | Read |
| [NOTE-509](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-509.md) | Ultraviolet Superradiance from Mega-Networks of Tryptophan in Biological Architectures | A radiative non-Hermitian Hamiltonian for N tryptophan 1La dipoles (single excitation) predicts superradiant states in microtubule architectures (max Γ/γ ≈ 4000 in a centriole, ≈ 7000 extrapolated for bundles) and a thermal quantum yield that grows with size and is insensitive to static disorder up to 200 cm⁻¹. Steady-state spectroscopy gives tryptophan QY 17.6 ± 2.1% in microtubules against 10.6 ± 0.6% in tubulin dimers. No lifetimes were measured, so the radiative rate is inferred, not observed. | Read |
| [NOTE-510](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-510.md) | Mashour, Roelfsema, Changeux & Dehaene — Conscious Processing and the Global Neuronal Workspace Hypothesis | A proponents' review. Conscious access is ignition: a sudden, self- sustaining, all-or-none activation of long-range hub neurons (prefrontal among them) that broadcasts one representation, against a decaying wave for unseen stimuli. Its best evidence is van Vugt et al.'s monkey recordings, where the signal-detection threshold is the prefrontal ignition threshold, plus a late (>200 ms) seen/unseen divergence across modalities and drug-invariant frontal-parietal disconnection under anaesthesia. It is a theory of access; it calls phenomenality without access untested, and admits the main theories cannot yet be told apart. | Read |
| [NOTE-511](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-511.md) | Block — Mental Paint | Block defends phenomenism, the view that phenomenal character outruns representational content, against both forms of representationism. Internalist representationism has only functional resources, and a child raised among ever-changing colours has colour experiences without abiding functional differences. Externalist representationism fails on swampman, on the difference between attention and awareness, on bodily sensations, on Inverted Earth with intact long-term memory, and on an empirical shifted-spectrum argument from normal variation in colour vision. What stays the same across representational change is mental paint. | Read |
| [NOTE-512](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-512.md) | Going Beyond Linear Mode Connectivity: The Layerwise Linear Feature Connectivity | LLFC: c·f⁽ℓ⁾(αθ_A + (1 − α)θ_B) = αf⁽ℓ⁾(θ_A) + (1 − α)f⁽ℓ⁾(θ_B) for every layer ℓ and α, some c > 0. Observed whenever LMC holds (spawning or permutation), across MLP, VGG-16, ResNet-20/50. Lemma 1: LLFC ⇒ error ≤ 2ε on the path. Theorem 1: weak additivity of ReLU + commutativity (W_A H_A + W_B H_B = W_A H_B + W_B H_A) ⇒ LLFC with c = 1. Weight and activation matching minimise the two factors of (W_A − PW_BPᵀ)(H_A − PH_B). | Read |
| [NOTE-513](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-513.md) | On Linear Mode Connectivity of Mixture-of-Experts Architectures | G(n) = ℝ^d × ℝ × S_n (common gate translation + expert permutation) preserves dense and top-k MoEs and, under genericity, is all of the gate's symmetry (Thms 4.1, 4.2, k ≥ 2). Translation leaves barriers unchanged. Weight matching = LAP on expert order (centred gates or Gram matrices) + per-expert weight matching, O(n³ + nh³). Barriers near zero (One Billion Word: 0.0044–0.0066 vs 0.14–0.86 without expert ordering), but only the inserted MoE layer is trained; the ViT/GPT-2 backbone is shared and frozen. | Read |
| [NOTE-514](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-514.md) | Linear Mode Connectivity and the Lottery Ticket Hypothesis | Instability = max error on the line between two copies trained from the same state under different SGD noise, minus the mean endpoint error; stable means under 2%. Networks are unstable at initialization (except LeNet) and stable after 1.5–20% of training. IMP subnetworks at extreme sparsity are matching when, and only when, they are stable; rewinding to an early iterate makes them so at ImageNet scale. | Read |
| [NOTE-515](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-515.md) | Knowledge is a Region in Weight Space for Fine-tuned Language Models | Task vectors of RoBERTa-base fine-tuned on 12 datasets × 20 seeds cluster by dataset with 98% accuracy, and by task family (NLI, sentiment, topic) with 90%. Hull samples of a group's fine-tuned models beat every outside model on the group's data and beat the group's own members in 88% (MNLI) to 96.7% (NLI family) of comparisons; extrapolation past the members fails fast. The centroid of models from other datasets, re-tuned with BitFit, is a better start than the pretrained model on 9 of 12 datasets. | Read |
| [NOTE-516](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-516.md) | Taxonomizing local versus global structure in neural network loss landscapes | mc(θ, θ′) = ½(L(θ) + L(θ′)) − L(γ(t*)) on a trained Bezier curve, in 0-1 training error (Eq. 4); mc < 0 is a barrier, mc ≈ 0 well connected, mc > 0 unconverged ends. With Hessian top eigenvalue and trace and output CKA on mixup points, a load by temperature grid splits into phases I–IV, with IV-B (flat, connected, similar) the most accurate. Sharpness alone mispredicts across phases; with 10% label noise, the sharp phases beat flat but poorly connected phase III, and double descent appears along the Hessian transition. | Read |
| [NOTE-517](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-517.md) | Mode Connectivity and Data Heterogeneity of Federated Learning | FedAvg, 10 clients, 200 rounds, Dirichlet label skew α ∈ {0.1, 0.2, 0.5} and PACS. Client/global low-loss overlap shrinks with heterogeneity; global models from one start under different α disagree on > 20% of inputs, are separated on the line (about 10% accuracy drop) and joined by a one-bend chain. Theory: ε_C = C e^{C T_max} max(√h(α), √h(α′))((√log N + z)/√N + √ε(√(D + log N) + z)), via mean-field dropout stability. MNIST two-layer net: dropout error < 0.01 at N = 6400, up to 0.06 at N = 200. | Read |
| [NOTE-518](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-518.md) | Exact expressions for double descent and implicit regularization via surrogate random design | Surrogate design S^n_μ = Det(μ, K), density ∝ pdet(XXᵀ), K Poisson(γn) truncated at d. E[#rows] = n (Lemma 1); E[I − X̄⁺X̄] = (γnΣ + I)⁻¹ (Lemma 2); E[tr((X̄ᵀX̄)⁺)] = γn(1 − det((I/γn + Σ)⁻¹Σ)) (Lemma 3); λn = 1/γn. These give exact MSE in all regimes (Theorem 1) and E[X̄⁺ȳ] = (Σ + λnI)⁻¹v for n < d, with n = tr(Σ(Σ + λnI)⁻¹) (Theorem 2). For sub-Gaussian rows the i.i.d.-design MSE converges to the surrogate formula (Theorem 3), at an observed O(1/d) rate. | Read |
| [NOTE-519](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-519.md) | A Random Matrix Analysis of Random Fourier Features: Beyond the Gaussian Kernel, a Precise Phase Transition, and the Corresponding Double Descent | Q̄ = ((N/n)(Kcos/(1+δcos) + Ksin/(1+δsin)) + λI)⁻¹ with δσ = (1/n) tr KσQ̄ is a deterministic equivalent for E_W[(ΣXᵀΣX/n + λI)⁻¹] (Theorem 1); Ē_train and Ē_test follow (Theorems 2–3). As λ → 0, δ ~ 1/λ for 2N < n and O(1) for 2N > n; det(Ω⁻¹) ~ λ, so Ē_test → ∞ at 2N = n unless the test set is within σ² ≲ λ of the training set. N/n → ∞ recovers Gaussian kernel regression. Theory matches MNIST, Fashion- and Kannada-MNIST. | Read |
| [NOTE-520](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-520.md) | Linear Mode Connectivity in Multitask and Continual Learning | From a shared start ŵ₁, the multitask solution w*₂ is linearly connected to ŵ₁ and ŵ₂, but ŵ₁ and ŵ₂ are not; the ŵ₁ → w*₂ direction is nearly orthogonal to task 1's top 50 Hessian eigenvectors, and ŵ₁ → ŵ₂ lies in their span. Different starts (CIFAR), input noise, label corruption and removed classes break the line. MC-SGD averages the loss along both lines with a one-example-per-class buffer: after 20 tasks 85.3 / 82.3 / 63.3% (Permuted MNIST / Rotated MNIST / Split CIFAR-100), multitask 89.5 / 89.8 / 68.8, Stable SGD 80.1 / 70.8 / 59.9. | Read |
| [NOTE-521](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-521.md) | Geodesic Mode Connectivity | Length of a path in distribution space = √8 ∫ √dJSD (Fisher–Rao). Minimise the discrete energy Σ JSD(pᵢ‖pᵢ₊₁) over 25 interior models between two weight-matched ResNet-20 (4×, LayerNorm) CIFAR-10 networks, initialised on the line; the result keeps train and test loss low where the line has a large barrier, using unlabelled training images. One pair, no numbers in the text, hypothesis stated for all geodesics. | Read |
| [NOTE-522](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-522.md) | Unveiling mode-connectivity of the ELBO landscape | Claims, without reported results, that LDA's ELBO maxima from two SVI runs (New York Times corpus) are joined by essentially flat maximum-energy paths found by the simplified string method with natural-gradient bead updates; that the paths flatten with data size and number of topics K; and that statistical degeneracy, not only over-parameterisation (K > K*), explains it. The only figure is a schematic. | Read |
| [NOTE-523](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-523.md) | ZipIt! Merging Models from Different Tasks without Training | Merging two differently initialised models trained on disjoint tasks: permute-then-average puts the result outside both task basins. Matching correlated features within and across models (Eq. 8) and merging only the early layers lifts CIFAR-10 (5+5) joint accuracy from 46.2 (Git Re-Basin) to 79.1 fully merged and 83.8 at 13/20 layers (ensemble 87.4). Fully merged ImageNet-1k (200+200) stays at 8.6; 10/50 layers reaches 60.9 (ensemble 63.3). Theorem 1 tightens Entezari et al.'s barrier bound by (1 − 2Γ)^{1/(2d+4)} for redundancy fraction Γ. | Read |
| [NOTE-524](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-524.md) | Optimizing Mode Connectivity for Class Incremental Learning | In class-incremental learning (PODNet, CIFAR-100), the line between adjacent continual minima loses old-task accuracy in an interval. OPC adds a layer-wise Fourier perturbation δ_θ(λ) with δ(0) = δ(1) = 0 to the line, minimises old-task memory loss before a switching point λ* and new-task loss after it, with cylinder noise for flatness; EOPC averages 10 points near λ*. PODNet + EOPC: CIFAR-100 66.68 / 64.94 / 62.36 (5 / 10 / 25 steps) vs 65.47 / 63.13 / 59.85; forgetting 7.68 / 8.64 / 12.02 vs 19.26 / 25.01 / 28.55. | Read |
| [NOTE-525](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-525.md) | Does Data Scaling Lead to Visual Compositional Generalization? | (n, k) framework: two concepts with n values, k seen combinations per value. From-scratch ResNet-50s: near-100% ID, large OOD drops; 4× ID data leaves 60–80% drops; more values or combinations help. Features go from spurious, to decodable but entangled, to linearly factored (R² > 0.8, cosine < 0.1–0.2). Proposition 4.1: with linearly factored embeddings spanning 2n − 1 dimensions, k = 2 suffices for a linear classifier to be correct on all (n − k)·n unseen pairs. DINO, DINOv2, CLIP: partly factored, above chance, not perfect. | Read |
| [NOTE-526](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-526.md) | TIES-Merging: Resolving Interference When Merging Models | Task vector τ = θ_ft − θ_init. TIES keeps the top 20% of each τ by magnitude, sets γ_m = sgn(Σ τ̂_t), averages only entries agreeing with γ_m, and returns θ_init + λ τ_m. Validated: (IA)³ 66.4 vs 63.9 for task arithmetic; T5-base 73.9 vs 73.2; T5-large 76.9 vs 73.3; ViT-B/32 73.6 vs 71.8 (RegMean); ViT-L/14 86.0 vs 84.5. Unvalidated T5-base 69.7 vs 73.2. Oracle multitask signs give 72.0 against 73.1 for multitask training. | Read |
| [NOTE-527](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-527.md) | Loss Surfaces, Mode Connectivity, and Fast Ensembling of DNNs | Curve-finding: minimize E_{t∼U(0,1)} L(φ_θ(t)) over the bend θ of a one-bend chain or quadratic Bezier curve between two trained networks. The found curves keep loss and error near the endpoints where the line segment reaches near-chance error (Table 2). Points at t ≥ 0.4 already ensemble as well as the far endpoint. FGE, short cyclical learning rates late in training, beats Snapshot Ensembles at equal budget (Table 1). | Read |
| [NOTE-528](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-528.md) | Understanding Mode Connectivity via Parameter Space Symmetry | Minimum of full-rank ‖Y − W_l…W₁X‖² ≅ GL_h(ℝ)^{l−1}: 2^{l−1} components, independent of width. 1-D three-layer: 4 components, 3 with a skip. h ≥ 2: permutations connect all components. Homogeneous last layers: rescaled minima in one component with unbounded midpoint loss, even under last-layer permutations (Props. 5.3–5.4). Symmetry curves γ(t) = exp(t log g)·w have constant loss; curvature ≤ κ bounds the chord's distance from the level set by (1/κ)(1 − √(1 − (κ‖Δw‖/2)²)) ≈ κ‖Δw‖²/8. | Read |
| [NOTE-529](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-529.md) | Unveiling Mode Connectivity in Graph Neural Networks | GCN node-classification solutions from different seeds show linear loss barriers that vary by graph (small on Cora, Citeseer; large on Coauthor-CS, Squirrel) and vanish along fitted quadratic Bezier curves. GCN, GraphSAGE and GAT give similar barriers, MLPs different ones. On CSBM graphs barriers fall with density and feature separability and peak at middling homophily. Stated without proof: a barrier bound through the spectral gap, a generalisation bound proportional to the barrier, and a Wasserstein distance between graphs' interpolation-loss curves that bounds the domain-adaptation gap. | Read |
| [NOTE-530](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-530.md) | Bridging Mode Connectivity in Loss Landscapes and Adversarial Robustness | Bezier path (Garipov) trained on 50–2,500 clean samples between two backdoored or error-injected models: models near the ends keep most clean accuracy and lose the attack (CIFAR-10 VGG, 2,500 samples, t = 0.1: 88% clean, 1.1% backdoor; injection 0% throughout). Standard-loss paths between regular and adversarially trained models are flat in standard loss but have a PGD robustness-loss barrier, correlated with λ_max of the input Hessian (PCC 0.71–0.88). Proposition 1's proof assumes the loss is constant along the path in a way that, if true for all inputs, would remove the barrier. | Read |
| [NOTE-531](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-531.md) | Essentially No Barriers in Neural Network Energy Landscape | AutoNEB finds paths between minima whose highest training loss is almost the minima's for ResNets and DenseNets on CIFAR-10, with a small gap on CIFAR-100; test error rises at most 0.5% (CIFAR-10) and 2.2% (CIFAR-100) per §4.3, or 0.7% and 2.9% on the ResNets per Appendix B. Concatenating paths bounds every pair through a minimum spanning tree. Barriers shrink with width and depth. | Read |
| [NOTE-532](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-532.md) | Git Re-Basin: Merging Models modulo Permutation Symmetries | Weight matching, coordinate descent over per-layer linear assignments for an NP-hard objective, aligns independently trained nets in seconds. After alignment, MNIST MLPs and wide CIFAR-10 ResNet-20s have zero loss barrier; 1×-width models and ImageNet ResNet-50 do not, and LMC appears only during training. A two-unit counterexample shows no permutation can connect some perfect solutions, so LMC is a property of SGD solutions. | Read |
| [NOTE-533](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-533.md) | Do Deep Neural Network Solutions Form a Star Domain? | Conjecture 2: for width > αh (h the width at which SGD solutions are convex modulo permutation), the solution set is a star domain modulo permutation. Starlight (sample θ_n ∈ Z, t ∼ U[0,1], step on L((1−t)θ + tπ(θ_n)), re-permute by weight matching each epoch) finds θ⋆ whose train-loss barriers to held-out models are about 2–5× lower than regular–regular ones across 8 settings, falling with \|Z\| up to 50. Not zero; star loss itself can be high (DenseNet CIFAR-100 0.635 vs 0.006). BMA on the star domain: better AUROC, worse ECE than an ensemble. | Read |
| [NOTE-534](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-534.md) | Mode Connectivity Beyond Classifiers: Evidence from Generative and Contrastive Models | One pair of DDPMs (Flowers102) and one pair of NanoCLIP models (Flickr30k) are joined by chains built by staged layer moves, per-layer variance correction and AdamW retraining to a loss threshold. DDPM training loss stays below 0.04 (AutoNEB peaks at 0.17), NanoCLIP below 0.09 (AutoNEB 6.69, accuracy 0.05). Ablations: all-layers, forward-order and SGD variants all raise the average loss. Intermediate DDPMs generate worse (higher FID) at endpoint-level training loss. | Read |
| [NOTE-535](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-535.md) | Exploring Neural Network Landscapes: Star-Shaped and Geodesic Connectivity | Two-layer ReLU student of an orthonormal M-neuron teacher: the minimum manifold is explicit (Theorem 6); two random minima are 2-PL connected w.p. ≥ 1 − M((M²−1)/M²)^{m−2M}; any two are 4-PL connected for m ≥ 2M − 1; k minima share a linearly connected centre w.p. ≥ 1 − M((M^k−1)/M^k)^{m−kM}. Normalised geodesic distance is O(√M) for uniform minima but ≤ 1 + c₂/(r√m) for r-sparse ones. Deep linear nets: 2-PL a.s., 3-PL always, star centre a.s. for m > 1 + r(L − 1). Centres found empirically for FNN, VGG16, ResNet on MNIST/CIFAR-10 without permutation. | Read |
| [NOTE-536](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-536.md) | The Generalization Ridge: Information Flow in Natural Language Generation | I(Zℓ; Y) = H(G_Z) + H(G_Y) − H(G_Z ∘ G_Y), with H(G) = −tr(G log G) on trace-normalized Gaussian Gram matrices (bandwidth 1) of ℓ2-normalized last-token states and target-token embeddings. It rises, peaks at layers 10/12 (GPT-2-S, synthetic: 0.2721) and falls (0.0188 at layer 12), where OOD early-exit accuracy peaks (56.90%) and ID accuracy keeps rising (93.17%). Middle residual updates add most; OOD-fitted residual scales downweight the last layers. The profile's shape persists over 50 decoding steps. | Read |
| [NOTE-537](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-537.md) | The Role of Permutation Invariance in Linear Mode Connectivity of Neural Networks | Conjecture 1: wide SGD solutions can be permuted into one linearly connected basin. Theorem 3.1 proves an output-level version only for a one-hidden-layer net at uniform random init, rate Õ(h^{−1/(2d+4)}). The evidence is that independent solutions S and permutations S′ of one solution show the same barriers across width, depth and data; simulated annealing lowers barriers only for shallow nets on easy data. | Read |
| [NOTE-538](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-538.md) | Mechanistic Mode Connectivity | Mechanistic similarity = invariance to the same unit interventions on the latents of the data-generating process. Cue-reliant and cue-invariant ResNet-18 and VGG-13 models are quadratic- but not linear-connected, even after activation matching. Conjecture 1 (no LMC up to symmetry ⇒ mechanistic dissimilarity) is not what Appendix F.3 proves. For a one-hidden-layer ReLU net with interpolating minimizers, Lemma 2 (LMC forces identical activation patterns) with Theorem 1 (mechanisms of different complexity force different patterns) proves the converse: dissimilar mechanisms of different complexity ⇒ no LMC under any permutation. The paper presents this as verifying the conjecture. CBFT (cross-entropy + barrier loss + class-mean invariance loss) removes the cue on synthetic CIFAR-10/100 and Dominoes. | Read |
| [NOTE-539](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-539.md) | Loss Surface Simplexes for Mode Connecting Volumes and Fast Ensembling | SPRO: train connecting vertices to minimize mean loss at 5 uniform samples in a simplicial complex minus λ log volume. It joins up to 7 modes in one complex and finds a low-loss region of at least 10 dimensions for VGG-16 on CIFAR-10 (volume collapses at the 11th vertex). ESPRO, simplexes grown from single modes at about 10 epochs per vertex, beats deep ensembles in error, calibration and corruption robustness. | Read |
| [NOTE-540](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-540.md) | Generalized Linear Mode Connectivity for Transformers | Symmetry hierarchy S1 permutation ⊂ S2 semi-permutation ⊂ S3 orthogonal ⊂ S4 invertible. Transformer alignment = P_FF per layer, semi-permutation P̃_H over heads (matched on QK and OV circuits), one orthogonal O on the residual stream after LayerNorm → RMSNorm. Test-loss barriers (Table 2): vanilla 1.69–4.34, weight matching 0.34–1.56, learned matching 0.00 (ViT ×3), 0.02 (Tiny Shakespeare), 0.42 (BookCorpus); permutation-only learned 0.29–1.60. Learned matching mainly refines O. Small models only. | Read |
| [NOTE-541](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-541.md) | Intermediate Layer Classifiers for OOD generalization | ILC_l(x) = W_l r_l(x) + b_l on frozen layer-l features, l ≤ L − 2, layer chosen on OOD validation data. Few-shot, best ILC minus last-layer retraining: +16.8, +6.3, +1.6, +6.3 points (ResNets on CMNIST, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100C, MultiCelebA); +27.0 on MultiCelebA at π ≤ 0.03. Zero-shot worst-group accuracy: Waterbirds 79.4 → 87.1, CelebA 56.0 → 82.0, MultiCelebA 20.8 → 46.0. Layer 7 beats 8 everywhere in Figure 8. Intermediate features are less displaced by shift for minority groups. | Read |
| [NOTE-542](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-542.md) | Rethinking generalization requires revisiting old ideas: statistical mechanics approaches and complex learning behavior | VSDL model: f = f(x; α, τ), α = m_eff/N lowered by label noise, τ raised by early stopping. Thermodynamic limit m, N → ∞ with α = m/N fixed. Continuous perceptron: s(ε) ~ ln ε, so 1/ε − α = 0 gives ε ~ 1/α (Eqs. 6–8). Ising perceptron: s(ε) ~ −(π²/2)ε² ln ε, and −π²ε ln ε = α has no solution for large α, so ε falls discontinuously to 0 at αc (Eqs. 9–13). Rigorous bound: error ≤ ε* + ε_τ, ε* the rightmost crossing of s(ε) and −α log(1 − ε) (Eqs. 14–18). No new theorem, no experiment. | Read |
| [NOTE-543](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-543.md) | Proving Linear Mode Connectivity of Neural Networks via Optimal Transport | Layerwise neuron alignment equals a Wasserstein distance between empirical weight distributions (Birkhoff), so LMC modulo permutation follows when neuron weights are i.i.d. and layers are wide: for mean-field two-layer SGD (Theorem 3.1), and for deep Gaussian or sub-Gaussian nets with m̃_ℓ = Õ((T_ℓ/ε)^{m̃_{ℓ−1}}) (Theorem 5.2), tight by Theorem 5.3. Low-dimensional weights relax this (Theorem 5.4). | Read |
| [NOTE-544](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-544.md) | Explaining Landscape Connectivity of Low-cost Solutions for Multilayer Nets | ε-dropout-stable ReLU nets are ε-connected by a piecewise-linear path (Theorem 1); ε-noise-stable nets by 10 segments with barrier Õ(ε) (Theorem 2), or 13 through a narrow low-loss net (Theorem 3). For any width there is a teacher dataset on which a two-layer student's global minima are disconnected (Theorem 4). MNIST convnets and a VGG-11 on CIFAR-10 satisfy the conditions roughly. | Read |
| [NOTE-545](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-545.md) | Freedom of the Will and the Concept of a Person | Persons differ from other creatures in the structure of the will: they have second-order volitions, desires that a given desire be the one that moves them to act, and wantons do not. Forming one is identifying with a desire. Freedom of the will is having the will one wants, and a decisive identification ends the series of higher orders "without cutting it off arbitrarily" (p. 16). Responsibility needs neither a free will nor alternatives: the willing addict acts of his own free will. The view is neutral on determinism, and on how the will came to be (n. 10). | Read |
| [NOTE-546](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-546.md) | Alternate Possibilities and Moral Responsibility | Frankfurt argues that PAP is false because circumstances can make an action unavoidable without bringing it about: Black stands ready to make Jones4 act and never needs to, so Jones4 is as responsible, for blame or praise, as he would be without Black (§IV). A fact that explains nothing about the action cannot excuse it (§V). The replacement principle excuses only an agent who acted "only because he could not have done otherwise", and Frankfurt says it is compatible with determinism. | Read |
| [NOTE-547](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-547.md) | Stories and the Meaning of Life | Fischer's own sketch of his framework (guidance control, not regulative control, is the freedom-relevant condition; guidance control is ownership plus moderate reasons-responsiveness; responsibility is historical and compatible with determinism; the Frankfurt cases' moral is the actual sequence), followed by the paper's thesis: acting freely is artistic self-expression that gives a life narrative value, a product judged mainly morally and prudentially, so the activity's aesthetic nature does not fix how the life is evaluated. | Read |
| [NOTE-548](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-548.md) | Moral Responsibility | A survey of moral responsibility. Its most exact reports, for this record: Fischer and Ravizza's guidance control as an owned, moderately reasons-responsive mechanism, with page references (§2.3); Wolf's critique of Real Self views and the requirement that an agent be able to form her values on the basis of the True and the Good (§3.1.1); and the moral competence condition, through JoJo (§3.2). Wolf's praise/blame asymmetry is noted in one sentence. | Read |
| [NOTE-549](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-549.md) | Rarely categorical, highly separable representations along the cortical hierarchy | Within single regions of mouse cortex during the IBL task, neurons' 8-variable selectivity profiles are more clustered than a covariance- matched Gaussian only in VISp, AUDp and SSp-ul, while pooled modules and the whole cortex cluster along anatomical lines. Over the conditions each region distinguishes (M_IC 5–16), ≥ 95% of random balanced dichotomies are decodable above a shuffle null in 15 of 16 regions (GU 0.82). Clustered neurons provably cap the condition geometry's participation ratio near min(k, M). | Read |
| [NOTE-550](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-550.md) | List & Pettit — Group Agency and Supervenience | Four conditions of agency (§2). A group's judgments supervene on members' contributions under a constitution (§3). With a universal domain, robust group rationality is inconsistent with majoritarian, uniform proposition-wise and proposition-wise supervenience (Propositions 1–3), and consistent with set-wise supervenience, as the premise-based and distributed premise-based procedures show (Propositions 4–5; Table 4). The group's judgment on a conclusion can be fixed by members' judgments on premises alone. Emergent agency without members' conception of the group is judged unintelligible (§6). | Read |
| [NOTE-551](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-551.md) | The Ripple Effect: Emotional Contagion and its Influence on Group Behavior | Study 1 (94 undergraduates, 29 groups, 2×2 confederate valence × energy): members' mood followed the confederate's valence (self-report change +.41 vs −.26, χ²(1) = 9.97; coders 2.75 vs 2.33, χ²(1) = 10.30). Pleasant contagion predicted self- and peer-rated cooperativeness, coder-rated group cooperativeness (r = .44) and lower conflict (r = −.42 to −.48). Valence asymmetry failed (χ² < 1) and energy effects were marginal and opposite in sign. Study 2 (113 MBA students, 26 groups, no confederate): mood ICC rose from .00 to .24; contagion correlated with cooperation (.49) and conflict (−.49). | Read |
| [NOTE-552](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-552.md) | Towards a Theory of Collective Emotions | Collective emotion as synchronous convergence in affective responding towards one event or object. The minimal case needs only shared appraisal structures. Mutual awareness (contagion, mediated sharing) and group membership (identity, collective intentions, norms, collective memory, group-based sentiments) amplify it and change its quality, including a transition from "I-mode" to "We-mode" collective emotion. A conceptual synthesis with no data; the authors say the key linkages lack evidence. | Read |
| [NOTE-553](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-553.md) | Huebner — Genuinely collective emotions | Collective emotion is defended by extending a homuncular, computational account of individual emotion to distributed systems. Fear needs four integrated capacities (p. 10). The USS Palau crew implements most of them but shows no fear, so it is reclassified as collective danger detection; a 2008 campaign is offered as a likelier case, without data. Unfelt collective emotion is defended by arguing that some individual fear is non-conscious (§5), and functional kinds are defended against homology (§6). Gilbert's plural-subject account is rejected as reducible to individual commitments. | Read |
| [NOTE-554](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-554.md) | List — Three kinds of collective attitudes | Aggregate attitudes: a rule or market summarises members' attitudes; proposition-wise supervenience; no direct role; rationality contingent (majority beliefs on p, q, p∧q can be inconsistent, Table 1). Common attitudes: all hold, with common awareness; enriched proposition-wise supervenience; coordination; consistent by unanimity. Corporate attitudes: a group agent's; holistic supervenience, like non-reductive physicalism; action-guiding; rationality presupposed. Three lessons of near-independence; Table 2 summarises. | Read |
| [NOTE-555](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-555.md) | Conceptualization of the Holobiont Paradigm as It Pertains to Corals | A mini-review arguing that corals must be studied as holobionts. The holobiont is defined by location (coral plus microbiota in body, mucus and skeleton), and its membership can change. Traits belong to host–symbiont combinations: a novel anemone–alga pairing out-performed both natural ones in oxygen flux at 32–34 °C, and two octocorals lost symbionts by different routes, one per host cell and one with host cells. It asks, without answering, whether the holobiont is the unit of selection. | Read |
| [NOTE-556](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-556.md) | Defining Coral Bleaching as a Microbial Dysbiosis within the Coral Holobiont | A review that redefines bleaching as three holobiont dysbiosis stages: microbial buffering, Symbiodiniaceae reorganisation by shuffling or switching, and traumatic dysbiosis ending in death (Figure 3). The supporting material is cited and correlational. Vibrio rose from about 0 to 30% relative abundance in bleached corals and returned in resilient ones, but the authors say cause and consequence cannot be separated. "Dysbiosis" names both the disruption and the healthy adaptive response, and the stages have no operational boundaries. | Read |
| [NOTE-557](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-557.md) | Signaling cascades and the importance of moonlight in coral broadcast mass spawning | Two experiments at Heron Island on Acropora millepora. In 2011, colonies under ambient night light (N = 6) spawned with the reef, while colonies lit after sunset (N = 5) or kept dark (N = 5) did not spawn that night. 184 transcripts selected by variance changed around gamete release only in ambient colonies. In 2006, 90 colonies under blue, green or white nocturnal light spawned 6–8 h or two nights late, and under red light on time. The GPCR and melanopsin cascade is a model built from correlated expression. | Read |
| [NOTE-558](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-558.md) | Phase Shifts, Herbivory, and the Resilience of Coral Reefs to Climate Change | Four roofless 25 m² cages on Orpheus Island's reef crest kept large and medium fishes out for 30 months after the 1998 bleaching, against four partial cages and four open plots. Macroalgae averaged 56% cover in cages and 4.1% and 1.7% outside. Coral cover reached 7.7% inside against 19.2% and 20.2%. Recruitment fell to about a third (39 against 108 and 118 per 25 m²) and mortality of established colonies was 24.2% against 9.8% and 11.3%. Reopened, the cages lost their algae in 30 days. | Read |
| [NOTE-559](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-559.md) | In Epistemic Networks, Is Less Really More? | Over a wider parameter space than Zollman used, the advantage of sparse networks vanishes when the better option is even slightly better, when groups are larger, or when agents gather more data per round. It survives only where inquiry is hard, and Kummerfeld and Zollman's effects behave the same way. Transient diversity is the robust lesson. | Read |
| [NOTE-560](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-560.md) | Nonreductive Physicalism and the Limits of the Exclusion Principle | With causes as proportional difference-makers, Kim's exclusion principle fails. A revised principle (a property and its realizer never both cause an effect) is true of some systems and false of others. A higher-level property excludes its realizer as cause exactly when the effect is realization-insensitive, surviving nearby changes of realizer. That is plausibly the norm in the special sciences, which makes higher-level causes autonomous. | Read |
| [NOTE-561](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-561.md) | Double-Loop Learning, Teaching, and Research | Defines single- and double-loop learning and restates the theory of action. People espouse many theories but act on one, Model I, which keeps reasoning tacit and makes errors in governing values undiscussable. That produces self-sealing individual and organizational defensive routines. A CEO workshop transcript shows the pattern, and a quasi-experimental design to test it is proposed but not run. | Read |
| [NOTE-562](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-562.md) | Cancer across the tree of life: cooperation and cheating in multicellularity | A review framing cancer as cheating on five foundations of multicellular cooperation and surveying cancer-like phenomena across the independent origins of complex multicellularity. Division-of-labour cheating appears in every form, resource and environment cheating only in animals and plants so far. Complex multicellularity is read as a cheater detection and suppression system, with proliferative units as a possible intermediate level of selection. | Read |
| [NOTE-563](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-563.md) | Beyond Markets and States: Polycentric Governance of Complex Economic Systems | Ostrom's retrospective. Polycentric arrangements, many formally independent decision centres, can outperform single hierarchies. Long-surviving common-pool resource institutions share eight design principles, not specific rules. In experiments communication and self-chosen sanctions sustain cooperation, and in the field local monitoring predicts outcomes. No single regime type is a panacea. | Read |
| [NOTE-564](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-564.md) | The Epistemic Benefit of Transient Diversity | A bandit model with beta priors. Sparse networks beat dense ones, as in 2007, but extreme priors reverse the order, and sparse networks of dogmatic agents often never converge. Limited information and dogmatism each sustain diversity, and together sustain it too long. What communities need is diversity that is transient. | Read |
| [NOTE-565](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-565.md) | Responsibility, Moral and Otherwise | A lecture arguing that deep responsibility extends beyond the moral, to prudential and aesthetic traits and to art, and that the self-disclosure view explains this. Watson's two-level view, attributability with accountability stacked on top, is rejected: the two are independent, and accountability may need nothing metaphysically robust. What makes a self a fit target of reactive attitudes is offered as a hunch: an intelligent self that perceives, understands and appreciates the world as we do. | Read |
| [NOTE-566](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-566.md) | "Exit, Voice, and Loyalty": Further Reflections and a Survey of Recent Contributions | Hirschman revisits Exit, Voice, and Loyalty.
