| [NOTE-918](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-918.md) | Andoni, Laarhoven, Razenshteyn & Waingarten — Optimal hashing-based time–space trade-offs for approximate near neighbors | For c-approximate near-neighbour search (find a point within cr when one lies within r) over n points in Euclidean space, the paper gives a data structure for every pair of exponents with c²√ρq + (c²−1)√ρu ≥ √(2c²−1), using space n^{1+ρu+o(1)} + O(dn) and query time n^{ρq+o(1)} + dn^{o(1)}, on worst-case data (for Hamming and ℓ_1, c√ρq + (c−1)√ρu ≥ √(2c−1)). It proves the curve cannot be beaten by list-of-points structures, the model of all known data-independent hashing schemes, on random instances, and unconditionally in the cell-probe model only at one end (query n^{o(1)}) for one or two probes. So the exact trade between space spent organizing and per-query time is known within the hashing model; outside that model, for more than two probes, it is not, and data-dependent schemes are covered only by conjecture. | Read |
| [NOTE-919](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-919.md) | Weber, Schek & Blott — Similarity search in high-dimensional spaces: when partitioning loses to a scan | Under uniformly distributed, independent data and queries in the unit cube with Euclidean distance, the paper estimates the average fraction of blocks that an optimal nearest-neighbour search must read in a partitioned or clustered index. That fraction reaches the 20% at which a sequential scan wins, given an assumed five-fold sequential advantage, at about 15–20 dimensions for rectangular regions, 26 for spherical ones, and below a crude 610 for any partitioning into convex clusters of two or more points. The "around 10" in the abstract is the measured crossover for an R*-tree and an X-tree on 50,000 uniform points and on 45-dimensional image features. As an alternative it proposes the VA-file, a scanned file of compact per-vector approximations that filters out all but a few vectors. The analysis says nothing about data with low intrinsic dimension; that the results carry over by fractal dimension is a conjecture. | Read |
| [NOTE-920](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-920.md) | Buneman, Khanna & Tan — Why and where: a characterization of data provenance | The paper separates two meanings of the provenance of a piece of output data. Why-provenance is the witness basis: for each valuation of the query that produces the value, the part of the source the query's patterns matched, one witness per derivation. Where-provenance is the location in the source a value was copied from. For a hierarchical data model and a query language that covers positive (SPJU) relational queries, the witness basis is preserved by the paper's query rewriting, and the minimal witness basis is the same for equivalent queries with equality conditions, while where-provenance is not invariant over equivalent queries in general and is preserved by rewriting only for a restricted class it calls traceable. Proofs are omitted, and nothing covers negation, aggregation, updates or additions to the source. | Read |
| [NOTE-921](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-921.md) | Halevy — Answering queries using views: a survey | A survey that separates two problems of answering queries from stored views: finding an equivalent rewriting, which query optimization needs, and finding a maximally-contained rewriting or all certain answers, which data integration needs when sources are incomplete. Its theoretical findings, mostly reported from other papers: an equivalent conjunctive rewriting exists only if one exists no longer than the query, so finding one is NP-complete in the size of the query and view definitions, and checking a candidate is itself NP-complete; the inverse-rules algorithm builds the maximally-contained rewriting, as a possibly recursive datalog program, in time polynomial in the query and views; and finding all certain answers is polynomial in the size of the stored data in many open-world cases, but co-NP-hard in that size under the closed-world assumption even for conjunctive views and queries, or open-world with union in the views or ≠ in the query. Choosing which views to store is left as the next problem; cost-based choice among rewritings is described for practical optimizers, without guarantees. | Read |
| [NOTE-922](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-922.md) | Olston & Widom — Offering a precision-performance tradeoff for aggregation queries over replicated data | Olston and Widom propose TRAPP: caches hold, for each numeric value, an interval its source guarantees to contain the current value, the source pushing a refresh whenever the value leaves it. A query carries a precision constraint R, and the system chooses which values to fetch exactly so that the answer interval is at most R wide whatever the true values, at least total refresh cost. For SUM (and AVG without a predicate) that choice is a 0/1 knapsack problem, NP-complete in general and polynomial with equal costs; COUNT and MIN have simple rules. Staleness becomes bounded imprecision, never error, and the cost of the source-side upkeep that guarantees this, and of setting the bound widths, is outside the optimization. The one experiment is 90 stock prices with random costs. | Read |
| [NOTE-923](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-923.md) | Kleinberg — The small-world phenomenon: an algorithmic perspective | On an n × n lattice where each node also gets q long-range links drawn with probability proportional to d^(−r), short paths exist for r = 0, but no algorithm that sees only the links of nodes the message has visited finds them faster than about n^(2/3) steps in expectation. At r = 2 the greedy rule (pass to the contact nearest the target in lattice distance) delivers in O((log n)²) expected steps (proved for p = q = 1); for 0 ≤ r < 2 every such algorithm needs Ω(n^((2−r)/3)) and for r > 2 Ω(n^((r−2)/(r−1))). So efficient decentralized search depends on how the long-range links are distributed relative to the lattice, not on the links' existence or on the graph's diameter. The k-dimensional version (r = k) is stated without proof, and the model is a lattice with a known distance that every node can compute to the target. | Read |
| [NOTE-924](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-924.md) | Fagin, Lotem & Naor — Optimal aggregation algorithms for middleware | Given m lists of the same N objects, each sorted by one attribute's grade, and a monotone function combining the grades, the threshold algorithm (TA) reads the lists in parallel, random-accesses each newly seen object's other grades, and stops once k seen objects score at least the combined score of the last grades read. It is correct for every monotone combining function, needs constant buffers, and is instance optimal among correct algorithms that make no "wild guesses": on every database its cost is within a constant factor of any such algorithm's, the factor being m + m(m−1)c_R/c_S, which is best possible when the combining function is strict (conjunction-like). Without the no-wild-guesses restriction no algorithm is instance optimal, and the counterexample is a two-list conjunction whose target sits in the middle of both lists, which any algorithm must search linearly. Fagin's Algorithm's sublinear cost O(N^((m−1)/m) k^(1/m)) is cited from Fagin, not proved here, and holds only when the lists' orderings are probabilistically independent. The model prices queries over a given set of single-attribute sorted lists. It does not price building or keeping the lists, choosing an arrangement, or any computation beyond accesses. | Read |
| [NOTE-925](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-925.md) | Larsen & Nelson — optimality of the Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma | For n, d ≥ 2 and lg^0.5001 n / √min{n, d} < ε < 1 there is an n-point set in R^d such that every map into R^m, linear or not, that keeps all squared distances within 1 ± ε needs m = Ω(ε⁻² lg(ε²n)), which is Ω(ε⁻² lg n) once ε > 1/min{n, d}^0.4999. So the Johnson–Lindenstrauss bound is optimal up to a constant, and the distributional lemma plus a union bound is the best route. The proof is an encoding argument over k-sparse point sets with k = ε⁻²/256, and the count it ends on is m = Ω(k lg(d/k)). | Read |
| [NOTE-926](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-926.md) | Achlioptas — database-friendly random projections | A random projection keeps all pairwise distances of n points within 1 ± ε with probability at least 1 − n^−β when k ≥ (4 + 2β)/(ε²/2 − ε³/3) · log n and the matrix entries are independent ±1, or √3 times {+1, 0, −1} with probabilities 1/6, 2/3, 1/6. This is the same k₀ as the best bound for Gaussian projections. The proof shows that every even moment of a unit vector's projection is at most that of the all-equal vector (1, …, 1)/√d, and that this vector's moments are at most the Gaussian ones. | Read |
| [NOTE-927](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-927.md) | Lee & Naor — extending Lipschitz functions via random metric partitions | A random partition of a metric space whose pieces are small and whose points are, on average, far from piece boundaries yields a "gentle" partition of unity, and averaging a Lipschitz map over it extends the map into any Banach space. This gives ae(X) ≤ C log n/log log n for every n-point metric space X (Theorem 1.10), improving Johnson, Lindenstrauss and Schechtman's C log n; ae(X) ≤ C log λ(X) for doubling X; ae ≤ C r² on K_r-minor-free graph metrics; e(ℓ₂ᵈ, Z) ≤ C√d; and, with the Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma, eₙ(L₂, Z) ≤ C√(log n). For maps into Hilbert space it does not improve Johnson and Lindenstrauss's K√(log n), and it leaves √(log n) open. | Read |
| [NOTE-928](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-928.md) | Linial, London & Rabinovich — the geometry of graphs | Every n-point metric embeds in ℓ₂ with distortion O(log n) in O(log n) dimensions (Theorem 3.2(1), attributed to Bourgain). The paper reproves the distortion bound by a randomized Bourgain-style construction into ℓ_p^{O(log² n)}, and it gets the dimension from Johnson–Lindenstrauss. Every embedding of a constant-degree expander into ℓ_p, 1 ≤ p ≤ 2, of any dimension, has distortion Ω(log n) (Proposition 4.2), so the bound is tight. The lower bound comes from Leighton and Rao's flow–cut gap, and the same embeddings give an O(log k) max-flow/min-cut gap for k commodities. | Read |
| [NOTE-929](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-929.md) | Alon & Klartag — optimal compression of approximate inner products | Storing every inner product and squared distance of n points of norm at most 1 in R^k to additive error ε takes Θ(n log n/ε²) bits once k ≥ log n/ε², Θ(nk log(2 + log n/(ε²k))) for log n ≤ k ≤ log n/ε², and Θ(nk log(1/ε)) below, for 1/n^0.49 ≤ ε ≤ 0.1. Comparing these counts across dimensions shows that some n points in R^k cannot be mapped into fewer than Ω(min{k, log(2 + ε²n)/ε²}) dimensions with additive error ε, for every ε ≥ 2/√n. A bipartite version of the Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma reaches O(log(2 + ε²n)/ε²) dimensions; the one-family version at that size is left open. | Read |
| [NOTE-930](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-930.md) v2 | Johnson & Lindenstrauss — extensions of Lipschitz mappings into a Hilbert space | Lemma 1: any n points in ℓ₂ⁿ map into ℓ₂ᵏ, k = [K(τ) log n], with ‖f‖_lip‖f⁻¹‖_lip ≤ (1+τ)/(1−τ), by a Haar-random rank-k orthogonal projection, with positive probability. The proof concentrates the norm of a projected unit vector about its median by Lévy's isoperimetric inequality and takes a union bound over the normalized differences of the points; K ≥ (10/τ)² suffices. The lemma is a tool for Theorem 1: Lipschitz maps from n-point subsets of any metric space into ℓ₂ extend to the whole space with Lipschitz constant at most C(log n)^{1/2} times the original. | Read |
| [NOTE-931](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-931.md) | Baraniuk, Davenport, DeVore & Wakin — a simple proof of the restricted isometry property | If an n × N random matrix satisfies the concentration inequality used in JL proofs, Pr(\|‖Φx‖² − ‖x‖²\| ≥ ε‖x‖²) ≤ 2e^{−n c₀(ε)}, then a union bound over a (12/δ)^k-point net on each of the C(N, k) ≤ (eN/k)^k coordinate k-subspaces, with a short bootstrapping step from net to subspace, gives the restricted isometry property for all k ≤ c₁n/log(N/k) with probability at least 1 − 2e^{−c₂n} (Theorem 5.2). Gaussian, ±1 and Achlioptas's sparse ensembles qualify with c₀(ε) = ε²/4 − ε³/6, and the same argument gives the property in any fixed orthonormal basis. | Read |
| [NOTE-932](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-932.md) | Dasgupta & Gupta — an elementary proof of the Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma | For n points in ℝᵈ and 0 < ε < 1, a projection onto a random k-dimensional subspace, scaled by √(d/k), keeps every squared pairwise distance within a factor 1 ± ε with probability at least 1/n once k ≥ 4(ε²/2 − ε³/3)⁻¹ ln n. The proof bounds each tail of the squared length of a random unit vector's first k coordinates by Markov's inequality on an exponential of Gaussian squares, and then takes a union bound over the n(n−1)/2 pairs. | Read |
| [NOTE-933](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-933.md) | Donoho & Tanner — observed universality of phase transitions | For Gaussian matrices, ℓ1 minimization (and its nonnegative LP form) recovers a k-sparse vector from n random measurements in dimension N with probability tending to 1 below a curve ρ(δ; Q) in the plane δ = n/N, ρ = k/n, and to 0 above it; this was proved earlier and is restated here as Theorem 2.1. In 2,948,000 linear programs over eight non-Gaussian ensembles at N = 200, 400 and 1600, the 50% success points fall on the same curves, but exact finite-N agreement is rejected: the differences from the Gaussian decay as N^(-1/2), so the paper supports only an asymptotic ("weak") universality, as an observation, not a theorem. | Read |
| [NOTE-934](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-934.md) | Barnett, Barrett and Seth — Granger causality and transfer entropy are equivalent for Gaussian variables | For jointly Gaussian stationary processes X, Y and Z, Geweke's Granger causality F_{Y→X\|Z} = ln(\|Σ(X\|X⁻⊕Z⁻)\|/\|Σ(X\|X⁻⊕Y⁻⊕Z⁻)\|) equals twice the transfer entropy T_{Y→X\|Z}, for multivariate predictor, predictee and conditioning variables (Eq. 13). The proof: OLS residual covariance is the partial covariance Σ(X\|Y), and a Gaussian's conditional entropy is ½ln\|Σ(X\|Y)\| + ½n ln(2πe). The authors keep G-causality apart from physically instantiated causation. | Read |
| [NOTE-935](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-935.md) | Seth — Measuring autonomy and emergence via Granger causality | G-autonomy ga_{X\|E} is the log ratio of a variable's prediction-error variance without and with its own past, given external variables E. G-emergence ge_{M\|m} = ga_{M\|m}·(1/N)Σ gc_{mᵢ→M} makes a macro variable emergent to the extent that it is both autonomous from and Granger-caused by its micro variables. Validated in a predator–prey model and a boids model, where flocking shows high G-emergence and Granger causation from the flock's centre of mass to each boid. Seth says the measures are relative to the predictor and the variables included. | Read |
| [NOTE-936](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-936.md) | Williams and Beer — Nonnegative decomposition of multivariate information | Redundancy is I_min(S; A₁…A_k) = Σ_s p(s) min_i I(S = s; A_i), the expected minimum specific information. Restricted to antichains of sources and ordered by α ≼ β iff every source of β contains one of α, the collections form a lattice. The Möbius inverse of I_min on it gives partial-information atoms that are nonnegative (Theorem 5) and sum to I(S; R). Interaction information is synergy minus redundancy for three variables and a signed mixture for four, which explains its negativity and its +1 bit for both 3-parity and three copies. | Read |
| [NOTE-937](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-937.md) | Bertschinger, Rauh, Olbrich, Jost and Ay — Quantifying unique information | For a target X and sources Y, Z, the unique information of Y is UĨ(X : Y \ Z) = min over Q ∈ Δ_P of MI_Q(X : Y \| Z), where Δ_P is the set of joints with the same (X,Y) and (X,Z) marginals. If unique information should depend only on those marginals, this is an upper bound on any such measure, and the shared and synergistic information it implies are lower bounds. It is zero exactly when the other source is Blackwell-sufficient. The measures are non-negative, satisfy the bivariate PI axioms and the identity property, and are a convex programme, but are bivariate only. | Read |
| [NOTE-938](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-938.md) | Kraskov, Stögbauer and Grassberger — Estimating mutual information | Two k-nearest-neighbour estimators of mutual information, I⁽¹⁾ and I⁽²⁾ (Eqs. 8–9), from the Kozachenko–Leonenko entropy estimate (Eq. 20) taken at one length scale in the joint and marginal spaces, so that the biases largely cancel. The only approximation is a locally constant density. Numerically the systematic error scales with k/N and vanishes for independent variables, a conjecture without proof; the ordered Weinman exponential is the one case where the stronger form fails. Extensions to multi-information (Eqs. 23, 30). Conditional mutual information is not treated. | Read |
| [NOTE-939](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-939.md) | Massey — Causality, feedback and directed information | The textbook DMC, P(y^N\|x^N) = Π P(y_n\|x_n), is the DMC used without feedback; the right definition is P(y_n\|x^n y^{n−1}) = P(y_n\|x_n). Directed information I(X^N→Y^N) = Σ I(X^n; Y_n \| Y^{n−1}) is at most I(X^N;Y^N), equal without feedback (Theorem 1), and in a causal system bounds what the output says about the source (Theorem 3), so feedback cannot raise DMC capacity. Statistical dependence has no direction; directed information does. | Read |
| [NOTE-940](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-940.md) | Schreiber — Measuring information transfer | Defines transfer entropy T_{J→I} as the Kullback entropy between I's transition probabilities with and without J's past, at history lengths k for I and l for J (Eq. 4), which is the conditional mutual information I(i_{n+1}; j_n^{(l)} \| i_n^{(k)}). It is directional and ignores static correlation. A kernel estimator is proposed. Tent-map and Ulam-map lattices show it detecting the coupling direction where time-delayed mutual information fails; a heart–breath pair shows an asymmetry that the author says a common trigger could also explain. | Read |
| [NOTE-941](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-941.md) | Eichler and Didelez — Causal reasoning in graphical time series models | Defines the causal effect of intervening on one component of a stationary multivariate time series on another at a later time, and relates it to strong Granger noncausality through mixed graphs. Under Assumption 2.3 (an intervention independent of the system's past and of the other contemporaneous variables, and acting on the future only through the present), a missing Granger edge a → b means no effect on b at the next step, a ∉ an(b) means no effect at any horizon, and time-series back-door and front-door criteria identify effects from observational data. A present edge is only "potentially causal". | Read |
| [NOTE-942](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-942.md) | Williams and Beer — Generalized measures of information transfer | With the I_min partial information decomposition, transfer entropy T_{Y→X} = I(X_{t+1}; Y_t \| X_t) is the unique information of Y_t about X_{t+1} (state-independent transfer, SITE) plus the synergy of X_t and Y_t (state-dependent transfer, SDTE). SITE alone suffices for perfect open-loop controllability (Theorem 1). Time-delayed mutual information is SITE plus redundancy. Two-source transfer splits into unique, redundant and synergistic parts. On a sleep-apnoea recording, heart→breath transfer is all SDTE. | Read |
| [NOTE-943](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-943.md) | Lizier, Prokopenko and Zomaya — Local information transfer as a spatiotemporal filter | Transfer entropy is the expectation of a local transfer entropy, t_{Y→X}(n+1, k, l) = log p(x_{n+1} \| x⁽ᵏ⁾_n, y⁽ˡ⁾_n)/p(x_{n+1} \| x⁽ᵏ⁾_n), defined at every point and possibly negative. Apparent transfer entropy conditions on the destination's past; complete transfer entropy also on its other causal parents. On elementary cellular automata, with k ≥ 6 (rule 110) and k = 16, local transfer entropy highlights gliders and domain walls as the dominant information-transfer structures; k = 1 and local time-lagged mutual information do not. The averages carry none of this. | Read |
| [NOTE-944](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-944.md) v2 | Harder, Salge and Polani — A bivariate measure of redundant information | I_min gives 1 bit of redundancy to two independent bits copied into the target, because it compares amounts of specific information and not their direction in the space of distributions over the target. The paper adds an identity axiom, I∩((X,Y); X, Y) = I(X; Y), and defines a bivariate I_red: project each posterior p(z\|x) onto the convex hull of the other source's posteriors, count what survives, take the smaller direction. I_red satisfies all four axioms and gives a nonnegative PID. It agrees with I_min except where I_min overstates redundancy. | Read |
| [NOTE-945](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-945.md) | James, Barnett and Crutchfield — Information flows? A critique of transfer entropies | Information flow from X to Y is information in Y attributable solely to X's past. Transfer entropy is not it. For Y_t = X_{t−1} ⊕ Y_{t−1} it is 1 bit, but the bit is synergistic, carried by both pasts jointly (co-information −1). For Z_t = X_{t−1} ⊕ Y_{t−1} both transfer entropies are 0, and the causation entropies (conditional transfer entropies) are 1 bit each, again localizing a joint bit. By PID, transfer entropy is unique plus synergistic information; conditioning adds synergy, it does not only remove redundancy. | Read |
| [NOTE-946](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-946.md) | Ay and Polani — Information flows in causal networks | In a finite causal Bayesian network, X_B is causally independent of X_A imposing X_S if setting x_A after setting x_S leaves X_B's post-interventional distribution unchanged. For every model on a DAG this holds iff every directed path from A to B meets S (ud-separation, Theorem 2). Information flow I(X_A → X_B \| X̂_S) is conditional mutual information with interventional probabilities in place of observational ones, zero under causal independence. Examples show it can differ from conditional mutual information and from transfer entropy in either direction. Example 6's one bit holds at k = 1, by the reading's check. | Read |
| [NOTE-947](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-947.md) | Giarrocco & Averbeck — sensory and choice information flow between A1 and PFC | In 37 sessions of simultaneous recordings from A1 and dorsolateral PFC of two macaques reporting by bar release whether two tones came from the same side, cue-side information flowed A1 to PFC only (onset 120–147 ms), while choice information (release or hold) flowed first PFC to A1 (onset 315–365 ms after target) and then A1 to PFC (352–419 ms), both peaking near 500 ms, close to the bar release. The flow measure is a lagged regression on one-dimensional projections, so the result is correlational, within a trial, and does not separate the decision from the motor response. | Read |
| [NOTE-948](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-948.md) | Kübler & Birbaumer — BCI and extinction of goal-directed thinking in CLIS | Of 35 patients trained with EEG BCIs in Tübingen, degree of paralysis explained BCI performance (η² = .40) only because of the seven in the completely locked-in state, none of whom reached the 70% needed for yes/no communication; without them the relation vanished (η² = .12, n.s.). All seven were already in CLIS when training began. The authors propose, by analogy with the curarized rat, that lost perception of the contingency between a response and its consequences extinguishes goal-directed thinking, while "passive sensory information processing is intact", and predict that a contingency learned before CLIS and carried into it should prevent extinction. | Read |
| [NOTE-949](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-949.md) | Slovic — the construction of preference | A review, from an award address, of the preference-reversal literature. Normatively equivalent elicitation procedures (choice against pricing, choice against matching) give systematically different orderings, and about 90% of reversals violate procedure invariance rather than transitivity. Two mechanisms explain them: an attribute weighs more when it is compatible with the response scale, and the prominent attribute weighs more in choice than in matching. Slovic concludes that for important, complex and unfamiliar options preferences are constructed on the spot in elicitation. The evidence is about the response under each procedure; nothing in it tests whether a constructed preference persists or changes later judgements. | Read |
| [NOTE-950](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-950.md) | Ma & Kragel — map-like emotion knowledge in hippocampus and vmPFC | In fMRI of 29 people passively watching 14 emotional films, decoders trained on hippocampal patterns predicted an independent sample's consensus ratings of 13 emotion categories better than positions in a two-dimensional affective space, and vmPFC showed the reverse; patterns could also be decoded into the activity of a Tolman–Eichenbaum Machine that had learned a grid built from rating correlations by random walk, hippocampus favouring its small-scale conjunctive layer and vmPFC its large-scale structural layer. Effects are small (prediction–outcome correlations of about 0.04–0.10), and no learning in the participants was measured. | Read |
| [NOTE-951](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-951.md) | Chaudhary et al. — intracortical spelling in a completely locked-in patient | A man with ALS (born 1985), who had used an eye-movement BCI with an auditory speller until February 2019 and was judged completely locked-in from a few weeks before implantation in March 2019, was given two 64- channel arrays in left motor cortex. Attempted and imagined movements gave no usable signal; from day 86 he was given auditory feedback of firing rate, matched target tones from day 98, and from day 106 spelled with the same speller he had used before CLIS. Over days 106–462 he produced intelligible text on 44 of 107 days on which spelling was attempted, at about 1 character per minute. | Read |
| [NOTE-952](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-952.md) | Pattee — the physics of symbols | The epistemic cut is the separation of subject from object, symbol from referent, controller from controlled, which dynamical laws cannot describe without losing the function across it (von Neumann's regress). Measurement codes a rate-dependent dynamical state into quiescent symbols and control is its converse; both are executed by non-integrable (non-holonomic) constraints. The cut is epistemic, not ontological, and in life it arises first at the genotype–phenotype control interface: in Pattee's account control of construction came first, not measurement. | Read |
| [NOTE-953](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-953.md) | Sung, Rigotti & Lee — factorized goal and uncertainty codes in lateral PFC | A reanalysis of 20 people's fMRI from a 2014 two-stage Markov task with cued goals and block-wise transition noise. Goals and transition uncertainty are linearly decodable, weakly, from vlPFC, dlPFC and OFC, in a geometry whose nonlinear dichotomies decode worse than goal and linear ones ("factorized"), and a goal decoder trained under one noise level transfers to the other. Goal separability and transfer in lateral PFC correlate with choice flexibility and optimality across subjects; uncertainty separability does not. Unfitted model-free agents show a flexibility–stability trade-off that model-based agents and humans do not. | Read |
| [NOTE-954](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-954.md) | Powers, Clark & McFarland — General Feedback Theory, Part I | Builds a hierarchy of negative-feedback control systems in which each order perceives only the feedback signals of the order below and acts only by setting their references, which are replayed recordings of their own past perceptions. An "imagination connection" sends those references back into the higher system's perception, so that it can remember, plan "mentally", hallucinate and dream, under a "mixing control" the authors cannot specify ("We are open to suggestions", p. 20). An inherited N-system, driven by error in intrinsic physiological variables, reorganizes the network at random, forming new input functions as well as new outputs; an organization persists when the behaviour it produces lessens intrinsic error. | Read |
| [NOTE-955](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-955.md) | Fuchs, Mermin & Schack — an introduction to QBism | QBism in eight pages. Quantum states and all probabilities, 0 and 1 included, are an agent's personal judgements; a measurement is "any action an agent takes to elicit a set of possible experiences", and its outcome is the experience it elicits. The agent applies quantum mechanics to everything external to her, other agents and their reports included, and to nothing but her "own direct internal awareness of her own private experience". Locality follows because one agent's experiences are time-like separated; the Bell parameter λ is set outside physical science. No theorem or model: an interpretive essay. | Read |
| [NOTE-956](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-956.md) | Parr & Friston — attention or salience? | A short review that separates two things called attention: gain control, which weights currently available sensory data by their estimated precision, and salience, the expected information gain of an action (typically a saccade) that would acquire new data. It then ties them together: a saccade is driven by a prediction that a location will be sensed with high precision, so covert attention to a place biases an overt saccade there, which the authors read as support for the premotor theory. | Read |
| [NOTE-957](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-957.md) | Feldman & Lynch — self-generated validity | A theoretical paper, with no new data. When the belief, attitude or intention asked about is not already in memory, the question creates it, and the created answer is later retrieved as an input to other answers and to behaviour; when it is in memory, question order and format still decide which earlier answer is used. An earlier response is used for a later one if it is accessible and more diagnostic than other accessible inputs. Expertise, direct experience and trait involvement reduce the effects, because they supply judgements already formed and rehearsed. | Read |
| [NOTE-958](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-958.md) | Sandved-Smith et al. — computational phenomenology of mental action | A three-level discrete active-inference model in which attentional states set the precision of the perceptual likelihood and meta-awareness states set the precision of the attentional likelihood; mental action is a choice of 'stay' or 'switch' over attentional states, defined at the second level only, against a preference to observe oneself 'focused'. Simulations reproduce the cycle of focus, mind-wandering, noticing and refocusing, with longer mind-wandering under low meta-awareness. The stimuli are fixed by the generative process, so mental action changes only how strongly they update belief; the likelihoods themselves are not learned. | Read |
| [NOTE-959](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-959.md) | Powers, Clark & McFarland — General Feedback Theory, Part II | Names six orders of perception, from spinal loops through sensations, configurations, sequences and relationships to system concepts, with demonstrations whose reaction times lengthen with order (about 0.3 s at third order, 0.4–0.45 s at fourth). The N-system "merely alters the properties of a system, thus changing the transformations applied to existing information" (p. 37): reorganization is a change of perception, felt as insight, and a new perceptual organization can be vetoed by imagining its use. Consciousness is defined as a feedback function under N-system action. Conflict freezes a lower system at a virtual reference, and a system switched "entirely to the imagination-connection" is one of the ego's defences. | Read |
| [NOTE-960](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-960.md) | Friston et al. — action and behavior: a free-energy formulation | Existence is taken to require a low-entropy ensemble density; an ergodic assumption turns that entropy into time-averaged surprise, and because the setup stipulates that action is the only way an agent changes the hidden states it senses, action as well as perception must minimize a free-energy bound on surprise. Action enters nowhere in the generative model: it is a gradient descent that fulfils proprioceptive and visual predictions, and in simulations of eye, arm, mountain-car and Lorenz movements it cancels unexpected perturbations so they are not perceived. The paper fixes the model and re-samples the data, and answers the worry that this confirms a wrong model by appeal to existence: agents without the right priors cannot exist. | Read |
| [NOTE-961](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-961.md) | Bruno et al. — self-assessed well-being in chronic locked-in syndrome | Of 168 members of the French LIS association invited, 91 answered and 65 gave usable ratings: 47 (72%) rated their present life at or above the midpoint between their best period before LIS and their worst period ever (median +3), 18 (28%) below (median −4). Happiness was associated with longer time in LIS (OR 1.5 per year), recovered speech (OR 20.5) and absence of anxiety (OR 0.19). All had chronic LIS after a brainstem vascular accident, a median of 8 years earlier; 55% had recovered some speech and 70% some limb movement, and answers were given with a proxy's help. | Read |
| [NOTE-962](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-962.md) | Owen et al. — detecting awareness in the vegetative state | A 23-year-old woman who met the clinical criteria for the vegetative state five months after a traumatic brain injury, told in the scanner to imagine playing tennis or walking through her house, activated the supplementary motor area for the first and parahippocampal, posterior parietal and lateral premotor cortex for the second, as 12 healthy volunteers did. The authors take her compliance as "a clear act of intention" that "confirmed beyond any doubt" her awareness. No question was asked or answered. | Read |
| [NOTE-963](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-963.md) | Powers — Feedback: Beyond Behaviorism | A control system "will produce whatever output is required in order to achieve a constant sensed result" (p. 77), so behaviour is the control of input, not output, and stimulus-response laws follow from the environment once the controlled quantity is found. Above the lowest level a system's output is a reference level for the level below, so the hierarchy closes through lower systems down to muscle effort sensed kinesthetically; its top is a set of inherited intrinsic reference levels whose error drives reorganization. The paper says nothing about imagination: every loop it describes closes through the environment. | Read |
| [NOTE-964](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-964.md) | Monti et al. — willful modulation of brain activity in disorders of consciousness | Of 54 patients diagnosed vegetative (23) or minimally conscious (31), 5, all with traumatic injury, produced task-specific fMRI activity to motor and spatial imagery commands; 4 had been admitted as vegetative, and 2 of those showed no behavioural sign of awareness at the bedside even after the scans were known. One patient, Patient 23, answered five of six autobiographical yes/no questions correctly by choosing which imagery to perform, the investigators scoring blind; the sixth gave no signal. He was not one of the two behaviourally unresponsive patients: retesting found inconsistent signs of a minimally conscious state, but no bedside communication. | Read |
| [NOTE-965](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-965.md) | Rauh, Bertschinger, Olbrich and Jost — Reconsidering unique information | Theorem 2: no redundancy function on the Williams–Beer lattice satisfies symmetry, self-redundancy, monotonicity, non-negative atoms and the identity axiom. In XORCOPY (two independent bits, their XOR, and the target their joint copy) identity forces three 1-bit atoms {i}{jk} under a 2-bit total, so {12}{13}{23} ≤ −1. Bertschinger et al.'s bivariate measures cannot be extended to that lattice. Their unique information is monotone in each argument as expected; their shared and synergistic information violate left monotonicity. | Read |
| [NOTE-966](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-966.md) | Griffith and Koch — Quantifying synergistic mutual information | Synergy is the whole minus the union of its parts. S_VK = I(X_1…n : Y) − I_VK, where the union information I_VK is the least I*(X_1…n : Y) over joints that keep every source–target marginal. It sits between WholeMinusSum and S_max, which respectively subtract redundancy and count unique bits as synergy, and correlational importance measures something else. Versions 1–2 held that independent predictors share no information about the target; v6 withdraws it. For two predictors I_VK is Bertschinger et al.'s optimisation, so S_VK is their CI. | Read |
| [NOTE-967](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-967.md) | Griffith, Chong, James, Ellison and Crutchfield — Intersection information based on common randomness | The redundancy is the information about the target in the Gács–Körner common random variable of the sources, I_∧ = I(X_1 ∧ … ∧ X_n : Y): the largest I(Q : Y) for Q a function of every source. It is defined for any n, satisfies target monotonicity, which no earlier measure did, and lies below I_min. But it is zero whenever the sources have full support, so it fails identity and continuity, and its synergy goes negative. A zero-error variant satisfies identity in zero-error form and goes negative too. | Read |
| [NOTE-968](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-968.md) v2 | Ince — Measuring multivariate redundant information with pointwise common change in surprisal | I_ccs measures redundancy as the expected local co-information over only those events where each source, the joint source and the overlap change the target's surprisal in the same direction, under the maximum-entropy joint matching source–target and joint-source marginals. Defined for any number of sources. It keeps symmetry, self-redundancy, subset equality and an independent-sources identity, and drops Harder et al.'s identity, monotonicity and non-negative atoms. A game-theoretic argument that unique information depends on the source–source marginal is offered against Bertschinger et al. | Read |
| [NOTE-969](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-969.md) | Eyink and Aluie — Localness of energy cascade I | Builds an exact band-pass decomposition of kinetic energy from smooth filters, a multiscale Germano identity, in which each band's energy changes by the flux into it minus the flux out. It then restates, with heuristic sketches, Eyink's (2005) bounds: under a scaling hypothesis on velocity increments with exponents strictly between 0 and 1, the mean energy flux across ℓ takes at most O((ℓ/Δ)^(2/3)) from scales above Δ and O((δ/ℓ)^(2/3)) from scales below δ. It argues, without proof, and checks on one 512³ simulation, that sign cancellations give Kraichnan's faster 4/3 decay. Locality here is in scale, for one field. Nothing in it bears on units. | Read |
| [NOTE-970](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-970.md) | Granero-Belinchón, Roux and Garnier — Scaling of information in turbulence | Estimates, with k-nearest-neighbour estimators, the conditional entropy of a velocity sample given samples a lag τ before it (the "entropy rate") on one Modane wind-tunnel record, as a function of τ. It finds slopes of −1/3 (inertial) and −1 (dissipative) against log of inverse lag, and shows these are S₂'s scaling through a Gaussian formula the data obey. A sign-of-increment conditioning gives unequal entropy rates, which the paper reads as proof of the energy cascade. That inference fails: one-point skewness alone produces the inequality. No information quantity is tied to the energy balance, and none is transferred. | Read |
| [NOTE-971](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-971.md) | Wiskott and Sejnowski — Slow feature analysis | Finds instantaneous functions y = g(x(t)) whose outputs vary as slowly as possible, minimizing ⟨ẏ²⟩ under zero mean, unit variance and decorrelation. Over a fixed nonlinear expansion (all monomials of degree one and two), the problem is solved in closed form by sphering and then taking the smallest eigenvectors of the derivative covariance, a generalized eigenproblem. Stacked modules learn translation, size, rotation, contrast and, less well, illumination invariance for 1-D patterns, depending only on the training stimulus. The closed form is proved; everything about invariance, generalization and hierarchy is demonstrated on synthetic signals. The premise that slower means more abstract is assumed, not shown, and no generative model is used. | Read |
| [NOTE-972](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-972.md) v2 | Raju, Machta and Sethna — Information loss under coarse graining | For a Boltzmann distribution linear in its couplings, the Fisher information that coarse-grained data lose is the expected conditional covariance of the energy operators. Under an exact RG step with linear beta functions it is the Hessian of the analytic constant, so the singular part of the metric is kept. In the diffusion model it is exact: the metric scales as n^(1−μ) by Hermite order. The claims that every relevant direction is kept and that irrelevant ones contract at b^−(d−2λ) rest on a scaling argument. On the paper's own scalings the dividing line is λ = d/2, not 0. | Read |
| [NOTE-973](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-973.md) | Parish and Duraisamy — Non-Markovian closure for LES via Mori–Zwanzig | Derives large-eddy-simulation closures from the Mori–Zwanzig identity by Stinis's finite-memory approximation, which turns the memory integral into auxiliary relaxation equations, a finite Markovian augmentation of the resolved modes. Its error is not bounded and its memory length is fitted (Burgers: τ₀ ≈ 0.2 over the spectral radius of the resolved Jacobian) or preset. Against filtered DNS it matches dynamic Smagorinsky on isotropic turbulence and channel flow, beats Smagorinsky and the t-model on the Taylor–Green vortex, and puts the subgrid drain at the cutoff, as DNS does. | Read |
| [NOTE-975](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-975.md) | Chorin, Hald and Kupferman — Optimal prediction with memory | Writes the resolved components of an ODE with random unresolved initial data as an exact generalized Langevin equation (Markovian term, memory, noise) under three projections, and approximates the memory two ways: by solving a Volterra equation for its expansion coefficients from Monte Carlo correlation functions, and by the t-damping (t-model) equation dΦ/dt = R(Φ) + tS(Φ), which needs no prior data. On one 4-variable Hamiltonian example both restore the decay of the conditional mean that the Markovian truncation misses, the Volterra scheme to about t ≈ 8. No error bound for any approximation, and no Markovian augmentation. | Read |
| [NOTE-976](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-976.md) | Shalizi and Crutchfield — Information bottlenecks, causal states and statistical relevance bases | A three-page note. For memoryless transduction X → Y, the causal states are the cells of the partition of inputs by p(y\|x). Among partitions that keep all information about Y, they have the least entropy. The note asserts, calling it evident, that these are what the information bottleneck delivers as β → ∞, and that Salmon's statistical relevance basis is the same construction. It proves neither, and it says nothing about the IB solutions at finite β, nor whether they nest. The record supplies the proof of the limit and shows that every finite-β optimum is a stochastic coarsening of the causal partition ([THEORY-743](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-743.md)). | Read |
| [NOTE-977](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-977.md) | Shpak, Stadler, Wagner and Altenberg — Simon–Ando decomposability and fitness landscapes | States Simon and Ando's (1961) theorem for x(t+1) = (A* + εC)x, with A* block-diagonal, as existence statements: as ε → 0 the non-leading eigenvectors approach the blocks', and times T0 < T1 < T2 < T3 exist that separate within-block relaxation, quasi-equilibrium, aggregate cross-block dynamics and global equilibrium. No rate in ε and no bound on aggregation error is given. It then applies an entrywise proxy (minimal within-class rate ≫ maximal cross-class rate) to mutation–selection on hypercubes, which low mutation rates meet trivially, and to recombination, which rarely meets it. It concludes that Simon–Ando aggregation is one source of dynamical sufficiency among several, distinct from symmetry (equitable partitions) and from linkage-equilibrium character aggregation. | Read |
| [NOTE-978](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-978.md) | Crutchfield and Shalizi — Thermodynamic depth of causal states | The rate at which Lloyd and Pagels' thermodynamic depth grows (the dive) is the entropy rate of whatever macrostate process it is computed over. So depth measures randomness. Lumping or splitting macrostates sets it to any value from zero up. The paper proposes the causal states as the macrostates. Among partitions of the past that predict the future as well as the past does, they are the coarsest, with the least statistical complexity and the least dive ([THEORY-756](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-756.md)). Several errors are noted. One stated entropy rate is in fact a single-symbol entropy, a footnote makes prescience vacuous, and a strict inequality fails in general. The result survives. The "objectivity" is relative to the measuring instrument, as the paper's own logistic-map example shows. | Read |
| [NOTE-979](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-979.md) | Shpak, Stadler, Wagner and Hermisson — Aggregation of variables and system decomposition | Separates aggregation of variables, a lower-dimensional map y = Qx whose dynamics close, from decomposition into non-interacting subsets: either can hold without the other. For a linear system the aggregate operator must satisfy ĀQ = QA. For a partition, the block sums close for every state exactly when the partition is column-equitable. Equitable partitions of mutation–selection matrices reduce single- and two-peak fitness landscapes exactly, and fail for three or more peaks unless the classes are refined to overlap classes. Simon–Ando aggregation is treated as the approximate limiting case, without error bounds. | Read |
| [NOTE-980](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-980.md) | No, Ingber and Weissman — Strong successive refinability | Extends successive refinement to second order. For finite alphabets, a two-stage code can reach both decoders' rates with their dispersion terms if the source is successively refinable throughout a neighbourhood of its law (Corollary 6), which holds for any discrete source under Hamming distortion; the Gaussian under squared error is shown directly. Layered codes then use L_n refinement stages to cut encoding complexity, at a rate penalty of order L_n log n / n, for binary and Gaussian sources. It does not treat logarithmic loss, which the reading that named it had recalled; the log-loss refinability result is No and Weissman's, concerns direct log-loss with soft reconstructions of the source itself, and does not reach the information bottleneck, whose loss is remote. | Read |
| [NOTE-981](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-981.md) | Charvin, Catenacci Volpi and Polani — Exact and soft successive refinement of the IB | Defines successive refinement for the information bottleneck as extending a coarse optimum T₁ to a fine optimum (T₁, S), and shows it equivalent to some pair of optima forming X → T₂ → T₁. With an injective fine decoder, it is also equivalent to the coarse decoder points lying in the convex hull of the fine ones, which a linear programme checks. Refinability is proved for binary X and Y, for Y a function of X, and for jointly Gaussian variables. Numerically the hull test on computed optima often fails, and the loss, measured by unique information, stays under a few percent. Those failures are uncertified. Run here with certified optima, the test shows that the four-state source of [CLAIM-387](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-387.md) is not refinable between β = 8 and β = 12: its stochastic optima do not nest either. | Read |
| [NOTE-982](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-982.md) | Constantin, E and Titi — Onsager's conjecture on energy conservation | A one-page proof that a weak solution of the 3D incompressible Euler equations on the periodic box conserves energy if it lies in L³(0,T; B^α_{3,∞}) ∩ C([0,T]; L²) with α > 1/3. The flux of energy into scales below a mollification scale ε is written exactly as a commutator, (u⊗u)^ε − u^ε⊗u^ε = r_ε − (u−u^ε)⊗(u−u^ε), of size ε^(2α), against a gradient of size ε^(α−1), so the flux is O(ε^(3α−1)) and vanishes. This is the positive half of Onsager's conjecture only. It does not show that rougher solutions dissipate. Two printed formulas in the manuscript are wrong as typeset, without effect on the result. | Read |
| [NOTE-983](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-983.md) | Rahaman et al. — On the Spectral Bias of Neural Networks | A ReLU network is piecewise linear, so its Fourier transform falls as k^(−d−1) along almost every direction and as k^(−2) along the normals to the faces of its linear regions; that is proved for compactly supported networks only. Trained networks fit low frequencies first, even when high frequencies carry ten times the amplitude, and high-frequency components are the first to be destroyed by parameter noise; both are experiments. The tie from the decay to the order of learning is a heuristic bound, and the volume "proof" in Appendix D does not hold. On a curve embedded in the plane, high latent frequencies are fitted more easily as the curve gets more petals. The paper puts this down to the shape of the curve, but most of it comes from the curve getting longer. | Read |
| [NOTE-984](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-984.md) | Coifman and Maggioni — Diffusion wavelets | A self-adjoint diffusion operator T with spectrum in [0, 1] defines a multiresolution analysis by thresholding its dyadic powers at a precision ε: V_j is spanned by the eigenvectors with λ^{t_j} ≥ ε, so the V_j are exactly nested spectral subspaces and the wavelet spaces W_j are spectral bands, about one octave of the generator each. The paper's contribution is an algorithm that builds localized orthonormal bases for approximations of these spaces without computing eigenvectors, by squaring the operator on each compressed basis. As written, that algorithm thresholds T^{2^{j−1}}, not T^{2^j−1} as the paper states, and the paper's own Fig. 9 follows the former. Localization, stability and the near-linear complexity are argued or observed, not proved for the compressed algorithm. | Read |
| [NOTE-985](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-985.md) | Coifman and Lafon — Diffusion maps | A symmetric non-negative kernel normalized into a reversible Markov chain gives a family of diffusion distances D_t, one per number of steps t, and an embedding by eigenvectors weighted by λ_l^t in which Euclidean distance is D_t. An α-normalization by a kernel density estimate makes the small-bandwidth limit the graph Laplacian with a density potential (α = 0), the Langevin generator whose invariant density is the sampling density (α = 1/2) or the Laplace–Beltrami operator (α = 1). The truncation is claimed accurate to relative precision δ, which is wrong: the bound is absolute. Several displays carry errors, and the heat-kernel proof has a gap. | Read |
| [NOTE-986](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-986.md) | Nadler, Lafon, Coifman and Kevrekidis — Diffusion maps and reaction coordinates | Ties diffusion maps to the dynamics that generated the data. For samples from p = e^{−U}, the small-ε generator of the α-normalized walk is Δψ − 2(1 − α)∇ψ·∇U: the graph Laplacian (α = 0) gives Fokker–Planck with potential 2U, α = 1/2 gives the Langevin dynamics with potential U itself, and α = 1 gives Laplace–Beltrami. So the slow eigenfunctions of the α = 1/2 map approximate the slow modes of the sampled stochastic system, and the paper proposes them as reaction coordinates. The expansions are formal, and with the paper's kernel every printed generator is too large by a factor of two. Its double-well example is separable. From equilibrium samples the slow eigenfunction is recovered well and the slow eigenvalue is not. That slow eigenfunctions are closed in mean, and in law only under a condition, is the record's addition. | Read |
| [NOTE-987](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-987.md) | Rosas, Mediano et al. — Reconciling emergences | The primary paper behind [LIT-025](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-025.md). A supervenient feature V is causally emergent of order k iff Un⁽ᵏ⁾(V_t; X_t′ \| X_t) > 0; a system has one iff Syn⁽ᵏ⁾(X_t; X_t′) > 0, and the witness the proof gives is the microstate itself. Syn⁽ᵏ⁾ = D⁽ᵏ⁾ + G⁽ᵏ⁾ by definition of the ΦID atoms. The practical criteria Ψ, Δ, Γ are redundancy-free and sufficient only, and as proved they certify the system's capacity, not the candidate feature: under the minimum-MI decomposition the parity of two independent self-copying bits has Ψ = 1 bit and no emergence. Ψ is the whole-minus-sum information about V's next value minus V's one-step dynamical dependence, which ties it to Barnett–Seth dynamical independence ([THEORY-764](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-764.md)). | Read |
| [NOTE-988](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-988.md) v2 | Equitz and Cover — Successive refinement of information | Defines successive refinement: a description at distortion D₁, followed by an addendum reaching D₂ < D₁, with both stages at the rate–distortion limit. For finite alphabets it proves this possible iff some pair of optimal test channels forms a Markov chain X → X̂₂ → X̂₁, so that the coarse reconstruction is a stochastic degradation of the fine one, not necessarily a function of it. The condition holds for every discrete source under Hamming distortion, and the paper also shows it for the Gaussian under squared error and the Laplacian under absolute error. It fails for the three-letter source (1−p, 2p, 1−p)/2 under absolute error when p < 3 − 2√2, where the finer optimum uses fewer reproduction letters than the coarser. The whole result is asymptotic, for block codes. The paper's own Fig. 1 shows that single-shot optimal quantizers of a Gaussian do not nest even though the Gaussian is refinable. | Read |
| [NOTE-989](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-989.md) | Chorin, Hald and Kupferman — Optimal prediction and the Mori–Zwanzig representation | Writes Zwanzig's nonlinear Mori–Zwanzig identity with the projection taken as conditional expectation on the resolved variables under an invariant measure: ∂ₜSᵗA = R(SᵗA) + ∫₀ᵗ K(s, S^{t−s}A) ds + S⊥ᵗF, with R(A) = E[LA\|A], F = LA − E[LA\|A] and K(s, A) = E[LS⊥ˢF\|A]. First-order optimal prediction, dv/dt = R(v), is that identity with the memory and noise dropped, and for a canonical Hamiltonian system it is Hamiltonian in a renormalized 𝓗 = −log∫e^{−H}. In a perturbative nonlinear Schrödinger example with one resolved mode, a memory kernel cut off at a hand-chosen time recovers the decay of the conditional mean that the Markovian scheme misses. The paper states no fluctuation–dissipation relation and no criterion for when the Markovian term suffices. | Read |
| [NOTE-990](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-990.md) | Lush, Botan, Scott, Seth, Ward & Dienes — Trait phenomenological control and the rubber hand illusion | Hypnotisability predicted rubber hand illusion reports after both synchronous and asynchronous brushing (n = 353, about half a scale point per SWASH point, rs 0.26), a visual control item as well, and synchronous drift weakly (rs 0.11); it also predicted vicarious pain and mirror touch. The expectation manipulation failed and the pre-registered difference-score test was inconclusive, so the study shows that the standard controls do not exclude suggestion, not that the illusion is suggestion. | Read |
| [NOTE-991](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-991.md) | Apps & Tsakiris — The free-energy self | A free-energy account of self-recognition and body ownership. One's own body, face and voice are represented probabilistically as "me" by a high-level multimodal prior learned from cross-modal correlations, and the self is "the most parsimonious and accurate explanation for sensory inputs". The rubber hand, enfacement and rubber-voice illusions are one effect: synchronous stimulation leaves unimodal surprise that multimodal areas explain away by shifting probability from one's own body part to the other's. Context acts as a prior. No brain area is self-specific. The authors grant there is little direct evidence and that the account is hard to falsify with standard fMRI. | Read |
| [NOTE-992](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-992.md) | Abdulkarim & Ehrsson — No causal link between hand position sense and limb ownership | A motor slid the hidden hand 8 cm toward or away from the rubber hand during brushing, too slowly to be noticed. Pointing followed it by about 5–6 cm, but questionnaire ownership depended only on synchrony and not on where the hand was moved, in two experiments of 18. With the hand still, the classic synchronous drift and its correlation with the illusion reappeared. The authors conclude drift is not a cause of ownership; the null is from small samples within the illusion's known spatial range. | Read |
| [NOTE-993](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-993.md) | Kalckert & Ehrsson — Moving a rubber hand that feels like your own | A moving rubber hand illusion in which the participant's hidden finger moves a model finger by a rod. Synchrony gave ownership, agency and drift toward the model; asynchrony removed all three. Passive movement removed agency and kept ownership and drift; a model hand rotated 180° removed ownership and drift and kept agency. The double dissociation is on questionnaires; agency was stronger, and tied to ownership, only when the hand was owned. | Read |
| [NOTE-994](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-994.md) | Borg, Harrison, Stazicker & Salomons — Is the folk concept of pain polyeidic? | Six objections to the experimental philosophers' claim that the folk concept of pain is bodily, not mental: small and skewed samples, acute pain only, a loaded "in the mind" probe, means near neutral, a non-Cartesian mental reading of the same data, and an invalid step from "partly bodily" to "bodily". Pilot vignettes in which damage never hurt drew mind-centred answers. The authors propose that the folk concept is "polyeidic": several framing-sensitive dimensions, of which mental/bodily is one. | Read |
| [NOTE-995](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-995.md) | Starmans & Bloom — Windows to the soul | Asked which of two pictured flies or snowflakes was "closer to" a cartoon character, preschoolers and adults chose those near the eyes, even when the eyes were on an alien's chest and even over positions the character could see. The authors conclude that people intuitively locate the self at or near the eyes, and, since 4-year-olds do it too, not from learned ideas about the brain. The judgement is about where another, drawn person is; the step to the self, and on to a "phenomenological sense" of where we reside, is assumed and not tested. | Read |
| [NOTE-996](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-996.md) | Nichols & Bruno — Intuitions about personal identity | Survey studies of Arizona undergraduates on Williams's personal-identity cases. A transplant case makes memory look necessary for being "still Jim"; a stripped-down Pain case has about 70% say "you will feel the pain" after distinctive mental states are wiped; neither depends on first- or third-person telling, so Williams's explanation by person fails here. Abstract questions and a forced choice favour psychology (over 80%; 64%, p = 0.053). The authors weigh intuitions by robustness and conclude for a psychological criterion conditionally. The results describe a concept under framing; they do not show what persistence is, and the Pain item may test bare sentience, not identity. | Read |
| [NOTE-997](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-997.md) | Ehrsson et al. — No specific relationship between hypnotic suggestibility and the rubber hand illusion | A reanalysis of Lush et al.'s (2020) open data, n = 353. The synchronous-minus-asynchronous difference in rubber-hand illusion ratings is unrelated to hypnotisability (rho = -0.066, BF01 = 5.7), is significant in every hypnotisability quartile, and is not changed by explicit suggestions about which condition should work; the hypnotisability correlations Lush et al. report appear equally for the asynchronous condition and an "impossible" control item. The authors conclude the illusion is a perceptual one, "driven primarily by multisensory mechanisms". The reply grants every number and disputes that the asynchronous condition controls for expectation. | Read |
| [NOTE-998](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-998.md) | Hohwy & Paton — Explaining away the body | With a foreign arm seen exactly where one's own arm lies, synchronous tapping raised ratings that the felt touch was produced on the seen arm, and after onset also that a finger hovering 5 cm away caused it or that it was caused on a cardboard box; the box gave no synchrony difference without prior onset. Samples of 9 to 13, single leading questions, no ownership item, no expectation measure, and a 0.13 °C cooling of the real hand in one comparison of four, significant only one-tailed. | Read |
| [NOTE-999](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-999.md) | Lenggenhager, Tadi, Metzinger & Blanke — Video ergo sum | In video virtual reality, synchronous stroking of one's back and of a body seen 2 m ahead made people rate that body as theirs and shift their felt self-location about 17–25 cm toward it, in two samples of 14; a mannequin worked, a box mostly did not. Nobody felt disembodied or saw from elsewhere, so the authors claim a partial, heautoscopy-like state, not an out-of-body experience. The effects are modest and partly inconsistent, and critics argued they may be self-recognition in a video system rather than an illusion of ownership. | Read |
| [NOTE-1000](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1000.md) | Seth — Interoceptive inference, emotion, and the embodied self | An opinion article that extends predictive coding to interoception. Felt emotion is the content of hierarchical top-down predictions of the causes of interoceptive signals. Prediction errors are registered in the anterior insula, and are also cancelled by autonomic action under attenuated precision. The experience of body ownership is the same inference run over interoceptive and exteroceptive signals together. The evidence is indirect and cited: insula anticipation and error responses, false cardiac feedback, interoceptive sensitivity predicting rubber-hand susceptibility, and a heartbeat-synchronous virtual hand owned more. No direct test is claimed. | Read |
| [NOTE-1001](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1001.md) | Roseboom & Lush — Serious problems with interpreting rubber hand illusion experiments | Resampling 351 synchronous-condition reports from Lush et al. 2020 into 10,000 studies of 20, the authors find that samples from above the median of hypnotisability almost always "find" the rubber hand illusion, and samples from below it find agreement with the ownership statement about 4% of the time. The ownership result holds at n = 50; the result for the averaged statements is largely a matter of power. No asynchronous condition, drift or new data are analysed. | Read |
| [NOTE-1002](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1002.md) | Blanke & Metzinger — Full-body illusions and minimal phenomenal selfhood | Names minimal phenomenal selfhood (MPS), the simplest experience of being a self, and gives it three dimensions: global self-identification with the body, self-location, and a weak, geometrical first-person perspective. Part ownership (rubber hand, somatoparaphrenia) does not reach MPS; out-of-body experience, heautoscopy and full-body illusions do, varying it dimension by dimension. A passive multisensory sense of owning the whole body suffices, so agency is causally enabling but not constitutive. The necessity and sufficiency claims are asserted, not shown. | Read |
| [NOTE-1003](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1003.md) | Lush & Seth — Reply to: No specific relationship between hypnotic suggestibility and the rubber hand illusion | The reply to Ehrsson et al. accepts their reanalyses and denies their reading: expectancies are higher for synchronous than asynchronous brushing, the difference does not vary with hypnotisability (b = -0.16, P = 0.072, B = 0.07), so a null relation between hypnotisability and the synchrony effect is what demand characteristics predict. Agreement with the ownership item rises with hypnotisability (b = 0.76 per SWASH point, rs = 0.27) and reaches minimal agreement only in the top 31%. Whether multisensory integration matters to RHI measures awaits experiments that control expectation. It shows that the suggestion control [THEORY-765](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-765.md) accepts can be met without the confound being removed. | Read |
| [NOTE-1004](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1004.md) | Longo et al. — What is embodiment? A psychometric approach | 131 people rated 27 statements after synchronous and asynchronous brushing of a rubber hand. Principal components analysis found embodiment of the rubber hand, loss of own hand, movement and affect in both conditions and deafference after asynchrony only; embodiment split into ownership, location and agency. Ownership and location crossed from negative to positive with synchrony and each predicted proprioceptive drift (1.34 cm against 0.30 cm); agency stayed negative. No control separates any of it from expectation. | Read |
| [NOTE-1005](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1005.md) | Lush — Demand characteristics confound the rubber hand illusion | People told about the rubber hand procedure, but never put through it, expect the illusion statements more than the control statements and more under synchronous than asynchronous brushing (d = 1.40 and 1.05, n = 20), which is the pattern published reports show. So the field's standard controls do not control for suggestion. The paper does not show that the illusion is suggestion, and says so. | Read |
| [NOTE-1006](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1006.md) | Botvinick & Cohen — Rubber hands 'feel' touch that eyes see | The founding report of the rubber hand illusion. Synchronous brushing of a seen rubber hand and the hidden real hand made ten subjects feel the touch at the rubber hand and feel it as their own; after 30 minutes, blind reaches drifted toward the rubber hand in proportion to how long the illusion lasted, and asynchronous brushing removed both effects. The authors read it as constraint satisfaction among vision, touch and proprioception, and conclude that intermodal matching "can be sufficient for self-attribution". | Read |
| [NOTE-1007](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1007.md) | Reuter, Sienhold & Sytsma — Putting pain in its proper place | Three online studies on the "pain is in my fingertip, the fingertip is in my mouth" argument. People reject its conclusion for pain about as much as for tissue damage and inflammation, and accept it for a paper-clip; across fourteen items, acceptance tracks how misleading the conclusion is rated; and "technically speaking" wording raises acceptance. The authors explain the argument's failure by implicature, not by an intensional "pain" or a non-spatial "in", and conclude that the data favour a bodily conception of pain. | Read |
| [NOTE-1008](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1008.md) | Alsmith & Longo — Where exactly am I? | Ten adults pointed a rotating pointer "directly at" themselves, by hand blindfolded or by eye. Answers fell mostly on the upper face or the upper torso, and the pointer's starting position, above or below, decided which. The authors conclude that the self is judged neither spread over the body nor at one point, and that the spatial concept of the self is "inherently ambiguous". A pilot-sized study with a fifth of its trials lost and a misreported reanalysis; its start effect is also what a first-acceptable-stop strategy predicts. | Read |
| [NOTE-1009](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1009.md) | Rohde, Di Luca & Ernst — Feeling of ownership and proprioceptive drift do not go hand in hand | With robot stroking and a visual probe of felt finger position, drift toward a rubber hand was as large when the hand was only seen as under synchronous stroking (about 6 cm), and as large under asynchronous stroking interrupted every 10 s; only continuous asynchrony kept it near zero. Ownership by questionnaire needed synchrony. The authors conclude that drift is visuo-proprioceptive integration that asynchrony suppresses, separate from ownership, and not a proxy for it. Groups of ten; the vision-only ownership report is anecdotal. | Read |
| [NOTE-1013](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1013.md) v2 | Buckmaster, De Lellis, Székelyhidi and Vicol — Onsager's conjecture for admissible weak solutions | The admissible version of the negative half of Onsager's conjecture. For every β < 1/3 and every smooth strictly positive e(t) on [0, T] there is a C^β weak solution of 3D Euler on the torus with ∫\|v\|² = e(t) exactly, so with e decreasing the energy only falls and the coarse-grained flux runs into vanishing scales on every time interval ([THEORY-776](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-776.md)). That is the one-way transfer Isett's solutions lacked, but one-way only for the box as a whole (no local energy inequality), and chosen by the prescribed profile, since an increasing e works just as well. | Read |
| [NOTE-1014](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1014.md) | Boyle — The Line: AI and the Future of Personhood | A law professor's essay on the line between persons and things, run across four cases: AI, corporations, nonhuman animals and transgenic entities. Personhood is pressed on two tracks, empathy-driven moral reasoning and efficiency-driven legal engineering, and the corporate history shows the second track working without a theory. Boyle predicts some intermediate legal status for AI, argues that capacity-based criteria cannot escape a species-bound standpoint, and ends on a hybrid of species membership as of right plus capacity. It argues and predicts; it does not measure. | Read |
| [NOTE-1015](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1015.md) | Schüler and Wiskott — Slow feature analysis as variational inference | Under a Gaussian random-walk prior on the latents and an encoder N(g(x_t), I) that sees one time step, the ELBO is a per-point reconstruction term minus half the unordered slowness loss, an exact identity (up to a constant the paper drops by a slip). The reconstruction term stands in for SFA's constraints, by argument. In the linear case the paper gives only a necessary condition; solving it here shows the optimum recovers SFA's slow span on whitened input, cut at lag-one autocorrelation ½, with no basis or order, and departs from SFA on raw input. Its two-sentence account of Turner and Sahani is not a substitute for reading them. | Read |
| [NOTE-1016](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1016.md) | Tushnet — Worth a Thousand Words: The Images of Copyright | Copyright law takes the word as its model and treats images as either transparent or opaque, with incoherent results in copyrightability, infringement, authorship and fair use. Realism is a style, not a fact. Describing an image changes how it is seen and remembered, so a test that asks factfinders to dissect works in words and then judge their gestalt cannot work. The proposed cure is a reproduction right against near-exact copies plus a narrowed derivative-works right. | Read |
| [NOTE-1017](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1017.md) | Balganesh — The Immanent Rationality of Copyright Law | A review essay on Drassinower's What's Wrong with Copying?. It reports a Kantian, rights-based account on which a work is a communicative act and infringement is compelled speech, praises its coherence, and defends rationalist theorizing against the charge that it is faith-based. It then objects that the method needs a criterion of what is fundamental, a defence of autonomy if it is to justify, an account of copyright's private-law enforcement, and room for change over time and for instrumental reasoning at the level of the system. | Read |
| [NOTE-1018](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1018.md) | Machta, Chachra, Transtrum and Sethna — Parameter space compression | Two physics models are not sloppy at their microscopic scale and become so when observed coarsely. For the hopping model the Fisher eigenvalues of the density at time t scale as t^(3/2−k), proved here ([THEORY-774](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-774.md)). For a decimated critical Ising model, Monte Carlo shows the field and temperature eigenvalues staying put while the rest fall in bands drawn at b^(2y−d) per step ([THEORY-777](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-777.md), Proposed). That rate, the source of [LIT-1254](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1254.md)'s Eq. 21, is argued by the same scaling argument, read off a figure without error bars, so [THEORY-742](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-742.md)'s scaling claim stays scaling-only. The supplement already states the d/2 line. The causal claim about emergent theories is not shown. | Read |
| [NOTE-1019](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1019.md) | Sotomayor — Andy Warhol Foundation for the Visual Arts, Inc. v. Goldsmith | Under the first fair-use factor, transformation is a difference in the purpose of a particular use, judged by degree and weighed against commerciality. New meaning or message counts only as evidence of a different purpose, and copying is justified most clearly when the source is the target. AWF's licence of Orange Prince to illustrate a Prince magazine shared the photograph's purpose and was commercial, so the factor favours Goldsmith. Kagan's dissent would measure the factor by added expression and meaning. | Read |
| [NOTE-1020](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1020.md) | Del Vecchio and Slotine — Contraction and singular perturbation | Contraction gives global, explicit, uniform-in-time bounds for singular perturbation: the fast state reaches an εχ_z(d + K)/λ_z neighbourhood of the slow manifold at rate λ_z/ε, and the reduced (quasi-steady-state) trajectory is O(ε)-accurate for all time. Theorem 3 as printed is false: it needs the reduced system, not f alone, to be contracting. The robustness lemma is proved for constant metrics only; the reading re-derives it for state- and time-dependent ones, and with it the two steps [THEORY-771](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-771.md) lacked. | Read |
| [NOTE-1021](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1021.md) | Boyle — The Public Domain | Intellectual property is a limited monopoly, and its limits and the public domain do as much work as its rights. Cheaper copying makes the limits more important, not less. A second enclosure is fencing facts, genes, methods and musical fragments without evidence that it helps; the database right is the one natural experiment, and it failed. The music chapter shows a genre founded by rewording recent songs. The argument is mostly from chosen cases. | Read |
| [NOTE-1023](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1023.md) | Lessig — Remix: Making Art and Commerce Thrive in the Hybrid Economy | Remix is quotation in media, and its meaning comes from the reference, so it needs the original. Copyright regulates copies, every digital use is a copy, so the law that once left amateurs alone now reaches every ordinary use and makes read/write culture presumptively illegal. Commercial and sharing economies are kept apart by whether money is a proper term; hybrids join them and survive only while the line holds. The legal reforms and the economics are argued, not measured. | Read |
| [NOTE-1024](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1024.md) | U.S. Copyright Office — Copyright and Artificial Intelligence, Part 3: Generative AI Training | Training copies works at every input step, so the copy trigger fires and everything turns on fair use. Weights count as copies only of works they can regenerate. Under Warhol the training use is judged by its ultimate purpose: often transformative for a general model, barely so for one that serves the originals' audience. Expression, not just ideas, is learned, and machine learning is not human learning. Market dilution by same-kind outputs is harm. Licensing should develop without intervention. | Read |
| [NOTE-1025](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1025.md) | Bousquet and Slotine — Contraction and near-decomposability | Under contraction of the fast modules and of the reduced slow system, and coupling terms bounded affinely in the off-manifold state, a nearly decomposable system stays within O(ε) of its singular-perturbation reduction, uniformly in time after a transient of order (1/β_f + 1/(εβ_g)) log(1/ε), for ε below an explicit critical separation ε_c. Deterministic trajectory error only. Remark 8 prints ε_c inverted, and the slow-error bound needs an unstated d_g = 0. | Read |
| [NOTE-1026](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1026.md) | Perzanowski and Schultz — The End of Ownership | Ownership of what we buy is being replaced by licences, DRM and services. The law of exhaustion that protected buyers is built around owning a tangible copy, and digital use and transfer either copy at every step or involve no copy the buyer holds. The authors argue licences are permissions that cannot redefine a sale, show by survey that "Buy Now" misleads, and propose a multifactor digital exhaustion test. Argued from cases and one survey; US law as of 2016. | Read |
| [NOTE-1028](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1028.md) | Chorin and Lu — Discrete stochastic parametrization by NARMAX | Model reduction done wholly in discrete time: advance the resolved variables by a fixed integrator and fit the exact one-step discrepancy as a NARMAX series, so memory lives in a few lags of the discrepancy, the resolved variable and the innovations. On Lorenz 96 with ε = 0.5 one or two lags reproduce x₁'s statistics and double forecast lead time at δ = 0.05. The link to Mori–Zwanzig is analogy, not derivation; nothing is proved and no error is bounded. The record's check: a partially observed linear Gaussian VAR(1) is exactly ARMA, with order 1 + the rank of its MZ memory kernels, so a memory non-zero at every lag is carried exactly by finitely many history-measurable coordinates. | Read |
| [NOTE-1029](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1029.md) | Lin and Lu — Wiener projections and the Koopman–Mori–Zwanzig formalism | An exact link between Mori–Zwanzig and NARMAX, with the approximation named. For an invertible map with an invariant measure, projecting onto the whole past of chosen functions of the resolved variables removes the memory term: the reduced equation is the causal Wiener filter on the coarse variable's own history, with a residual orthogonal to all of it. NARMAX follows only by an "uncontrolled" rational approximation of the filter; no error is bounded.
