The record's checks: Mori's kernels and the Wiener filter are both fixed by the coarse variable's autocovariance; for a scalar coarse variable of a linear Gaussian VAR(1) both are rational with the same numerator, the rational form is exact, and the memory Hankel rank is d − 1 for any rational autocovariance of rank d. | Read |
| [NOTE-1030](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1030.md) | Rosas et al. — Software in the natural world | Three exact closures of a coarse-graining Z of a stationary discrete process X, built from computational mechanics. Informational closure (the micro past adds nothing to predicting Z, which is Barnett–Seth dynamical independence) is proved equivalent to causal closure (Z's ε-machine equals its υ-machine). For spatial maps it implies computational closure (Z's ε-machine is a coarse-graining of X's), and the converse fails. For Markov chains closure is tied to strong lumpability. The proofs of the main equivalences hold, re-derived in [THEORY-820](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-820.md) and [THEORY-822](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-822.md). The lattice claims are asserted and in part false. Several examples contain slips. The modular random walk closes by symmetry, not modularity. Nothing is said about approximate closure. | Read |
| [NOTE-1031](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1031.md) | Besley and Prat — Handcuffs for the grabbing hand | A retrospective-voting model in which an incumbent can pay outlets to suppress verifiable bad news. Because one outlet reporting informs every voter, each outlet must be paid what it would earn as the only one to break the story, so the media are captured exactly when n·τa < r: the number of outlets, the transaction cost of transfers and audience revenue protect against capture, and the rent of office invites it. Capture ends turnover and lowers voter welfare without deceiving anyone: voters know silence is uninformative. | Read |
| [NOTE-1032](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1032.md) | Beckers and Halpern — Abstracting causal models | Shows that Rubenstein et al.'s exact transformation is too permissive, because a distribution or a sparse intervention set can hide essential differences, and strengthens it in four steps: uniform transformation (exact for every distribution, equivalent to a map on contexts that commutes with every allowed intervention), τ-abstraction (τ surjective, the map on interventions fixed by τ), strong abstraction (every intervention τ can translate is allowed) and constructive abstraction (τ acts variable-cluster by variable-cluster), which it says all three of Rubenstein et al.'s examples are. | Read |
| [NOTE-1033](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1033.md) | Kleinberg and Raghavan — Algorithmic monoculture and social welfare | Two firms each hire the best available candidate by either a private noisy ranking or one shared algorithmic ranking. If, at equal accuracy, a second mover prefers an independent ranking (preference for the first position) and is better off after a less accurate competitor (preference for weaker competition), then for every human accuracy there is a more accurate algorithm that both firms strictly prefer to use, yet both are worse off, and so is welfare, than if neither used it. The Mallows model meets the conditions for every candidate distribution; Gaussian and Laplacian random utility models meet them for three candidates; Plackett–Luce never does. | Read |
| [NOTE-1034](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1034.md) | Bergemann and Morris — Information design, a unified perspective | A designer who can commit to how players are informed, but not to what they do, can attain exactly the Bayes correlated equilibria: joint distributions of states and actions in which no player, told his recommended action, wants to deviate. The set is a polytope given by linear obedience constraints, so information design is a linear program over it. Read literally there is a designer; read metaphorically the set bounds what any information structure could produce. More prior information shrinks the set. Public signals serve a designer who wants correlated actions, private ones the reverse. Its two-firm example with strategic substitutes misstates the optimal rule for the parameters it assumes. | Read |
| [NOTE-1036](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1036.md) | Hayek — The use of knowledge in society | Argues that the economic problem of a society is not allocating given resources by a known plan but using knowledge "of the particular circumstances of time and place", which exists only dispersed and cannot be put into statistics for a central authority. Decisions that depend on it must be left to the "man on the spot", and the price system tells him the relative scarcities he needs without the causes behind them. An argument from examples and from the logic of choice, with no model or evidence. | Read |
| [NOTE-1037](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1037.md) | Rubenstein et al. — Causal consistency of structural equation models | Defines an exact transformation between structural equation models: a map τ on states and a surjective, order-preserving map ω on a declared set of perfect interventions such that pushing each low-level interventional distribution forward by τ gives the high-level model's distribution under the image intervention. It proves that marginalising childless or never-intervened variables, averaging linear micro-variables when every column of the coupling matrix has the same sum, and taking the equilibrium of a contracting linear process with constant noise are each exact, and stresses that each is exact only for the intervention set declared. | Read |
| [NOTE-1038](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1038.md) | Weatherall, O'Connor and Bruner — How to beat science and influence people | In Bala–Goyal network models with Bayesian policy makers who do not gather evidence, a propagandist who forwards only the real results of unbiased scientists that happen to favour the worse action, or who runs honest studies and publishes only the unfavourable ones, can leave policy makers near-certain of the false theory while the scientists converge on the true one. It works best when the problem is hard, studies are small, scientists are many and policy makers hear few of them. A journalist who reports one result for each side every round slows policy makers' learning and never helps it. | Read |
| [NOTE-1039](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1039.md) | Szeidl and Szucs — Media capture through favor exchange | In Hungary, 1994–2016, state-owned firms' advertising, unlike private firms', shifted sharply toward outlets at five events that made them connected to the right-wing government and away at the event that cut the connection, and corruption coverage moved the other way at the three events with content data. A structural model whose slant gap between a connected and an unconnected outlet splits into owner ideology plus a favor-exchange term attributes the coverage drop to both, under identifying assumptions the authors call strong for print and weaker for online. | Read |
| [NOTE-1040](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1040.md) | Di Tella and Franceschelli — Government advertising and media coverage of corruption scandals | In the four main Argentine national newspapers, April 1998–December 2007, months in which a newspaper received more government advertising were months in which it gave less front-page space to the federal government's corruption scandals, within newspaper and month and within each newspaper-president pair: in this version, 0.31 of a front page per month per standard deviation of advertising. The association holds for advertising placed by the central agency Télam and not for autonomous agencies, and not for scandals of non-political actors. The design shows an association; the authors read it as consistent with coverage traded for transfers. | Read |
| [NOTE-1041](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1041.md) | James, Hynes, Whelan, Dreher and Humphry — From access and transparency to refusal | A conceptual paper with illustrations, no data of its own. It sorts responses to algorithmic governance into access and inclusion, transparency, and refusal. It argues that the first two rest on traditional public-administration values, and so reproduce the structures they mean to correct. Both are "bidirectional": inclusion gives the powerful access to the included, and transparency can be demanded of the governed. Refusal, collective and generative rather than individual exit, is the response it favours, with its limits for those who depend on the state. | Read |
| [NOTE-1042](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1042.md) | Collins — Learning from the outsider within | Black women intellectuals in sociology are outsiders within: trained into its paradigms but rooted in experience those paradigms omit or distort. From that position they see two kinds of anomaly, omission and distortion, which outsiders lack the professional authority to press and insiders are not placed to see, having produced them. The essay argues this from the content of Black feminist thought, with no study of who detects what; it proposes institutionalizing the tension rather than resolving it. | Read |
| [NOTE-1043](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1043.md) | OECD — Preventing policy capture | An institutional report, not research. It defines policy capture as "the process of consistently or repeatedly directing public policy decisions away from the public interest towards the interests of a specific interest group or person", by legal or illegal means, and adds three criteria adapted from Carpenter and Moss: an explicit policy goal, a captor's intent to extract rents, and a shift of the process from that goal. It maps the vehicles (including supplying research and manipulated information) and risk factors, and recommends four strategies: stakeholder engagement, transparency, independent oversight bodies, and organisational integrity. | Read |
| [NOTE-1044](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1044.md) | Perdomo, Zrnic, Mendler-Dünner and Hardt — Performative prediction | When a deployed model's predictions change the distribution they are scored on, D(θ), two solution concepts separate: a performative optimum minimizes the risk on the distribution it induces, and a performatively stable point is optimal for the distribution it induces, a fixed point of retraining. With a β-jointly smooth, γ-strongly convex loss and a map D(·) that is ε-Lipschitz in Wasserstein-1, retraining contracts at rate εβ/γ and converges to a unique stable point when ε < γ/β, and removing any one condition can break convergence. Stable points and optima are within 2L_zε/γ of each other, and can differ. | Read |
| [NOTE-1045](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1045.md) | Beckers, Eberhardt and Halpern — Approximate causal abstraction | Turns τ-abstraction into a graded relation. Given a metric on high-level states, the distance of a high-level model from a low-level one is the worst case, over allowed interventions and contexts, of how far the coarse-grained low-level outcome is from the high-level outcome, for the best context map; zero is exact abstraction. Probabilistic versions average over contexts and, with an intervention distribution, over the low-level ways of implementing each high-level intervention. An abstraction followed by an approximation is an approximate abstraction, the reverse order costs a distortion factor, and an approximate abstraction need not decompose into the two. | Read |
| [NOTE-1046](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1046.md) | McCombs and Shaw — The agenda-setting function of mass media | Among 100 Chapel Hill voters not yet committed to a candidate in September–October 1968, the aggregate emphasis they gave the campaign's issues correlated +.967 (major items) and +.979 (minor items) with the composite emphasis of the nine news media serving them, and voters who leaned to a candidate agreed more with all the news than with news about their own side in 18 of 24 comparisons. The authors read this as agenda-setting rather than selective perception, and say the correlations do not prove it. | Read |
| [NOTE-1047](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1047.md) | Barnehl and Schumacher — Media capture, captured | Proposes measuring media capture outlet by outlet, at monthly or weekly resolution, by placing each nominally independent outlet between two poles, regime-owned outlets and opposition outlets the regime cannot coerce, on topic prevalence (a structural topic model, on topics chosen as relevant to the regime's legitimacy) and on the tone of sentences mentioning the leader. Applied to Nicaragua, 2018–2022, it shows Canal 14 moving toward the regime pole in agenda and tone while Radio Corporación stayed near the opposition. The scores measure alignment; that the alignment was coerced is argued from context, not measured. | Read |
| [NOTE-1048](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1048.md) | Xu, Zhao, Song, Stewart and Ermon — A theory of usable information under computational constraints | Defines predictive V-information, I_V(X → Y) = H_V(Y \| ∅) − H_V(Y \| X), where each V-entropy is the least expected log loss a predictor in the family V can reach. With V unrestricted it is Shannon mutual information; with linear-Gaussian V it is R² times the variance. It is non-negative and zero under independence because V must be able to ignore its input. Unlike Shannon information it can be asymmetric and can be raised by computing on X, and its empirical estimate is within 4R(G_V) + 2B√(2 log(1/δ)/N) of the truth with probability 1 − 2δ. It is not bounded by Shannon information unless V's input-free predictions can match the marginal of Y. | Read |
| [NOTE-1049](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1049.md) | Kay, Kasirzadeh and Mohamed — Epistemic injustice in generative AI | A conceptual taxonomy, illustrated with reported cases, of four ways generative models can take part in epistemic injustice: amplified and manipulative testimonial injustice, hermeneutical ignorance and access injustice. Its sharpest move is to relocate the testimonial wrong: in the algorithmic setting it "requires a credibility excess assigned to the algorithm". It counts deliberate fabrication as testimonial injustice, which Fricker's account sets apart, and stretches hermeneutical injustice to unequal access to information. Nothing in it is measured by the authors. | Read |
| [NOTE-1050](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1050.md) | Espeland and Sauder — Rankings and reactivity | An interview study of US law schools (136 open-ended interviews with administrators and faculty, with corroborating data) proposing that public measures are reactive through two mechanisms: self-fulfilling prophecy, by which reactions to a measure confirm its expectations or raise its validity by making the measured conform to it, and commensuration, which simplifies, decontextualizes and ranks. The effects it sorts are reallocation of resources, redefinition of work, and gaming. A framework offered as "an orienting heuristic", not a general theory, and not a measurement of effect sizes. | Read |
| [NOTE-1051](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1051.md) | Short, Hill and Brown — What is ideological capture and how do we measure it | Defines ideological capture: regulators adopt standards, based on an ideologically motivated expert view of the public interest, that consistently marginalize important public values, with no lobbying needed. Measures it for US antitrust's consumer welfare standard. In a conjoint survey the public weighs layoffs, quality and lobbying far above price cuts, the standard's objective, and antitrust lawyers support replacing it 42.6 points less than the public, against a 5.9-point partisan gap. The verdict of capture also leans on historical secondary work. | Read |
| [NOTE-1052](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1052.md) | Arthur — Competing technologies and historical small events (working paper) | In a model where two types of agent arrive in random order and each adopts whichever of two technologies pays it more, with returns linear in the number of previous adopters, increasing returns make the difference in adoptions a random walk with absorbing barriers: one technology takes the market with probability one, which one is decided by the order of arrivals, it need not be the better one, and marginal subsidies cannot move it once it has locked in. Under diminishing returns the barriers reflect and the market shares predictably. | Read |
| [NOTE-1053](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1053.md) | Schram and Ule — Regulatory independence may limit electoral holdup but entrench capture | In a laboratory game of one infrastructure operator, two policymakers and three voters (59 groups), letting the first elected policymaker fix the price for all nine periods, the paper's "regulatory independence", moved prices toward the efficient level when policymakers' payoffs were aligned with consumers', and raised prices further above it when they were aligned with the operator, "capture entrenchment". Voters' pressure under flexible regulation lowered prices under capture but did not remove the effect. | Read |
| [NOTE-1054](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1054.md) v2 | Negro — Three arguments against metaphysical structuralism | Separates methodological, epistemological and metaphysical structuralism about consciousness, and three senses of "consciousness is structural": having an internal structure, being in a structure, and being the structure. Against the third, which metaphysical structuralism needs, it gives three arguments: Relational Mary, the novel experience argument and the lonely experience argument. Each is valid and rests on an intuition or a conceivability premise. It concludes that methodological and epistemological structuralism need only the first two senses and survive. | Read |
| [NOTE-1055](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1055.md) | Aldé — Two geometrical arguments against similarity structuralism | Defines similarity structuralism (phenomenal character is fully fixed by similarity relations, so by the geometry of a similarity space) and argues it cannot account for two accepted facts about colour experience: that exactly four hues are experienced as unmixed and all others as mixtures of two of them, and that the black–white axis is a single gradient while the axes through grey are opposing pairs. Neither fact, it argues, corresponds to any adequate geometric feature of CIELAB or its refinements. It answers the replies from incomplete colour spaces and from unreliable introspection, and concludes structuralism should be rejected for colour. | Read |
| [NOTE-1056](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1056.md) | Gładziejewski — Real patterns, the predictive mind, and the manifest image | A philosophy paper with no data. It traces Dennett's compression criterion for real patterns through minimum description length and Bayesian inference to variational free energy, so that learning a generative model is extracting real patterns from sensory data. It concludes that the manifest image is a structural description of sensory data, veridical even in a matched vat. The self-model compresses self-generated regularities by positing one common cause, so selves are real as patterns and unreal as substances, and which verdict to give is a dispute over criteria, not facts. It says nothing about consciousness or illusion. | Read |
| [NOTE-1057](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1057.md) | Safron, Klimaj & Sheikhbahaee — IWMT and the Human Consciousness Hypothesis | A seven-page symposium paper that restates Integrated World Modeling Theory and says it agrees with the Human Consciousness Hypothesis of the California Institute for Machine Consciousness. On IWMT, phenomenal consciousness is what it is like to be the coherent functioning of an embodied agent's generative world model, run either coupled to sense data (perception) or decoupled from it (imagination). Embodied grounding is required: integrated information or a global workspace without it does not suffice. Transformer language models are said to lack the recurrence, closure and embodiment needed. No new argument or data. | Read |
| [NOTE-1058](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1058.md) | Chandia-Jorquera et al. — Neurophenomenological signatures of pure awareness in Transcendental Meditation | Thirty-three experienced Transcendental Meditation practitioners and 33 age- and sex-matched controls who counted instead. Drawn retrospectively, the practitioners' traces of "pure awareness" were higher and more variable than the controls' (d = 0.77 and 1.32). A random-forest classifier separated meditation from counting at 65% balanced accuracy, chiefly on permutation entropy and aperiodic EEG, and meditation from the practitioners' own rest at 88%, chiefly on low-frequency phase coherence. No EEG feature was shown to track the reports. | Read |
| [NOTE-1059](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1059.md) | Lee-Youngzie et al. — Towards a mathematical structure of global phenomenal consciousness | A hypothesis article with no data. It maps the parts of an experience, ordered by subsumption into a finite topology, to similarity-judgement matrices of their qualia by a presheaf, and reads compatibility of narrow qualia on overlaps as the condition for phenomenal binding, and the presheaf's being a sheaf as the broad quale's being determined by its parts. It reads a sheaf failure as disunity in binocular rivalry and as context dependence in the Ebbinghaus illusion, and gives no rule for telling the two apart. Its worked topology example is malformed, and by its own definitions disagreement on an overlap is not a sheaf failure. | Read |
| [NOTE-1060](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1060.md) v2 | Lyre — Neurophenomenal structuralism | A programmatic paper. Its two assumptions: any phenomenal experience is fully individuated, in its specificity, by its place in a quality space (Q-structure), and Q-structure is mirrored in neural structure by a surjective homomorphism from neural maps. From these, with metaphysically necessary supervenience assumed and not argued for, it draws reductive physicalism, an instrumentalist structural representationalism, holism about experience, and the denial that spectrum inversion is nomologically possible. It addresses specific, not generic, consciousness, and says it is not a structural realism. No new data. | Read |
| [NOTE-1061](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1061.md) | Bo et al. — Deconstructing the brain bases of emotion regulation | Two fMRI samples (n = 182 and 176) looked at, or reappraised, aversive pictures. Bayes factors for and against each of two contrasts sort voxels into four systems: regions engaged only by reappraisal (anterior prefrontal, temporo-parietal, cerebellar), regions engaged by both negative emotion and reappraisal (most of the reappraisal network), regions engaged by negative pictures and unchanged by reappraisal (all subcortical ones, amygdala and PAG included, with much of cortex), and posterior cortical regions reduced by it. Reported negative affect fell under reappraisal (d = 0.92). Activity is measured; experience is reported once per trial. | Read |
| [NOTE-1062](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1062.md) | Whyte et al. — On the minimal theory of consciousness implicit in active inference | A review of active inference simulations of conscious content, self and state, which argues that they share a three-part "hard core": the imperative to minimise variational and expected free energy; conscious contents as the inferred hidden states of world, body or brain; and conscious access at the interface where continuous sensory beliefs become discrete beliefs that can inform counterfactual policy selection. The third part is an inference to the best explanation, and it is a criterion for which contents are conscious in humans, not for which systems have experience. Two close-to-core predictions are named. New in the paper: a re-run rivalry model that fits Levelt's laws, a predicted reward violation of them, and a sleep model that loses its P3b-like response. | Read |
| [NOTE-1063](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1063.md) v2 | Laukkonen, Friston & Chandaria — A beautiful loop | A conceptual theory that consciousness needs three things in an active-inference system: a unified generative model of the world (an epistemic field); competition to enter it that coherent, precise inferences win (Bayesian binding); and epistemic depth, the recursive sharing of that model back through the hierarchy, formalised as a hyper-model that predicts precision at every level. Awareness is graded by epistemic depth, not by content. It is applied to attention, sleep and lucidity, meditation, cessation and psychedelics, and to AI. There are no data and no simulations, and the formal part is a standard hierarchical model with layer-wise precision hyperparameters. | Read |
| [NOTE-1064](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1064.md) | Luppi — Convergent controllers of information integration and its anaesthetic breakdown | Pairwise integrated information ΦR, computed from resting-state fMRI by integrated information decomposition, falls under anaesthesia in humans (sevoflurane), macaques, marmosets and mice, with one mouse regimen the exception, and returns on recovery: spontaneously in humans, and under central thalamic stimulation in two macaques. Network control energy rises with it. Regional loss follows cortical PVALB expression in three species, and species-specific models reproduce both the PVALB effect and the advantage of central over ventrolateral thalamic stimulation. The state measured is behavioural responsiveness, which the authors call "presumably consciousness". | Read |
| [NOTE-1065](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1065.md) | Ward — What is enactivism? | A conceptual paper. The usual taxonomy, which lumps every view stressing sensorimotor loops as "enactivism" and splits it into autopoietic, sensorimotor and radical variants, hides what is distinctive about The Embodied Mind. A second axis, organicist against informationalist, runs across the cognitivist–embodied one. Enactivism is organicist, and it adds the primacy of lived experience and a reciprocity in which scientific vocabularies reshape the experience they describe. Most embodied views, predictive processing among them, are informationalist. It argues for a taxonomy, not for enactivism's truth. | Read |
| [NOTE-1066](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1066.md) | Carruthers & Gennaro — Higher-Order Theories of Consciousness (SEP) | A survey of the theories that make a mental state conscious by its being the object of a higher-order representation: inner sense, actualist and dispositionalist higher-order thought, and self-representational and hybrid views. It sets out the objections (targetless states, the rock, animals, sufficiency) and the prefrontal evidence, and concludes no verdict. Since 2020 it is maintained by Gennaro, a higher-order theorist. Carruthers and Lycan, two of the theories' main sources, are reported to have given them up. | Read |
| [NOTE-1067](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1067.md) | Barrett et al. — The theory of constructed emotion: more than a feeling | A reply by the theory's architects to van Heijst et al., who gave basic emotion theory the emotion (a bioregulatory state) and constructed emotion the feeling (its representation). The reply says the split is a premise of basic emotion theory, not a division of labour: on constructed emotion the same allostatic signals that regulate the body make feeling, and an instance of emotion is one whole-brain event. It adds evidence lists for structured variation, an evolutionary frame from the extended synthesis, and the thesis that the two theories are incommensurable. No data. | Read |
| [NOTE-1068](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1068.md) | Lycan — Representational Theories of Consciousness (SEP) | A survey by one of its protagonists. Strong representationalism holds that a sensory quality, such as the green of an after-image, is a represented property of a represented, possibly nonactual object, and that representation of a certain functionally specified kind suffices for it. "What it's like" to experience the quality is kept apart as a further, higher-order property that needs awareness, and the theory addresses only the quality. The entry sets out the arguments for and the counterexamples against, and leaves wide against narrow content unsettled. | Read |
| [NOTE-1069](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1069.md) | Gurnee — Verbalizable representations form a global workspace in language models | A corpus-averaged Jacobian lens picks out, in each layer of Claude models, the directions a model is disposed to verbalize. Swaps, injections and ablations along these directions (the J-space) show them privileged for report, held concepts, two-hop reasoning and reuse of an argument by many functions, while continuation, anomaly detection and line wrapping use the same information without them. The J-space works in a middle band of layers, carries under 10% of activation variance, and is amplified and relayed by the weights more than other directions. Ablating it flattens experiential language about the self and about others. The authors take no position on phenomenal consciousness. | Read |
| [NOTE-1070](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1070.md) | Woods, Windt & Carter — Contentless experiences in meditation are neither truly contentless nor identical | An evidence synthesis of 135 expert texts on the goal-states of Shamatha (Wallace), Transcendental Meditation and Stillness Meditation. It codes 65 features. The states are said to lack thoughts, concepts, perceptions, images and memories, but to keep wakefulness, calm, stillness, bliss, knowing, freedom, unity and more. They are the same across the practices on 14 features, different on 4 (chiefly Shamatha's far greater attentional stability and vividness) and unclear on 47. So, on the texts, they are neither truly contentless nor identical. The data are teachers' descriptions, not participants' reports. | Read |
| [NOTE-1071](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1071.md) | Graziano — Illusionism big and small | An essay with no new data. Claims of consciousness come from an automatic internal model, and since every brain model is schematic, what people report having is a caricature of whatever the model tracks. Six hypotheses for what that is are offered. The author favours attention, or more deeply "the deep selective processing of information", depicted by an attention schema as an intangible essence. Theories that say how a brain produces a feeling and not how the feeling gets into the model that drives report ("Arrow B") are called magic. Its "small" illusionism still denies the phenomenal essence. What it keeps real is the process modelled. | Read |
| [NOTE-1073](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1073.md) | Jensen Hughes — Post-incident analysis of the Brookhollow Apartment fire | An independent review, commissioned by Sedgwick County and Wichita, of every public-safety agency's response to the fire of 13 October 2023 that killed Paoly Bedeski. It found "no single point of failure" but "systemic shortcomings that, when combined, contributed to an unorganized rescue effort": a dispatcher who did not replay her unit number, an 18-minute delay in the second alarm, no effective command, freelancing, search not resumed for over eleven minutes after a mayday that was under control within minutes, and Wichita Fire Department policies that existed and were not followed. It could not conclude the shortcomings changed the outcome. | Read |
| [NOTE-1074](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1074.md) | Wacquant — A concise genealogy and anatomy of habitus | A short essay that takes habitus back to Aristotle's hexis and to Bourdieu's first use of it, for the misfit between dispositions and a changing world in Béarn and Algeria, and clears four misreadings: habitus is multilayered and revised in practice, not the replica of one structure; it need not be coherent; it suits crisis and change as well as reproduction; and it never generates action by itself, but only as triggered by positions in a social world. A conceptual clarification, not a finding; its empirical warrant is cited. | Read |
| [NOTE-1075](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1075.md) | Swidler — Culture in action | Culture does not cause action by supplying the values that set its ends. It supplies a repertoire of skills, habits and styles from which people build strategies of action, which outlast the ends they serve. In settled periods culture constrains through the cost of retooling and loosely coupled beliefs; in unsettled periods explicit ideologies govern action directly, but structural opportunities decide which survive. A theoretical argument with illustrative cases and no data of its own. | Read |
| [NOTE-1076](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1076.md) | Pierson — Increasing returns, path dependence and the study of politics (working paper) | An argument, not a test: the conditions Arthur and North found to produce increasing returns (set-up costs, learning, coordination, adaptive expectations) are more common in politics than in markets, because politics is dense with compulsory institutions, rests on collective action and is opaque; and lock-in is more intense there, because competition and learning correct weakly, politicians' horizons are short and institutions are built to be hard to change. Its one case is the failure of two opposite US health-care reforms in 1993–96. | Read |
| [NOTE-1078](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1078.md) | Sewell — A theory of structure | A reformulation of Giddens's duality of structure. Structures are sets of virtual schemas and actual resources that sustain each other: resources enact schemas and schemas are validated by the resources their enactment yields. Change comes from inside, because structures are multiple and intersect, schemas transpose to new cases, resources are polysemic and accumulate unpredictably. Agency is the capacity to transpose schemas and remobilize resources. A conceptual argument, with a conjecture that depth, more than power, makes a structure durable. | Read |
| [NOTE-1079](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1079.md) | McFadyen et al. — Doorways do not always cause forgetting | Four conceptual replications from an independent lab. In passive, head-mounted virtual reality, doorways did not lower hits for carried or set-down objects; under a counting load they raised false alarms to recombined probes. Watching or walking a curtained hallway did not change memory for a 16-item grid. The nulls are informative but not direct failures to replicate: movement was passive, and Experiments 3 and 4 used a different memory task. | Read |
| [NOTE-1081](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1081.md) | Pettijohn & Radvansky — Doorways: event structure or updating disruption? | Two virtual-navigation experiments from the originating lab. Travel time was not longer through doorways, and a 3-second pause before the probe left the effect as it was, so neither a longer retention interval nor a passing cost of updating explains it. In both, the effect was confined to the carried object. The authors take this as support for interference between the two event models that hold that object. | Read |
| [NOTE-1082](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1082.md) | Radvansky et al. — Walking through doorways causes forgetting: further explorations | Three experiments. The doorway effect appeared with small monitors and in real rooms carrying a box of six objects, and returning to the room where the objects were picked up did not help: memory followed the number of rooms involved, worst after two new rooms. The authors attribute it to retrieval interference between event models that both contain the probed object, not to the loss of an encoding context. | Read |
| [NOTE-1083](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1083.md) | Radvansky & Copeland — Walking through doorways causes forgetting | Two desktop virtual-reality experiments. With distance held equal, walking through a doorway rather than across a large room raised errors and slowed responses to a probe for the object being carried; memory for the object just set down was not affected. The authors read it as situation-model updating at a spatial shift. The effect rests on few no-shift trials (5 per condition), and the shift and no-shift rooms differed in size and wall pattern. | Read |
| [NOTE-1084](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1084.md) | Zacks et al. — Event perception: a mind-brain perspective | States event segmentation theory: perception continuously predicts what comes next; a transient rise in prediction error opens a gate that resets working-memory event models and lets sensory input in, and that moment is perceived as an event boundary. Supported by unitization, memory, narrative and imaging studies, mostly correlational and largely from the authors' groups. Its one acknowledged misfit: the anterior cingulate does not respond at boundaries during passive viewing. It is about watching events, not one's own intentions, and does not mention doorways. | Read |
| [NOTE-1085](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1085.md) | Lerman, Yan & Wu — The majority illusion in social networks | A sampling fact about networks, not a finding about people: when an attribute is correlated with degree, the share of nodes that see it in a majority of their neighbours can far exceed its global share (60–80% of nodes when 5% hold it, in a heavy-tailed synthetic network), and more so in disassortative networks. A binomial model from the joint degree distribution predicts the share. No person's belief or behaviour is measured, and the attributes on the real networks are assigned, not observed. | Read |
| [NOTE-1086](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1086.md) | NTSB — United Airlines Flight 173, Portland, 1978 | The NTSB found that United 173 ran out of fuel after holding about an hour near Portland while its crew dealt with a landing-gear problem, that fuel exhaustion "was predictable", and that the probable cause was the captain's failure to monitor the fuel state and respond to the crew's advisories. The other two crew members either did not grasp the criticality or did not communicate it; no one was assigned to watch the fuel. It recommended indoctrination in "flightdeck resource management", with "participative management for captains and assertiveness training for other cockpit crewmembers". | Read |
| [NOTE-1087](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1087.md) | Helmreich, Merritt & Wilhelm — The evolution of Crew Resource Management training | A short history and argument. CRM began with a 1979 NASA workshop and United's 1981 program, and passed through five "generations", from managerial-style seminars to integration with technical training under the FAA's AQP. Its effects are hard to validate (accident rates cannot be used), acceptance of its concepts decays over time even with recurrent training, and it exported poorly across cultures. The authors propose error management (avoid, trap, mitigate) as a rationale all pilots can accept. Command is mentioned only in passing. | Read |
| [NOTE-1088](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1088.md) | GAO — NASA: better mechanisms needed for sharing lessons learned | A 2001 survey of NASA's 192 program and project managers (115 usable responses, 60 percent) found that NASA's policies required lessons to be reviewed and submitted, but managers did not routinely identify, collect or share them, its Lessons Learned Information System was little used, and NASA recorded how often the system was searched but not whether any lesson was applied, so "NASA has no assurance that lessons are being applied". The occasion was the 1999 Mars failures, not Challenger. | Read |
| [NOTE-1089](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1089.md) | Acharya, Blackwell & Sen — The political legacy of American slavery | Among Southern whites today, those in counties where a larger share of the 1860 population was enslaved are more Republican, more opposed to affirmative action, more racially resentful and colder toward blacks; the association survives 1860 controls and a cotton-suitability instrument, and is not accounted for by today's black share, by 1935–40 migration or by income inequality. The divergence in voting appears after Reconstruction, not before the war, and is smaller where agriculture mechanized early, which the authors read as a post-emancipation amplification of attitudes then passed down locally. | Read |
| [NOTE-1091](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1091.md) | Aevyra — The Ledger of Will | A careful, self-limiting formal note on what a reduced memory must keep so that an agent can still revise: a retained state supports a declared family of future questions, interventions and changes of evaluative law exactly when those targets are constant on its fibres, and under repeated revision exactly when its fibres lie in the coarsest revision-invariant refinement (Moore–Nerode). The rest is design proposal and an unexecuted experimental protocol. Elementary and correct; the authors say plainly that it synthesizes established ideas. | Read |
| [NOTE-1092](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1092.md) | Penglase — The unspoken whiteness of Brazilian jiu-jitsu | An anthropologist's argument, from secondary histories, Gracie family sources and a little ethnography, that the Gracies' challenge matches against luta livre placed their jiu-jitsu in Brazil's racial hierarchy as white, mostly through class, neighbourhood and employment rather than in words. Along the way it documents that the Gracies fought over the rules as well as under them, and that jiu-jitsu prospered while luta livre, poorer and darker, went underground; it then absorbed luta livre's no-gi style until only the social difference remained. | Read |
| [NOTE-1093](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1093.md) | Bigand et al. — The geometry of interpersonal synchrony in human dance | In 35 dyads of untrained dancers facing each other, shared music and visual contact were varied independently. Each raised interpersonal synchrony, in different principal movements and with no interaction: lateral and hand movements synchronized through seeing the partner, anteroposterior movements such as head bobs through the shared music, and vertical bounce through both. Which factor drove a movement's synchrony could be read from its spatial direction (100% classification) and not from its periodicity. The direction of coupling between partners was not estimated. | Read |
| [NOTE-1094](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1094.md) | Psychopathy as a Clinical and Empirical Construct | The PCL-R's items form four correlated factors, Interpersonal, Affective, Lifestyle and Antisocial, which pair into Factors 1 and 2 and are explained by one superordinate factor. Psychopathy is dimensional, its antisocial features belong to it as much as its affective ones, and the authors deny that any one component is its essence. Cleckley's 1941/1976 profile is a clinical synopsis from an unrepresentative sample, not the standard the measure should be judged by. | Read |
| [NOTE-1095](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1095.md) | Sales Practices Investigation Report | The board's own investigation finds that the harm came from the sales model and the performance management that enforced it, kept in place by a decentralized structure and a culture of deference, with control functions that handled cases one by one and a board told too little. It names and sanctions individual leaders as well. It also records that leadership blamed individual employees, and that signals of the harm reached people who could not act on them, or were filtered before they reached those who could. | Read |
| [NOTE-1096](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1096.md) | Flayelle et al. — A taxonomy of technology design features that promote potentially addictive online behaviours | A narrative review and a taxonomy. Design features of six kinds of online service are linked, mostly by cross-sectional, qualitative or indirect evidence, to loss of control. They are sorted by the learning and control process each exploits. Model-free: reinforcement schedules and personalized triggers. Model-based: overvaluation, interference with deliberation, partial goal fulfilment, cognitive biases. Providers select features by their effect on use and revenue, and personalize them under informational asymmetry. For the record it maps closely onto the parts of the potential account: features that strengthen a cue-keyed ranking, move its reference course, falsify the user's reading of progress, or pre-empt the other perspectives. | Read |
| [NOTE-1097](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1097.md) | Induction and Profiling of Strong Multi-Componential Emotions in Virtual Reality | Virtual reality induces intense emotions that engage several components, which passive paradigms do not, and the authors argue this is a precondition for testing synchronization. Seven games, 53 participants, one retrospective questionnaire per game. Fear and joy clusters span appraisal, motivation, physiology, feeling and regulation, and appraisal predicts their intensity best. Componentiality is a property of associations across observations. Nothing is measured within an episode. | Read |
| [NOTE-1098](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1098.md) | Toward an integrative psychometric model of emotions | An integrative psychometric model of emotions must allow distinct emotions, variation between and within persons, and causal relations among components, one property from each broad class of emotion theory. Reflective and formative latent-variable models fail. A network model passes. In it, the network of causally interacting components constitutes the emotion, and a distinct emotion is a weakly emergent small-world community. Strong connectivity predicts self-sustaining activation and hysteresis, hence longer emotions. A programme paper: no data, and limits named candidly. | Read |
| [NOTE-1099](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1099.md) | Statistical ranking and combinatorial Hodge theory | Rank aggregation as combinatorial Hodge theory. Aggregated pairwise comparisons form an edge flow, and its orthogonal decomposition gives a least-squares global ranking (the gradient), local inconsistency (curl) and global inconsistency (harmonic). The size of the cyclic residual certifies whether any global ranking is meaningful. The framework is cardinal, generalizes Borda, and is not Kemeny. | Read |
| [NOTE-1100](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1100.md) | EMA: A process model of appraisal dynamics | A computational process model of appraisal after Smith and Lazarus. Appraisal is a single, fast, parallel mapping from the agent's causal interpretation (its beliefs, desires, intentions, plans, probabilities and utilities) to per-proposition appraisal frames. Emotional dynamics come from the time course of the perception, inference and action that change the interpretation. Frames compete for the coping response, and the most recently accessed one with the highest mood-adjusted intensity wins. Coping alters the world or the agent's mental state, which drives reappraisal. Illustrated by an actor's 2.6-second reaction to a pigeon. | Read |
| [NOTE-1101](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1101.md) | The current status of research on the structure of evaluative space | The evaluative space model restated by its authors. Positivity and negativity are separable systems whose combined output is a bipolar approach–avoid predisposition. They can be activated reciprocally, independently or together. Coactivation is ambivalence, which is rare, arousing and behaviourally indeterminate, and gives the same net output as neutrality. Negativity has the higher gain and positivity the higher intercept, and both recalibrate with context. Evaluation is heterarchical, with higher levels able to override lower. | Read |
| [NOTE-1102](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1102.md) | Control Theory, Goal Attainment, and Psychopathology | A commentary. Control theory adds to goal talk the need to perceive the present state and compare it with the goal. Psychopathology arises where the loop's input, reference value, comparison or output is extreme or biased. The five factors are sensitivities to classes of goals. Valence tracks the velocity of goal attainment against a reference value, so approach and avoidance can each produce either sign. Confidence, doubt and disengagement lie outside the loop, in expectancy-value theory. | Read |
| [NOTE-1103](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1103.md) | An Appraisal-Driven Componential Approach to the Emotional Brain | A programme for taking the component process model into the brain: five functionally defined networks, appraisal driving changes and synchronization in the other four, synchronization proposed to be neuronal phase or cross-frequency coupling, and feeling emerging when the degree of synchronization passes a threshold. It states that some action tendencies take priority by control precedence. It gives no measure of synchronization, signed or unsigned, per episode or otherwise. | Read |
| [NOTE-1104](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1104.md) | Interaction and threshold effects of appraisal on componential patterns of emotion: A study using cross-cultural semantic data | From the GRID data on the meaning of 24 emotion words in 27 countries, MARS models of 11 motivation, physiology and expression factors on 7 appraisal factors select interactions up to third order and some hinges. Goal compatibility is the main effect, agency and norm compatibility act only through it, and the structure is partly additive and partly hierarchical. The "threshold effects" are hinges in a continuous piecewise-linear fit. No synchronization measure, no time, and no choice data. | Read |
| [NOTE-1105](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1105.md) | Kahneman, Wakker and Sarin — Back to Bentham? Explorations of experienced utility | Decision utility, an outcome's weight in choice, and experienced utility, its hedonic quality, are distinct and can be measured separately. Experienced utility is instant (real-time report) or remembered (retrospective). Remembered utility follows a Peak-End rule with duration neglect, and choices follow remembered utility, so people choose dominated painful episodes. Total utility is axiomatized as a time integral of ordinal instant utility with a neutral zero. For the record, the dissociation is not a counterexample to potential read within the moment. It shows that potential read from deferred choices measures memory, and that a system's model of its own past states is systematically biased. | Read |
| [NOTE-1106](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1106.md) | The Emotion Process: Event Appraisal and Component Differentiation | The evidence for the emotion process, organised by appraisal criterion and by the component appraisal drives. Appraisal criteria predict action tendencies, physiology and expression better than emotion categories do. Intrinsic valence and goal congruence have partly different signatures and combine multiplicatively. Control amplifies goal-congruence effects. Coherence among components is proposed as the mark of an episode at one threshold and of awareness at a second. No negotiation among perspectives: appraisal is a profile of criteria that drives patterned responses. | Read |
| [NOTE-1107](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1107.md) | Brain networks subserving functional core processes of emotions identified with componential modeling | fMRI during 40 films, with each of 119 short events rated on 32 CoreGRID features. PLSC gives six brain–behaviour processes: valuation, novelty, hedonic impact, goal monitoring, caring for others and approach/avoidance. Valence splits into a wanting-like valuation network carrying the action tendencies and a liking-like hedonic network carrying feeling and expression, and no arousal process appears. There is no synchronization measure, but every event gets a signed score on each process. | Read |
| [NOTE-1108](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1108.md) | Levels of valence | A framework, not a study. Valence is located at two levels. Micro-valences are the outcomes of separate valenced appraisal checks, and they can conflict. Macro-valence is a one-dimensional integration of them and of other inputs, and it is what choice needs. The paper's work is in the paths between the levels, and above all in the integration rules, from weighted sums to lexicographic and elimination strategies that need no trade-offs. Intrinsic pleasantness and goal conduciveness are separate checks, and the paper grounds the separation in Berridge. | Read |
| [NOTE-1109](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1109.md) | Berridge and Robinson — Liking, wanting, and the incentive-sensitization theory of addiction | An invited review of the incentive-sensitization theory by its authors. 'Wanting' and 'liking' have dissociable brain systems. Drugs can sensitize the 'wanting' system so that it is lastingly hyper-reactive to drug cues and contexts while 'liking' stays flat or falls. Sensitized 'wanting' can oppose cognitive desire, run without report, and grow in abstinence, and the theory is being extended, on weak evidence, to behavioural addictions. For the record it is a mechanism for proxy-keyed potential in persons. It also shows that the addict case [CLAIM-433](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-433.md) settles holds only if the sign of valence is read along the proxy. | Read |
| [NOTE-1110](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1110.md) | Berridge and Kringelbach — Pleasure systems in the brain | A review. Reward splits into 'liking', 'wanting' and learning. 'Liking' is measured without report by taste reactivity, homologous across species, and is generated by small opioid hotspots. Dopamine and most "pleasure electrodes" raise 'wanting' and leave 'liking' alone, and sensitized 'wanting' can grow while the drug becomes less pleasant. Objective 'liking' can occur without felt pleasure. For the record, this is the sharpest test so far of "valence is potential". Read as written, the identity fails, and the dissociation calls for a hedonic marker measured apart from control. | Read |
| [NOTE-1111](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1111.md) | Hesp et al. — Deeply felt affect: the emergence of valence in deep active inference | A computational proof of principle with no data. Valence is a state of self, inferred at a slower, deeper level from affective charge, the update to the expected precision γ that sets how far the preference- driven action model, rather than habit, governs policy selection. Positive charge is rising confidence in the action model and negative charge falling confidence. The valence level sends priors on γ back down. "Felt" means explicitly represented, which the authors take as necessary, not sufficient, for self-reportable valence. For the record, this is the closest existing model of that felt valence is the system modelling its own potential. But its sign and intensity run against the record's potential account for negative valence, and it inherits the wanting/liking problem. | Read |
| [NOTE-1113](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1113.md) | Emotions are emergent processes: they require a dynamic computational architecture | The component process model restated for computational modellers. Emotion is a bounded episode of synchronization among subsystems (appraisal, autonomic, motor, motivation, feeling), driven by appraisal checks in a fixed order and aimed at control precedence. Feeling monitors the process by representing the other components and their coherence. The degree of synchronization is hypothesised to generate consciousness. Emotions are attractor basins of coupled oscillators, with hysteresis and catastrophe jumps. No operational measure of synchronization is given. | Read |
| [NOTE-1114](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1114.md) | Motivational trade-offs and modulation of nociception in bumblebees | A motivational trade-off in an insect. Bees given heated (55 °C) 40% sucrose feeders against unheated alternatives of 10–40% fed from the heated ones less as the alternatives got sweeter, and more steeply than without heat. Choice ran on learned colour cues, so the modulation is central. The authors take it as consistent with pain, not proof of it. One cost level, four resource levels in separate groups; graded at that cost, silent on a threshold in cost. | Read |
| [NOTE-1115](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1115.md) | Conscious emotional experience emerges as a function of multilevel, appraisal-driven response synchronization | A theoretical paper with a short review of EEG and neural-synchrony evidence. Conscious emotional experience is recruited when lower, automatic levels of appraisal and regulation fail, which happens when component synchronization is strong and lasting. Conscious regulation needs explicit representations. The feeling is a central representation of the components and their coherence, built by local and distant neuronal synchronization. Proposed measures are EEG band activity in felt versus unfelt episodes, and phase coherence between regions. | Read |
| [NOTE-1116](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1116.md) | Flows and Decompositions of Games: Harmonic and Potential Games | A finite game is read as a flow, the unilateral payoff differences on the graph of strategy profiles, and the Helmholtz decomposition of that flow splits the game uniquely into potential, harmonic and nonstrategic parts. Potential games are those with no harmonic part. Harmonic games, the pure-conflict part, generically have no pure equilibrium. The nearest potential game is a closed-form l2 projection. | Read |
| [NOTE-1117](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1117.md) | The power of goal-directed processes in the causation of emotional and other actions | A reversal of the default in dual-process models of action and emotion. Goal-directed processes, which select the action option with the highest expected utility, can be fast and automatic, so they, not stimulus-driven habits or appraisal-to-action-tendency links, are the default cause of action. Most of the competition that decides behaviour is between goal-directed processes, and values and expectancies settle it. Emotional actions are those whose tendencies have control precedence because the goals at stake are highly valued, so emotional episodes are decision processes with higher stakes. | Read |
| [NOTE-1118](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1118.md) | A Multi-Componential Approach to Emotion Recognition and the Effect of Personality | A crowdsourced film-rating study. Thirty-nine CoreGRID items rated after whole clips show emotion structure beyond valence and arousal (six dimensions) and predict discrete-emotion ratings better together than any component alone. Personality traits correlate with componential items. No synchronization, no within-episode measure, no physiology recorded. | Read |
| [NOTE-1119](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1119.md) | Bridging emotion theory and neurobiology through dynamic systems modeling | A dynamic-systems model of appraisal and emotion. Their constituents organize one another through feedback and circular causality into one emotional interpretation (EI): triggered by a perturbation, self-amplifying until it takes over the system, then self-stabilizing as competing cues are resolved. EIs are attractors, one at a time, with abrupt transitions between them. Vertical integration gives them momentum and selects among them. Stable EIs drive learning, so real-time and developmental order are interdependent. Predicts theta-band phase synchrony as an index of emotional relevance. | Read |
| [NOTE-1120](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1120.md) | Brown, Price & Dombrovski — Anxiety as a disorder of uncertainty | A narrative review and theoretical proposal, with no new data and no simulation. Computational learning studies of anxiety (seven, not a systematic search) find altered adjustment of learning rate to kinds of uncertainty, mostly with aversive outcomes, rather than inflated threat learning or valuation. The authors propose that in aversive environments avoidance of uncertain states keeps their uncertainty high and so perpetuates itself, that anxiety amplifies this by misreading noise as change, and that exposure works by reducing the uncertainty, not the threat. It covers fear-based disorders and says it does not explain GAD. | Read |
| [NOTE-1121](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1121.md) | Edwards et al. — Skills homework and phone coaching in a DBT intensive outpatient programme | A chart review of 56 of 88 patients in a Yale DBT intensive outpatient programme, kept because they finished a four-month cycle and gave enough diary-card data. Homework completion in months 1–3 correlated with larger drops in suicide and substance-use urges (r ≈ .35), and phone coaching with a larger drop in self-harm urges (r = .31); neither correlated with change in how often the behaviours occurred. Patients with no target behaviour in month 4 had completed more homework (91% against 80%); the coaching difference was not significant. Correlational, uncorrected for multiple comparisons. | Read |
| [NOTE-1122](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1122.md) | Juhász — Temporary protection and technology adoption (December 2015 draft) | A natural experiment: the Napoleonic blockade raised the effective cost of reaching London much more for northern than for southern departments of the French Empire. Better-protected departments added more mechanized cotton-spinning capacity by 1812, kept and extended that lead through 1887, had more productive spinning firms in 1840 and higher industrial value added per capita in 1860, but not in 1896, 1930 or 2000. The long-run estimates rest on an instrument the author concedes is weak (first-stage F mostly below 10). The protection was a war measure, not a policy; what persisted was the industry's location, not the protection. | Read |
| [NOTE-1123](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1123.md) | De Kleine et al. — Impaired action-safety learning and excessive relief during avoidance | A cross-sectional comparison of 47 healthy controls with 139 treatment-seeking patients (33 OCD, 40 panic disorder with agoraphobia, 66 PTSD) in a picture-based avoidance task. OCD and PTSD patients pressed the avoidance button more to the safety cue and kept a higher expectancy of the aversive picture after effective avoidance; PDA and PTSD patients reported more relief when it was omitted. Relief was already higher before avoidance was available, and patients rated the pictures as more aversive. That low confidence in avoidance makes omissions surprising and the relief reinforces avoidance is the authors' interpretation, not something the study tested. | Read |
| [NOTE-1124](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1124.md) | Gollwitzer & Sheeran — Implementation intentions and goal achievement: a meta-analysis | A meta-analysis of 94 tests (1990–2003, 8,461 participants, mostly students and laboratory tasks) finds that adding an if-then plan to a goal intention raised goal attainment by d = .65 against the goal intention alone, across four problems of goal striving, with large effects on cue accessibility and on the immediacy, efficiency and non-conscious running of the planned response in small sets of tests (k = 1 to 7). Plans are said to delegate control "to specified situational cues" while staying dependent on an active goal. Publication bias was checked only by comparing published with unpublished tests; the 2024 meta-analysis of 642 tests finds it substantial. | Read |
| [NOTE-1125](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1125.md) | Bjørnskov, Voigt & Khesali — Unconstitutional states of emergency (2021 working paper) | 853 national states of emergency, 1949–2017, from Hafner-Burton et al.'s list updated; 115 coded as unlawful from news, NGO reports and durations past the constitutional maximum. 97 of the 115 followed political turmoil, 14 natural disasters. Unlawful ones lasted 321 days on average against 115. Logits find democracies, richer countries and (after domestic events) higher investment prices less likely, and bicameral systems and second-chamber approval more likely, to see an unlawful one. Correlational, with pseudo-R² of 0.01–0.07; "suspected to be unlawful" is the authors' own gloss on the coding. | Read |
| [NOTE-1126](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1126.md) | Friedkin, Jia & Bullo — A theory of the evolution of social power | A Friedkin–Johnsen model of opinion change on each issue, with a reflection mechanism between issues: a member's closure to influence on the next issue equals their influence centrality on the last. In simulation it drives one member to full closure and the rest to full openness. In 30 four-person student groups discussing 15 choice dilemmas, prior centrality predicted next-issue closure, more strongly along the sequence; influence networks thinned and discussions shortened. The rate of consensus did not change. | Read |
| [NOTE-1127](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1127.md) | Chou, Wilson & Smith — The influence of anxiety on exploration | A narrative review of computational modelling studies of anxiety and exploration, almost all in reward tasks and sub-clinical samples. In bandit tasks, directed exploration tends to rise with trait or cognitive anxiety and fall with state or somatic anxiety; random exploration shows no link; in foraging tasks, and in one task with a predator to check for, anxiety goes with less exploration. Results are inconsistent across tasks and measures and none has been replicated. | Read |
| [NOTE-1128](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1128.md) | Goodson et al. — The standalone effect of safety behavior manipulations | A PROSPERO-registered review of 26 studies (2,048 participants, mean age 24.9, 26.6% male) that manipulated safety behaviours outside exposure; 19 entered four meta-analyses. Against control, reducing safety behaviours reduced them (d = 0.52 after one outlier was removed) and reduced symptoms (d = 0.43, k = 16; 0.31 after trim-and-fill, with significant Egger asymmetry). Instructed increases, all in non-treatment experiments, raised safety behaviours (d = 2.96) and symptoms (d = 0.65, five studies). The literature is mostly appearance concerns and social anxiety in young, non-clinical or subclinical samples. | Read |
| [NOTE-1129](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1129.md) | Dagan & Benvenisty — Autocratization and states of emergency (IDI research summary) | A think-tank summary of a comparative study of five democracies chosen because they autocratized (South Korea, India, Hungary, Venezuela and Turkey). In each, it says, emergency powers, extraordinary powers functionally equivalent to them, and emergency rhetoric played "a significant role" in weakening democratic institutions. It states that the convergence of emergency and autocratization "is not inevitable" and that many democracies weather emergencies intact. Narrative country sketches; no method, data or sources are given, and the cases are selected on the outcome. | Read |
| [NOTE-1130](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1130.md) | Gerstner et al. — Eligibility traces and plasticity on behavioral time scales | A review by theoreticians. In a three-factor rule, pre- and postsynaptic co-activation sets a decaying synaptic flag, the eligibility trace, and the weight changes only if a third signal (reward minus expected reward, surprise, novelty, or a neuron-specific error) arrives while it is set. Five experimental papers (2014–2017), mostly in slices, give traces of about 1 s in striatum, 3–10 s in cortex, about 2 s and about a minute in hippocampus. The authors grant that other mechanisms could bridge the same gap. | Read |
| [NOTE-1131](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1131.md) v2 | Sheeran, Listrom & Gollwitzer — The when and how of planning: 642 tests of implementation intentions | A meta-analysis of 642 tests (294 reports to September 2019). Forming implementation intentions improved behaviour (d = .27), cognitive performance (.47), affect regulation (.66) and social judgement (.52), pooled d = .36; publication bias was substantial, and a robust Bayesian estimate is d = .15, small and highly heterogeneous. Contingent if-then plans beat schedule plans (.43 against .29); rehearsing the plan once helped, recording it hurt, and effects were large only when motivation was high. A taxonomy of cues and responses finds nearly every kind effective. | Read |
| [NOTE-1132](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1132.md) | Soma et al. — The hive mind is a single reinforcement learning agent | A short theoretical paper with simulations. In an infinite, well-mixed population, imitation of success has the expected update of Cross Learning, and the weighted voter model of the honey-bee waggle dance that of Maynard-Cross Learning, the Maynard-Smith replicator dynamic. The population's type distribution is the policy of a stateless bandit agent, each member is one parallel sample of it, and no member learns. The authors keep the biology partial and the simulations qualitative. | Read |
| [NOTE-1133](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1133.md) | Ku & Finch — Routines die hard: ontological agency in securitisation | A conceptual paper with an illustration. Alongside the political agency securitisation theory grants its audience (accept, reject, contest), Ku and Finch propose ontological agency: keeping everyday routines going, which often means ignoring securitising moves. Observed by chance in Gangneung in 2022, people paid routine missile launches and beach-front military sites little attention; when a missile malfunctioned at night under a news embargo, tweets voiced fear of war and anger at the government. The authors argue such inaction lets securitisation reproduce itself and that accepting it delegates anxiety management to elites. | Read |
| [NOTE-1134](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1134.md) | Mancinelli & Bach — A systematic review of human avoidance learning | A PRISMA systematic review, not a meta-analysis, of 116 studies of avoidance learning in healthy humans with shock or noise (1939–2024). Avoidance is learned without terminating the CS, transfers by inference to stimuli never paired with harm, and persists when it can be performed, longest when it is most effective; this contradicts two-factor theory and favours expectancy and inference. But some avoidance persists after the US is visibly removed, which a purely inferential account does not predict. No clinical samples were included. | Read |
| [NOTE-1135](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1135.md) | Jia, MirTabatabaei, Friedkin & Bullo — Opinion dynamics and the evolution of social power in influence networks | DeGroot averaging on each issue, and between issues each member's self-weight is set to their share of control over the last consensus. With a fixed, strongly connected matrix of relative interpersonal weights, self-weights converge from every non-autocratic start to a unique equilibrium fixed by the eigenvector centralities: power ranks as centrality, accumulates at the top, is autocratic exactly for a star network and democratic exactly for a doubly stochastic one. Members whom no path reaches end with no power. | Read |
| [NOTE-1136](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1136.md) | Zorowitz, Momennejad & Daw — Anxiety, avoidance, and sequential evaluation | A decision-theoretic argument with simulations, no data. In sequential evaluation the ability to avoid danger later should make it less threatening now. An agent that computes values as if it will fail to avoid later (a β-pessimistic Bellman equation, weight w) spreads negative value to states far from the threat and avoids early, which reproduces qualitatively exaggerated threat appraisal, generalization, earlier cash-out in risk tasks and aversive pruning, and predicts a reduced free-choice premium. The misbelief concerns the agent's own future control, not the danger. | Read |
| [NOTE-1137](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1137.md) v2 | Craske et al. — Maximizing exposure therapy: an inhibitory learning approach | A clinical translation, not a study. It summarizes evidence that extinction leaves the original threat association intact and adds a competing inhibitory one, so fear can return. It argues that exposure should aim to violate expectancies, not to reduce fear within a session, and that fear reduction during exposure does not predict outcome. It sets out strategies for strengthening and retrieving inhibitory learning, with five invented case examples. Cognitive restructuring before or during exposure is held to blunt learning by lowering expectancy. The evidence on safety behaviours is reported as mixed. | Read |
| [NOTE-1138](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1138.md) | Friston et al. — Active inference and learning | A discrete-state active inference scheme in which a habit is one more policy, a state-to-state transition model learned by counting observed transitions, and the prior over policies is learned by counting which policies were pursued. In simulated T-maze foraging the agent first explores, then exploits, then acquires a habit; after the habit is acquired it persists when the reward is devalued, and before it is acquired behaviour switches at once. Simulations only; the authors say the scheme makes probably no new behavioural predictions. | Read |
| [NOTE-1139](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1139.md) | Miller, Resnick and Zeckhauser — Eliciting informative feedback: the peer-prediction method | A mechanism-design paper with proofs and a worked example. A center with no ground truth pays each rater a strictly proper scoring rule applied to the posterior over a reference rater's report implied by her own report. Truth-telling is a strict Nash equilibrium, payments can be scaled to buy effort and balanced among raters, and coarse reports can be elicited for two types. Uninformative equilibria remain, and collusion, risk aversion, unelicited private signals and trust in the center are left as limits. | Read |
| [NOTE-1140](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1140.md) | Kaisers & Tuyls — Frequency adjusted multi-agent Q-learning | A short algorithmic paper with plotted experiments. The selection–mutation model of Boltzmann Q-learning (Tuyls et al. 2003, 2005) assumes every Q-value changes at rate α; in Q-learning only the chosen action's does, so its expected change carries a factor x_i, and Q-learning departs from the model depending on initialization. A frequency-adjusted update removes the factor and matches the model. Three 2×2 games, one temperature, no quantitative measure of fit. | Read |
| [NOTE-1141](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1141.md) | Son et al. — QTRAN: learning to factorize with transformation | Defines Individual-Global-Max (IGM): per-agent values factorise a joint value when the profile of individual argmaxes is the joint argmax. Additivity and monotonicity are sufficient conditions; QTRAN trains the sum of individual values plus a state value to equal the joint value at the greedy profile and bound it elsewhere, which is sufficient and, up to rescaling, necessary. Every single-state matrix game satisfies IGM; VDN and QMIX missed the optimum in 177 of 310 random 3×3 games. | Read |
| [NOTE-1142](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1142.md) | Hart & Mas-Colell — A simple adaptive procedure leading to correlated equilibrium | A theorem with a proof. Regret matching, switching from one's last action to each alternative with probability proportional to the positive regret for not having made that switch in the past, drives the empirical joint distribution of play almost surely to the set of correlated equilibria when every player uses it. Regrets vanish exactly when the empirical distribution approaches that set. A stylized variant is analysed by Blackwell approachability; the main procedure needs inertia and needs players to see one another's past play. | Read |
| [NOTE-1143](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1143.md) | Balduzzi et al. — Open-ended learning in symmetric zero-sum games | A framework paper with an algorithm and two small experiments. Symmetric zero-sum games between parametrized agents split into transitive and cyclic parts relative to a measure on agents. In a cyclic game an individual's performance is meaningless, so evaluation moves to populations: the value of the game between them, which is invariant to redundant members, and the convex hull of their evaluation rows. Training each supported agent on what it beats grows that hull. | Read |
| [NOTE-1144](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1144.md) | Sato & Crutchfield — Coupled replicator equations for the dynamics of learning in multiagent systems | A four-page letter. Two agents choose by softmax over reward memories that decay at rate α; with learning slow relative to play, each agent's choice distribution follows a replicator dynamic in the other's play plus α Σ_j x_j log(x_j/x_i), a pull towards uniform play. Without decay the system is conservative, Hamiltonian in zero-sum games; with decay it is dissipative. Rock–scissors–paper simulations show tori, Hamiltonian chaos, heteroclinic transients, limit cycles and chaotic attractors. Derivation plus numerics, no data. | Read |
| [NOTE-1145](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1145.md) | Shazeer et al. — Outrageously large neural networks: the sparsely-gated mixture-of-experts layer | An engineering paper with large experiments. A sparsely-gated layer of up to 131,072 experts raises capacity over 1000-fold at roughly constant computation. Read here for one observation and one fix: without constraint the gate concentrates on a few experts, which the authors call self-reinforcing, and two auxiliary losses that penalize unequal importance and load remove it, which in one ablation also improves perplexity from 39.8 to 35.6. | Read |
| [NOTE-1146](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1146.md) | Czarnecki et al. — Real world games look like spinning tops | A hypothesis paper with theorems and sampled empirical games. Where players can signal n bits before the outcome is settled, every win–loss pattern on 2ⁿ strategies occurs, so cycles are astronomically long. Nash clustering layers any symmetric zero-sum game, and beating a whole cluster guarantees climbing. Sampled games show cluster size peaking at middling strength. The body says the geometry is not proved, the abstract says it is. Two of the smaller results have defective statements or proofs. | Read |
| [NOTE-1147](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1147.md) | Jacobs, Jordan, Nowlan and Hinton — Adaptive mixtures of local experts | A short paper that founds the mixture of experts. Scoring the error of a single, gate-selected expert, or the mixture's negative log-likelihood, makes experts compete for cases, and an expert better than the gate-weighted average gains responsibility for the case. On a vowel task 4 or 8 linear experts learned in half the epochs of matched backpropagation networks at equal accuracy, divided the task by class pair, and left all but 2 or 3 experts with mixing proportion near zero. | Read |
| [NOTE-1148](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1148.md) | Yang et al. — Mean field multi-agent reinforcement learning | An algorithms paper with a convergence proof and three experiments. Each agent's Q-function is approximated by its interaction with the mean action of its neighbours, which makes many-agent RL tractable for hundreds of homogeneous agents. Mean field Q-learning converges to a Nash Q-value under strong assumptions, learns Gaussian Squeeze with 500 and 1000 agents where baselines fail, matches MCMC on a 20 × 20 Ising model, and wins a 64-versus-64 battle game. | Read |
| [NOTE-1149](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1149.md) | Börgers & Sarin — Learning through reinforcement and replicator dynamics | A short theoretical paper.
