| [NOTE-1347](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1347.md) | Simoes, Dastani and van Ommen — Causal information bottleneck | The causal information bottleneck trades I(X; T), the information a variable abstraction T keeps about X, against Ic(Y \| do(T)), the reduction in Y's entropy when T is set by intervention under a chosen protocol over X. An intervention on T is defined as a mixture of interventions on X, weighted by Bayes inversion of the encoder under a uniform prior, and is identifiable by a backdoor formula. At full weight on control, the optimum is the partition of X by p(y \| do(x)), the causal macrovariables of Chalupka et al., which the ordinary bottleneck misses under confounding. Three toy SCMs confirm it; nothing larger is tried. | Read |
| [NOTE-1348](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1348.md) | Goguen & Burstall — Institutions | An institution is a category of signatures with a sentence functor, a contravariant model functor and a satisfaction relation per signature, subject to one axiom, the Satisfaction Condition: a translated sentence holds in a model exactly when the original holds in the model's reduct. From that axiom alone theories and model classes form a Galois connection, theories can be glued by colimits whenever signatures can (Theorem 11), constraints that force standard or free interpretations can be added as sentences without losing this, and an institution morphism with surjective model translation lets a prover for one logic decide entailment for another (Proposition 35). The Satisfaction Condition is a criterion of correct translation relative to a given model translation; it says nothing about where that model translation comes from. | Read |
| [NOTE-1349](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1349.md) | Gentner — Structure-mapping | Gentner proposes that an analogy maps the relations of a base domain onto a target and drops the objects' attributes, and that which relations go across is decided by systematicity: a relation belonging to a system tied together by higher-order relations is more likely to be imported than an isolated one. The rules look only at the form of the representation (arity and order of predicates), which lets literal similarity, analogy, abstraction and mere appearance be told apart by what kinds of predicate overlap. The framework is argued from examples; the empirical support is one study summarized in a paragraph. | Read |
| [NOTE-1350](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1350.md) | Sengupta, Tozzi, Cooray, Douglas and Friston — Towards a neuronal gauge theory | An essay proposing that variational free-energy minimization be cast as a gauge theory. The only connection it names is the Levi-Civita connection of the Fisher information metric on the manifold of a belief's sufficient statistics, so its gauge freedom is reparameterization of the variational family; its claimed payoff is that attention is precision weighting forced by that manifold's curvature. No gauge group, invariant Lagrangian or compensating field is written down. | Read |
| [NOTE-1351](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1351.md) | Flack — Multiple time-scales and the developmental dynamics of social systems | A review of the pigtailed macaque power-structure work. Fight outcomes flip; the peaceful silent bared-teeth signal that encodes a subordination contract almost never does, so the signalling network changes about two orders of magnitude more slowly and predicts fights better than any single fight. Power, read from that network, is a further slow variable. That the animals perceive and use these variables is argued from earlier studies and stated as what "the data suggest", not shown here. | Read |
| [NOTE-1352](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1352.md) | Marsland, Cui and Mehta — The minimum environmental perturbation principle | In niche models whose environmentally mediated interactions are symmetric, which it characterizes as impact vectors of the form q_iα = −a_i b_α ∂g_i/∂R_α, the uninvadable equilibrium minimizes a perturbation d(R0, R) of the environment from its supply point subject to no species having positive growth, with the species' scaled abundances as KKT multipliers. MacArthur's minimization principle is its Lagrange dual. d rises with every successful invasion. | Read |
| [NOTE-1353](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1353.md) v2 | Guida, Minutola and Presti — Propagation, not aggregation | A conceptual paper with no data. Organizational flexibility is put as a pattern of coordinated, values-consistent action that is retained and spread or absorbed and extinguished, not as the mean of members' flexibility. Whether a rise in a member's flexibility propagates is said to depend jointly on that member's leverage over the consequences colleagues meet and on whether the culture reinforces or penalizes values-consistent action; Bond's (2018) leader-based route is the high-leverage special case. Five propositions, a factorial design and two measures that do not yet exist are set out. | Read |
| [NOTE-1354](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1354.md) v2 | Škorić, de Hoogh and Zannone — Evidence-based subjective logic | Subjective logic's discounting x ⊗ y multiplies opinions and does not distribute over its evidence-adding consensus ⊕, so trust networks must be put in a canonical form, often by discarding edges, to avoid double-counting. EBSL replaces it with x ⊡ y = g(x)·y, a scalar multiple of y's evidence, which distributes over ⊕; the recursive, PageRank-like fixed point R = A ⊕ (offdiag R ⊡ A) then handles loops without discarding anything, and on Tribler data it converges in 9–47 iterations. There is no ground truth; robustness to self-promotion, slander and Sybil attacks is left for future work. | Read |
| [NOTE-1356](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1356.md) | Castro and Liskov — Practical Byzantine fault tolerance | A state-machine replication protocol that keeps safety with at most ⌊(n − 1)/3⌋ arbitrarily faulty replicas and no timing assumption, needing weak synchrony only for liveness; a three-phase commit within views and a view change that carries prepared requests forward. With MACs in place of signatures, a replicated NFS ran the Andrew benchmark 3% slower than Digital Unix's NFS on four replicas, with view changes not yet implemented in the measured library. | Read |
| [NOTE-1357](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1357.md) | Jasanoff — Technologies of humility | Jasanoff argues that predictive "technologies of hubris" — risk assessment, cost–benefit analysis, modelling — are blind at the edges, pre-empt political debate and cannot take in challenges outside their framing, and that formal participation does not fix this. She proposes "technologies of humility", institutionalized habits of thought organized around four focal points: framing, vulnerability, distribution and learning — "what is the purpose; who will be hurt; who benefits; and how can we know?" | Read |
| [NOTE-1358](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1358.md) v2 | Lynch et al. — RefraMED trial of RO DBT for refractory depression | In a three-centre British trial, 250 adults with chronic or treatment-resistant depression were randomised 162 to RO DBT plus usual care and 88 to usual care. RO DBT was 5.40 HRSD points better at 7 months, at the end of therapy, but 2.15 and 1.69 points at the 12-month primary end-point and at 18 months were not significant; flexibility (AAQ-II) and emotional coping were significantly better at 12 and 18 months, not at 7, and suicidal ideation and social support never differed. All eight possibly related serious adverse reactions were in the RO DBT arm. | Read |
| [NOTE-1359](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1359.md) | Jansma and Hoel — Engineering emergence | Extends causal emergence 2.0 from one micro→macro path to the whole lattice of partitions of a Markov chain's states: a partition's ∆CP is its CP minus the largest CP of any finer partition, and the partitions with ∆CP > 0 form the "emergent hierarchy". Shown on 5- and 8-state chains by enumeration and on 40-state preferential-attachment chains by a greedy sampler, where the spread of ∆CP within and across levels peaks near linear attachment; cycles let a single emergent scale be placed at any level. No theorem; the dynamical-consistency filter of CE 2.0 is dropped. | Read |
| [NOTE-1360](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1360.md) | Franklin — The Autobiography of Benjamin Franklin | Franklin's memoir of his life to 1757, written in four sittings from 1771 to 1790 and left unfinished. Its constant subject is how he got others to act with him: by modest, undogmatic speech, by putting his projects forward as "a scheme of a number of friends", by preparing opinion in print and through the Junto's satellite clubs, and, in the borrowed-book anecdote of Part Three, by asking an opponent for a favour. He gives that anecdote as proof of an "old maxim" and as a lesson in prudence, not as a claim about how liking forms. | Read |
| [NOTE-1361](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1361.md) | International Court of Justice — Chagos advisory opinion | The Court advised, by 13 votes to 1, that the decolonization of Mauritius was not lawfully completed in 1968, because the Chagos Archipelago was detached in 1965 without the free and genuine will of the people of the territory, a colony's "agreement" given under the administering Power's authority not counting as one; that the United Kingdom's continued administration is a continuing wrongful act it must end "as rapidly as possible"; and that resettlement of Chagossians is a human-rights matter left to the General Assembly, not decided by the Court. | Read |
| [NOTE-1362](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1362.md) | Soros — Fallibility, reflexivity, and the human uncertainty principle | Soros's statement of his framework. Participants' views are fallible, and acting on them changes the situation they are views of; a cognitive function (world to mind) and a manipulative one (mind to world) run at once, so neither has an independent variable. He calls fallibility and reflexivity together the human uncertainty principle, and says fallibility, not reflexivity, is the main source of the Knightian uncertainty in human affairs. A postscript withdraws the sharp line he draws between natural and social science. | Read |
| [NOTE-1363](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1363.md) | Fedus, Zoph and Shazeer — Switch Transformers | Routing each token to one expert (top-1, "switch" routing) with a fixed per-expert capacity, a load-balancing auxiliary loss α·N·Σ f_i P_i (α = 10⁻²), router computation in float32 inside bfloat16 training, a tenfold smaller initialization and higher dropout inside experts lets sparse Transformers train stably. At equal FLOPs per token on C4, Switch-Base with 64 experts reaches T5-Base's quality about 7 times faster in wall-clock time, gains hold on most fine-tuning tasks and all 101 mC4 languages, and a 1.6-trillion-parameter model is trained. The paper reports the gains; it does not study what experts specialize in. | Read |
| [NOTE-1364](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1364.md) | Fiss — The forms of justice | Fiss argues that the function of adjudication is to give meaning to public values, not to resolve disputes, so structural reform — a judge restructuring a state bureaucracy that threatens constitutional values, through a continuing injunction — is not a deviant form. Its legitimacy rests on the judge's process, dialogue and independence, not on consent. Its real problem is the remedy: rights and remedies jointly fix a value's meaning, but the judge's need to be effective in a world of recalcitrant actors erodes the independence that legitimates him, and he "will tailor the right to fit the remedy". | Read |
| [NOTE-1365](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1365.md) | Human Rights Watch — That's When the Nightmare Started | A human-rights report built on interviews with 43 Chagossians in the UK, Mauritius and the Seychelles, 14 other interviews and a documentary record taken largely from UK court judgments. It argues that the expulsion of 1965–73, the continuing bar on return and treatment on racial grounds are three continuing crimes against humanity — deportation or forcible transfer, other inhumane acts, and persecution — committed by the UK, the first jointly with the US, and asks for return, compensation and satisfaction as reparations. | Read |
| [NOTE-1366](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1366.md) | Blumenthal, Rocks and Mehta — Phase transition to chaos with nonreciprocal species-resource interactions | In MacArthur's consumer–resource model with species' benefits c and impacts e on resources correlated by ρ, the cavity method's replica-symmetric fixed point loses stability at ρ*² = (surviving species)/(non-depleted resources); below ρ* simulations do not settle, their largest Lyapunov exponents are positive and the probability of reaching a steady state falls with system size. With ρ = 1 the model has an optimization principle and competitive exclusion keeps the ratio ≤ 1, so the transition never occurs. | Read |
| [NOTE-1367](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1367.md) | Chizat and Bach — Global convergence of gradient descent for over-parameterized models using optimal transport | Training a sum of many units by gradient descent is, as the number of units grows, a Wasserstein gradient flow of a convex functional of the measure over unit parameters. A measure is a global minimizer exactly when the first variation F′(µ) is nonnegative everywhere and zero on its support. Under 2-homogeneity or partial 1-homogeneity, and an initialization whose support separates the domain, any limit of the flow is global, because mass in any region where F′ < 0 grows exponentially. The result is conditional on convergence and non-quantitative. | Read |
| [NOTE-1368](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1368.md) | Power et al. — What can ecosystems learn? | In a competitive Lotka–Volterra community where individual selection lowers the competitive effect ω_ij of species j on species i at a rate proportional to x_i x_j, and a normalising trade-off holds each row and column sum of ω fixed, interactions change as Hebbian learning does. In simulation (400 species, symmetric ω) the community comes to hold attractors for two past forcing patterns, completes them from fragments and switches with hysteresis. The memory needs the imposed trade-off, and in the long run it degrades. | Read |
| [NOTE-1369](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1369.md) | Cooper and West — Division of labour and the evolution of extreme specialization | A kin-selection model of one cooperative trait with two phenotypes that invest q1 and q2 in helping. Division of labour needs accelerating returns to helping (α > 1) but is not guaranteed by it; when it evolves one phenotype is always a pure reproductive (q2 = 0), so a feedback between helper and reproductive specialization drives the extremes. Relatedness does not affect whether division evolves for an essential trait, and favours sterile helpers. The authors infer that division of labour drives major transitions; the model contains no transition. | Read |
| [NOTE-1370](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1370.md) | Kolchinsky and Wolpert — Semantic information and autonomous agency | Defines a system's semantic information about its environment as the least syntactic information (initial mutual information, or transfer entropy over [0, τ]) that an intervention by coarse-graining the environment can leave while keeping the system's viability at τ unchanged, viability being the negative Shannon entropy of the system's state. Viability function, system–environment split, τ and initial distribution are the analyst's choices, which the paper concedes and proposes to fix by maximizing the measures. One five-location food-seeking toy; no theorem beyond 0 ≤ semantic ≤ syntactic. | Read |
| [NOTE-1371](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1371.md) | Rose et al. — Zero trust architecture (NIST SP 800-207) | NIST's abstract definition of zero trust: no implicit trust from network location or ownership, access to each resource granted per session by a policy engine and administrator and enforced at a policy enforcement point, on dynamic policy fed by asset state, identity, behaviour and threat intelligence. Seven tenets, three approaches, four deployment models, five use cases, seven threats and a migration path; its own survey judged the ecosystem not yet mature enough for widespread adoption. | Read |
| [NOTE-1372](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1372.md) | Shalizi and Crutchfield — Computational mechanics | For a discrete-valued, discrete-time stationary process whose joint distribution is known, the causal states (classes of pasts with the same distribution over the whole future) are as predictive as the full past, are the minimal and, up to measure zero, the unique such states, and have the least stochastic transitions; their entropy Cµ bounds the excess entropy from above. Minimality holds only for predicting the entire future: for any finite horizon a coarser state set can be as predictive and simpler. The paper proves these; it does not show how to estimate causal states from data. | Read |
| [NOTE-1373](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1373.md) | Marquis and Tilcsik — Imprinting: toward a multilevel theory | A review that defines imprinting by three features, a brief sensitive period, the stamp of the environment during it, and persistence despite later environmental change, and separates it from path dependence and cohort effects. It orders the literature in a 4 × 3 table (collectives, organizations, building blocks, individuals; economic and technological, institutional and individual sources) and proposes that entities carry layered imprints from several sensitive periods, including imprints taken secondhand from entities they copy. | Read |
| [NOTE-1374](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1374.md) | Friedkin — A formal theory of reflected appraisals in the evolution of power | Friedkin extends the Friedkin–Johnsen influence model across a sequence of issues: each member's self-weight on the next issue is set to their average total control over the last. In 50 four-person laboratory groups, prior control predicts the next self-weight. In 100,000 simulated random networks, over 98% evolve to one leader whose uninfluenced preference settles every issue through intermediaries. A re-run reproduces this, and shows that the DeGroot–Friedkin version of [LIT-1146](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1146.md) does not concentrate power on the same networks. | Read |
| [NOTE-1376](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1376.md) v2 | Supreme Court — Noem v. Abrego Garcia | An unsigned order on the government's application: the District Court's deadline had lapsed under the administrative stay, its order "properly requires the Government to 'facilitate'" Abrego Garcia's release from Salvadoran custody and to handle his case as if he had not been "improperly sent", and its word "effectuate" was unclear, may exceed the court's authority, and was to be clarified with deference to the executive in foreign affairs. The government had acknowledged the removal was illegal. | Read |
| [NOTE-1377](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1377.md) | Letten, Ke and Fukami — Linking modern coexistence theory and contemporary niche theory | Translating Tilman's two-consumer, two-resource model into Lotka–Volterra coefficients and then into Chesson's niche overlap ρ and fitness ratio, the authors find, by worked cases at equilibrium, that shifting the resource supply ratio changes only the fitness ratio (equalizing) except at extremes where essential-resource competitors become limited by the same resource and ρ jumps to 1; that impact-niche overlap moves ρ (stabilizing); and that requirement-niche overlap moves both, without changing whether the species coexist. | Read |
| [NOTE-1378](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1378.md) | Carstens and Land — Hyperstition: an introduction | A short interview in which Nick Land defines hyperstition as "a positive feedback circuit including culture as a component", "the experimental (techno-)science of self-fulfilling prophecies", whose ideas "function causally to bring about their own reality". His examples are confidence in markets, cyberspace and Jerusalem's destiny, and he says that under favourable conditions, "whose exact nature requires further investigation", hyperstition can "transmute lies into truths". Most of the interview is occult and apocalyptic, not analytic. | Read |
| [NOTE-1379](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1379.md) | Hofbauer and Schreiber — Permanence via invasion graphs | For ecological ODEs whose invasion growth rates have well-defined, nonzero signs on each subcommunity, it defines the invasion graph (edges S → T when every species in T but not S can invade S and every species lost cannot invade T) and proves that when the graph is acyclic, robust permanence holds if, and essentially only if, each species i has a positive invasion growth rate at every −i community. With cycles, signs are not enough. | Read |
| [NOTE-1380](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1380.md) | Li, Lin, Duan, Liang and Shroff — Theory on mixture-of-experts in continual learning | In a stylized continual-learning model, overparameterized linear regression tasks drawn from N ground truths, each carrying a feature signal a linear gate can read, a top-1 MoE whose gate is trained on a "locality" loss plus a Switch-style balancing loss sorts its experts into one set per task (or task cluster) within about M/η rounds. If gate training continues, the balancing loss eventually erases the gaps between experts' gate outputs and routing goes wrong; stopping it once the gaps settle keeps specialization, and noise then spreads load within each set. Forgetting then decays as 1/t, and more experts only lengthen exploration. | Read |
| [NOTE-1381](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1381.md) | Halpern and Moses — Knowledge and common knowledge in a distributed environment | Defines distributed, someone-, everyone- and common knowledge for processors in a system of runs, and shows that a guaranteed coordinated attack makes the attack common knowledge (Proposition 4), while over a channel that may lose any message nothing becomes common knowledge that would not be common knowledge with no messages delivered (Theorem 5), so no correct protocol ever attacks (Corollary 6). Temporal imprecision alone, uncertain start times and delivery times, makes common knowledge unattainable (Theorem 8). Weaker fixed-point variants (ε-, eventual and timestamped common knowledge) are attainable in many systems. | Read |
| [NOTE-1383](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1383.md) | Medrano, Friston and Zeidman — Linking fast and slow | A review for neuroimagers: multiscale time series are best tested with hierarchical generative models in which each level is a slower timescale, justified by centre-manifold and adiabatic reduction (the slaving principle) and compared by variational free energy; the worked example is adiabatic DCM of NMDA-receptor-antibody mouse LFP (Rosch et al. 2018). It states the slaving principle and the HKB model in a paragraph each, with no equations, and asserts rather than shows that the principle extends to discrete switching models such as HMMs. | Read |
| [NOTE-1384](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1384.md) | Cover — Violence and the word | Cover argues that legal interpretation "takes place in a field of pain and death": a judge's interpretation is a practical act whose meaning is bound to deeds that others, in roles, carry out on bodies. Because the judge cannot act alone, legal meaning depends on a social organization of violence — secondary rules that tell wardens which paper to obey, and plural courts so that no single mind's interpretation becomes a deed — and the perpetrator and victim of that violence cannot share its meaning. | Read |
| [NOTE-1385](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1385.md) | Holme and Newman — Coevolution of networks and opinions | N agents with G = N/γ possible opinions on a random graph; at each step a random agent either moves one of its edges to a random holder of its own opinion (probability φ) or copies a random neighbour's opinion (1 − φ). The process always ends in disconnected communities each of one opinion. For k̄ = 4 and γ = 10 a continuous transition at φ_c = 0.458 ± 0.008 separates a giant like-minded community plus small ones (φ < φ_c) from only small communities of mean size about γ (φ > φ_c), with exponents a = 0.61, b = 0.7 and z = 0.61 outside the percolation class. Simulation only. | Read |
| [NOTE-1386](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1386.md) | Feldman and Pentland — Reconceptualizing organizational routines | Feldman and Pentland split an organizational routine into an ostensive aspect, the pattern as participants understand and refer to it, and a performative aspect, its particular enactments, and argue that the ostensive guides, accounts for and names performances while performances create, maintain and modify the ostensive, so that variation and selective retention inside one routine make it a source of endogenous change. A theory paper with one worked example, academic hiring, and no data of its own. | Read |
| [NOTE-1387](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1387.md) v2 | Hoel — Causal emergence 2.0 | Replaces CE 1.0's single EI-maximizing macroscale with a path from the microscale up through coarse-grainings of a Markov chain, along which each step's gain in CP (determinism minus degeneracy, both normalized, uniform interventions per scale) is that scale's causal contribution; causal emergence is the total gain and "emergent complexity" the entropy of the gains along the path. Only dynamically consistent coarse-grains are admitted. Shown on three hand-built 8-state chains; the multi-path version is left open, and the paper's claim to capture all macroscale causation is asserted, not proved. | Read |
| [NOTE-1388](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1388.md) | Wang, Gao, Zhao, Sun and Dai — Auxiliary-loss-free load balancing for mixture-of-experts | Adds a per-expert bias b_i to the routing scores used only for top-K selection, not for the gate weights, and after each batch moves b_i by u·sign(mean load − load_i), so overloaded experts are selected less. On DeepSeekMoE-style models of 1B and 3B parameters trained on 100B and 200B tokens it gives slightly lower validation perplexity (9.50 vs 9.56; 7.92 vs 7.97) and much lower global load violation (0.04 vs 0.72 and 0.52) than an auxiliary loss with α = 0.001, one run each. Expert Choice routing is excluded because it leaks future tokens. | Read |
| [NOTE-1389](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1389.md) | Gioia, Schultz and Corley — Organizational identity, image, and adaptive instability | Gioia, Schultz and Corley argue that organizational identity, usually defined as central, distinctive and enduring, is better seen as fluid: members compare who they think they are with how they think outsiders see them, and the discrepancy pushes them to change either identity or image, so identity shifts while its labels stay. They call the result adaptive instability and argue that it helps organizations change. A conceptual paper with illustrations (Shell's Brent Spar, IBM, Oticon, British Airways) and no data. | Read |
| [NOTE-1390](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1390.md) | Scheppele — Autocratic legalism | Scheppele names a pattern within democratic decline: leaders elected on a mandate to sweep away the old order use constitutional amendment, legislation and appointments to capture courts, election bodies, media and other checks, "with exquisite legal precision", borrowing tactics from each other (Hungary, Poland, Turkey, Russia, Venezuela, Ecuador). They keep the forms of democracy and law and avoid the mass rights violations people have learned to recognize, so the danger is seen too late; the remedy proposed is civic education in constitutionalism. | Read |
| [NOTE-1391](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1391.md) | ECtHR Grand Chamber — El-Masri v. the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia | A unanimous Grand Chamber held the respondent State responsible for inhuman and degrading treatment in 23 days' incommunicado hotel detention, for torture by a CIA team at Skopje Airport carried out with its agents' acquiescence and help, for handing him to the US despite a real risk of further ill-treatment it knew or ought to have known of, for his whole captivity in Afghanistan under Article 5, and for failing to investigate; the burden of proof shifted to the State once he was shown to have entered its control. | Read |
| [NOTE-1392](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1392.md) | DeMarzo, Vayanos and Zwiebel — Persuasion bias, social influence, and unidimensional opinions | Agents average the reports of those they listen to with fixed relative weights, treating every round's report as new (persuasion bias, a DeGroot model). In a strongly connected network they reach a consensus weighted by the stationary distribution of the listening matrix, so influence comes from network position as well as precision; the consensus is correct only in "balanced" networks, and fully rational agents who know the network reach the correct beliefs in at most N² rounds. Long-run differences of opinion line up along one line given by the second eigenvectors, across every issue. | Read |
| [NOTE-1393](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1393.md) | Paluck, Green and Green — The contact hypothesis re-evaluated | The 27 randomized contact studies with outcomes measured at least a day later give a random-effects average of Δ = 0.39 SD, but the effects are heterogeneous (I² = 0.85), shrink with precision (the meta-regression's intercept is −0.01), are largest for disability, fall to 0.25 for ethnic, racial, religious and immigrant targets, and are 0.016 in the three pre-registered studies. No study tests interracial contact on anyone over 25. | Read |
| [NOTE-1394](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1394.md) v2 | Gross and Blasius — Adaptive coevolutionary networks | Reviews models, mostly 1998–2007, in which a network's topology and its nodes' states change each other, and names four recurrent outcomes: robust self-organization toward critical states (Bornholdt and Rohlf's threshold networks reach K = 2), spontaneous "division of labour" into classes of nodes (Ito and Kaneko), complex topologies from local rules, and new system-level dynamics such as bistability and oscillation in an adaptive SIS epidemic. A sketch, not a theory: the mechanisms are argued from examples, and its summary of Holme and Newman inverts the model's parameter. | Read |
| [NOTE-1395](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1395.md) | Mehta, Cui, Wang and Marsland — Constrained optimization as ecological dynamics | Any minimization of f(R) over R ≥ 0 under constraints g_i(R) ≤ 0 has the KKT points of a consumer–resource dynamics as its steady states: variables are resources, each constraint is a species whose abundance is its Lagrange multiplier, and binding constraints are the surviving species. For quadratic programs the dynamics is MacArthur's model, and the Lagrangian dual is a generalized Lotka–Volterra system. A cavity solution then gives the statistics of random quadratic programs, in agreement with numerics at M = 100. | Read |
| [NOTE-1396](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1396.md) | Kalla and Broockman — Reducing exclusionary attitudes through interpersonal conversation | Three pre-registered, placebo-controlled canvassing experiments (6,869 voters reached at the door or by phone). In Experiment 1, a conversation with narratives exchanged non-judgmentally moved an index of immigration attitudes by d = 0.08 pooled over 4.5 months; the same conversation without the narratives moved it by 0.02 (n.s.), and the difference, 0.06, is significant. Transphobia replications give 0.08 (with or without the participants' own narratives) and 0.04 by phone. | Read |
| [NOTE-1397](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1397.md) | Bunin — Ecological communities with Lotka-Volterra dynamics | For generalized Lotka–Volterra dynamics of a community assembled from a pool of S species with random interactions of mean μ/S, variance σ²/S and symmetry γ, the cavity method gives exact large-S results in the phase with a unique uninvadable fixed point: a Gaussian truncated at zero for abundances, the fraction of surviving species, and a loss of stability at σ = √2/(1 + γ) for equal carrying capacities, independent of μ. Beyond it lies a multiple-attractor phase in which the outcome depends on history; that phase is located, not solved, and its history dependence is shown numerically. | Read |
| [NOTE-1398](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1398.md) | Johansson, Hall, Sikström and Olsson — Failure to detect mismatches between intention and outcome | In a card-trick experiment, 120 people chose the more attractive of two female faces and were sometimes handed the face they had rejected. Only 13% of the 354 manipulated trials were detected at the time, at most 26% counting every form of later detection, and the detection rate did not depend on how similar the faces were. The reasons given for the rejected face did not differ from reasons given for real choices in length, emotionality, specificity or certainty, and some named features only the rejected face had. The authors call this choice blindness. | Read |
| [NOTE-1399](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1399.md) v2 | Zhang et al. — Dynamical reversibility and causal emergence based on SVD | Measures how close a Markov transition matrix is to a permutation by Γ_α = Σσᵢ^α of its singular values, shows log Γ_α − log N ≤ EI ≤ (2/α) log Γ_α, and defines causal emergence without a coarse-graining as the rise in the average singular value when those at or below a threshold ε are dropped. With ε = 0 it is a rank test; with ε > 0 it depends on ε, and any matrix with unequal singular values shows it for some ε. Its SVD-plus-k-means coarse-graining matches EI maximization on Hoel's Boolean networks, but its claim that the lumping commutes with the dynamics for any grouping (Proposition 5) is false. | Read |
| [NOTE-1400](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1400.md) | Krakauer et al. — The information theory of individuality | Splits I(S_n, E_n; S_{n+1}) two ways, into A* = I(S_{n+1}; S_n) plus nC = I(S_{n+1}; E_n \| S_n), or I(S_{n+1}; E_n) plus A = I(S_{n+1}; S_n \| E_n), and in the 2020 version names A* organismal, A colonial and nC environmentally determined individuality, read through a partial information decomposition left unspecified. Both A* and A can only grow as variables move from environment to system, so they cannot by themselves find a boundary; the 2020 version says a size cost is needed and does not supply one. Illustrated on one two-unit system; no algorithm and no data. | Read |
| [NOTE-1401](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1401.md) | Désidéri — Multiple-gradient descent algorithm (MGDA) | Defines Pareto-stationarity (some convex combination of the criteria's gradients is zero), proves it necessary for Pareto-optimality, and shows that when it fails the minimum-norm element ω of the gradients' convex hull gives a direction −ω along which every criterion decreases, with (u, ω) ≥ ‖ω‖² for every u in the hull. Steepest descent along −ω, the MGDA, has a subsequence converging to a Pareto-stationary point when the criteria are positive and coercive. The direction depends on how the gradients are scaled; the author calls the right scaling open. | Read |
| [NOTE-1402](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1402.md) | Hazen, Griffin, Carothers and Szostak — Functional information and the emergence of biocomplexity | Defines functional information I(E_x) = −log2 F(E_x), F the fraction of all configurations that reach at least degree E_x of a stated function, and illustrates it on letter strings, random Avida genomes and GTP aptamers. Its one empirical observation is that I against E_x is stepped in Avida, which it attributes to distinct classes ("islands") of solutions. The measure is relative to a function and to a uniform measure on configurations, and says nothing about history or identity. | Read |
| [NOTE-1403](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1403.md) | Kleinman, Liu and Redding — International friends and enemies | A country's real-income elasticity to a partner's productivity, from a constant-elasticity trade model with input-output links, predicts political alignment with that partner. Instrumented by a counterfactual Chinese productivity shock from the 1980 equilibrium (119 countries, 1980–2010) or by air-versus-sea distance (pairs, 1970–2012), it moves UN voting similarity (0.094 SD per SD in the panel), lowers strategic rivalry, and raises formal alliances. The paper's own model is strategic: alignment is a costly action a country takes to raise a partner on whom its income depends. | Read |
| [NOTE-1404](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1404.md) | Edmondson — Psychological safety and learning behavior in work teams | In 51 work teams at one office-furniture manufacturer, a team-level belief that the team is safe for interpersonal risk taking (psychological safety) predicted members' and outside observers' ratings of the team's learning behavior; team efficacy added little once safety was controlled. Learning behavior predicted observers' ratings of performance and carried the association of safety with performance, and safety carried the association of context support and leader coaching with learning. All of it is cross-sectional. | Read |
| [NOTE-1405](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1405.md) | Pettigrew and Tropp — Meta-analytic tests of three mediators of contact | Meta-analytic mediation tests over 54 studies of contact and prejudice that also measured knowledge of the outgroup (17 samples), intergroup anxiety (60) or empathy and perspective taking (14). All three mediate. Knowledge is much the weakest (Sobel Z = 3.87); anxiety reduction (26.6) and empathy (12.4) are strong, and in nine samples measuring both, anxiety and empathy together account for about half of the contact–prejudice covariance. | Read |
| [NOTE-1406](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1406.md) | Revonsuo — Binding and the phenomenal unity of consciousness | Separates stimulus-related binding, neural processing that recovers a stimulus's unity whether or not anything is conscious, from consciousness-related binding, the construction of phenomenally unified percepts, crediting the split to Smythies (1994). Distinguishes the phenomenal, neural and cognitive levels at which binding is posed, lists five kinds of phenomenal binding with the deficits that dissociate them, and argues from his own EEG result that 40-Hz synchrony accompanies constructing a unified percept, not holding it. | Read |
| [NOTE-1407](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1407.md) | Pettigrew and Tropp — A meta-analytic test of intergroup contact theory | Meta-analysis of 515 studies (713 samples, 1,383 tests, 250,089 people, 38 countries, through 2000) of face-to-face intergroup contact and prejudice. The random-effects mean is r ≈ −.21, 94% of samples are negative, experiments give −.34, and the most rigorous samples −.32. Samples structured to meet Allport's conditions give −.29 against −.20 for the rest, so the conditions help but are not needed; they work as a bundle. One of six publication-bias checks, Vevea and Hedges's, leaves no significant overall effect. | Read |
| [NOTE-1408](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1408.md) | Pettigrew — Intergroup contact theory | Pettigrew reformulates Allport's contact hypothesis as a longitudinal theory. Contact works through four processes (learning about the outgroup, changed behavior, affective ties, ingroup reappraisal, the last yielding "deprovincialization"). Its effects generalize through a sequence of decategorization, salient categorization and recategorization. A fifth essential condition, friendship potential, joins Allport's four; other proposed conditions are facilitating. Selection bias is real, but in European survey data the path from outgroup friendship to less prejudice is stronger than the reverse. | Read |
| [NOTE-1409](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1409.md) | Merton — The self-fulfilling prophecy | Names the self-fulfilling prophecy, "in the beginning, a false definition of the situation evoking a new behavior which makes the originally false conception come true", and applies it to American ethnic and racial prejudice. Beside it the essay sets a second route, "moral alchemy", in which the in-group condemns the out-group whatever it does by renaming the same conduct. It argues that institutional change, not education or good will, breaks the circle. | Read |
| [NOTE-1410](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1410.md) | Akkoyunlu, Ekanadham and Huber — Some constraints and tradeoffs in the design of network communications | A design paper on interprocess communication in networks of sequential processes: complete status of a transaction is impossible in an arbitrary distributed facility and, with time-outs, even in a reliable one, and the insertion property forces the system to withhold status. Its Appendix states, as a story of gangsters and a messenger who may be mugged, that no finite exchange over a lossy channel brings two parties to know they agree a message got through, with a shortest-sequence proof. That is the coordinated attack problem in substance, three years before Gray (1978), framed as mutual knowledge of delivery. | Read |
| [NOTE-1411](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1411.md) | Seeley et al. — Stop signals provide cross inhibition in honeybee swarms | Nest-site scouts of honeybee swarms deliver stop signals, head-butts with a brief vibration, to scouts dancing for sites other than their own while the swarm is choosing (213 of 237 signals in two two-box swarms), and to all dancers once it has chosen. An ODE model, in the supplement, shows that above a critical rate of such cross inhibition a swarm facing two equal sites breaks deadlock and picks one at random, and picks the better when they differ enough. | Read |
| [NOTE-1412](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1412.md) | Nisbett and Wilson — Telling more than we can know | Reviews dissonance, attribution, subliminal-perception, problem-solving and bystander studies, and reports eight small studies of its own, to argue that people have little or no introspective access to the processes by which stimuli affect their judgments. Their reports come from a priori causal theories, which observers given only a description share: in Nisbett and Bellows, subject and observer reports correlated .77 to .99, and both were accurate only for the judgment the culture has rules for. | Read |
| [NOTE-1413](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1413.md) v2 | Eberhardt and Lee — Causal emergence: when distortions in a map obscure the territory | Under Hoel's effective information, with uniform interventions at each level and macro interventions as uniform averages over micro states, the EI-optimal coarse-graining can merge micro states whose effects differ widely, so the macro variable has ambiguous manipulations; and the EI-optimal abstraction of a two-step matrix differs from the square of the one-step abstraction, so abstraction and marginalization do not commute. Both are traced to the maximum-entropy distribution, which the authors call extraneous to the system. The numbers check. | Read |
| [NOTE-1414](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1414.md) | Ito and Kaneko — Spontaneous structure formation in a network of chaotic units | In a globally coupled logistic map whose units each renormalize their incoming weights after strengthening those from units in similar states, identical units split, in the desynchronized high-turnover regime, into a persistent core that the others attend to and a periphery the core ignores; the split needs states and weights to act on each other. Simulation only, N = 100, one parameter point in detail. | Read |
| [NOTE-1415](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1415.md) | Chalupka, Eberhardt and Perona — Causal feature learning: an overview | A macro cause is a class of micro states with the same P(effect \| man(state)); a macro intervention is any manipulation into the class, which is unambiguous by construction. The causal coarsening theorem makes the causal partition a coarsening of the observational one except on a null set, so one experiment per observational class finds it. No distribution over interventions enters the definitions. The example is a one-dimensional toy, and two displayed equations carry slips. | Read |
| [NOTE-1416](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1416.md) | Comolatti and Hoel — Causal emergence is widespread across measures of causation | Writes a dozen measures of causal strength as functions of sufficiency and necessity, or of determinism and degeneracy, and finds every one showing causal emergence on a bipartite Markov chain whose macro is a deterministic NOT gate, under three intervention distributions; the system-level EI under the stationary distribution shows none, as data processing requires. The model is hand-built for a deterministic macro, so it is the kind of result [THEORY-787](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-787.md)'s promote_when says cannot settle it. | Read |
| [NOTE-1417](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1417.md) | Abrego Garcia v. Noem — Order granting expedited discovery | On remand, the district court reads "facilitate" as taking the steps available toward Abrego Garcia's release from Salvadoran custody, measures that against the government's own past practice of facilitated returns, finds that four days of court-ordered sworn declarations disclosed no step, and orders two weeks of discovery into his custody, what was done, what will be done and who authorizes the detention. It does not decide whether return was possible. | Read |
| [NOTE-1418](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1418.md) | Scacco and Warren — Can social contact reduce prejudice and discrimination? | A randomized field experiment with 849 young Christian and Muslim men in Kaduna: sixteen weeks of cooperative computer training in mixed or single-religion classes left stated prejudice and its supposed mediators unchanged, while mixed classes discriminated less than single-religion classes in dictator and destruction games. The control arm shows the contrast is mostly in-group bonding raising discrimination in single-religion classes; the effect toward unfamiliar out-group members holds for Christians only. | Read |
| [NOTE-1419](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1419.md) v2 | Lemmer and Wagner — Can we really reduce ethnic prejudice outside the lab? | Contact programmes run outside the laboratory improve self-reported ethnic attitudes by about a quarter of a standard deviation in controlled designs, and the effect is still there one to twelve months later in the few studies that looked. Indirect programmes do as well as direct ones between studies; within them, stories of cross-group friendship give the largest subtype estimate (0.42, k = 8) and online interaction none in the stronger designs. No included study measured behaviour. | Read |
| [NOTE-1420](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1420.md) | Chalupka, Perona and Eberhardt — Multi-level cause-effect systems | Defines the fundamental cause and effect of a confounded micro system as the partitions of causes by P(J \| man(i)) and of effects by P(j \| man(·)), learns both from experimental data, and proves they generically coarsen the observational partitions, so passive data plus one experiment per class find them. It assumes no distribution over interventions. Its claim that the effect partition is the minimal sufficient one fails for proportional, unequal columns. | Read |
| [NOTE-1421](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1421.md) | Lynch et al. — RefraMED, the NIHR EME monograph | The full report of RefraMED. Beyond the BJP paper it gives the trial's mechanism design and its failure: RO DBT participants were also randomised to a therapy room, written feedback and mode of reimbursement, as instruments for sessions attended, alliance and DBT skills, and the instruments were too weak to use. Without them, the decomposition of the 7-month effect is implausible, and the planned analyses of temporal order are not reported. Its adverse-event test, p < 0.01 for eight reactions in the RO DBT arm against none, does not reproduce (about 0.029), and differs from the BJP paper's 0.004. | Read |
| [NOTE-1422](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1422.md) | Serván and Allesina — Tractable models of ecological assembly | For competitive Lotka–Volterra communities with A = D(v)BD(w), B symmetric with positive entries, assembled by rare, low-density, well-separated invasions, MacArthur's Lyapunov function V orders the feasible sub-communities, so the assembly graph is acyclic and every feasible sub-community can be assembled without extinctions; with the paper's Theorem 1 this makes sequential and all-at-once assembly reach the same end-points. One end-point when B is positive definite, several when it is not. | Read |
